Every row is an EXPECTED RESULT, NOT AN EXECUTED TEST. Numerical values are hypothetical accounting units, not prices or campus spending.
Case | Schedule | Expected state and consequence
Ambiguous charged timeout | B=10,S=0; reserve q=6; grant; timeout | S=0,H=6, available=4. A distinct q=6 operation is denied; no automatic paid retry is issued. Final authoritative charge c=4 gives S=4,H=0 and available=6.
Unsafe timeout-release control | Same initial trace, but release q merely on timeout; reserve and send another q=6 | Two actual charges of 6 can total 12>B=10. This locally refutes the timeout-release candidate, not federation as a whole.
Simultaneous reservations | B=10,S=H=0; two independent attempts each request q=6 | Either ordering admits exactly one: H=6, available=4. Both cannot pass an atomic post-state check.
Nested-scope contention | Campus has 10 available, project has 5; request q=6 | Reject with neither ledger changed; campus capacity does not override project authority.
Client replay | Repeat same scoped idempotency key and manifest | Return existing O and authorized status only; no new attempt or send right. Different manifest with same key is rejected.
Attempt replay | Duplicate CommitDispatch(A) or replay an old grant after settlement | Durable consumed state rejects reissuance. Deduplication tombstones or retired-issuer rejection must outlive the replay opportunity; deleting records cannot revive A.
Crash in commit/send gap | G durable; send outcome unknown; restart | No resend and no timeout release. Recover UNCERTAIN with q held; settle only using final charge evidence or fenced proof of non-issuance.
Duplicate reconciliation | Final c=4 delivered twice for q=6 | First event produces S=4,H=0; second changes nothing. A contradictory later invoice triggers incident handling, not silent extra admission.

review.rationale: The hypothetical arithmetic is consistent: holding 6 under cap 10 leaves 4; settling at 4 restores availability to 6; unsafe timeout release can expose two liabilities totaling 12. Atomic nested checks, replay tombstones and idempotent settlement support the other expected outcomes, conditional on their stated implementation rules.

argument_steps.title: 12. Hand-worked adversarial table: money, replay and crashes

argument_steps.argument: The minimum proposed extension consists of a home identity/policy authority, a transactional reservation ledger, protected audit storage and a fully controlled egress adapter. Tenant clients, agent-generated URLs, backends, tools, observability exporters and partner/provider endpoints are separate boundaries. A malicious tenant's direct network connection, hidden API credential or classification downgrade defeats the premises unless prevented independently. A lying destination can violate retention despite a valid grant. A provider charging above q invalidates the liability premise; incident detection after an excess invoice cannot restore the original hard-cap guarantee. Audit failure before commit denies issuance; post-commit audit export failure does not release liability. Metadata and error logs themselves require approved storage. These controls are proposals, and campus-local placement alone does not establish their correctness.

review.rationale: The limitations follow from the proof premises: bypass credentials defeat complete mediation, dishonest recipients defeat retention expectations, and charges exceeding q defeat the liability bound. Incident detection cannot retrospectively restore a violated hard-cap guarantee.

argument_steps.title: 13. Trust boundaries and limits of the conditional proof

argument_steps.argument: The same reservation semantics can govern approved API-only service or separately approved frontier access; they do not require federation. Campus-local service avoids external model disclosure but still needs local authorization, quotas and tool/log mediation. Federation additionally needs destination-specific agreements and remote enforcement; it receives no special policy exemption. If separately approved API accounts bypass the shared payer ledger, the campus-wide cap claim cannot be applied to them. Provisionally prefer campus-only service plus separately approved, financially mediated external access unless a measured policy-permitted federation benefit justifies the additional boundaries. Next test: implement a non-sensitive model harness for the exact transitions above, enumerate short schedules including restart and duplicate events, and independently check grant order, packet destinations and S+H after each event. Include unsafe cached-approval and timeout-release controls. Require zero observed forbidden grants, duplicate sends and overshoots before considering a reviewed pilot; a finite pass supplies bounded support only. Availability lost to conservative holds, queue waiting and safe denial must also be measured, not hidden as successful service.

review.rationale: Accepted as a bounded proposal, not evidence of baseline superiority. Reservation controls need not require federation, and separately approved access must still satisfy financial mediation for a campus-wide cap claim. The proposed tests and measurement of safe-denial losses address real remaining obligations without claiming a finite pass proves security.

reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied bounded extract of bfcf812f-b3a9-46ff-862c-4d0b4cd76978 identifies the authorization-to-dispatch and reservation gaps; its original artifact was not supplied. Its partition argument motivates retaining the home authority rather than permitting fresh authorization from cached policy. Peer extracts 5c8fdc17-0ce8-4ea3-b8dc-79e05f97d0db and cc14dcfd-f2c0-41f7-92f4-768a1511e7f2 raise compatible liability-bound and complete-mediation requirements. I adopt those requirements as inputs to test, not their assertions as certified premises, and give the accounting argument below. Their domains include all spending paths; a separately approved API account with untracked credentials would not satisfy that domain. The peer economic threshold is not used because no workload costs or useful-completion counts are available.

review.rationale: The supplied prior extract identifies the stated policy and reservation gaps. Both peer extracts explicitly list liability-bound and complete-mediation premises. The step correctly treats these as unverified inputs and does not import the truncated economic argument.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Evidence boundary and relation to previous work

reasoning_steps.argument: R identifies one research task; its calls are not separate useful completions. O identifies one logical inference or tool operation and binds an immutable canonical request manifest: home issuer, principal, project, purpose, payload and attachment references, classification restrictions, destination, model/version request, tool permissions, retention/contract profile and resource ceilings. A changed destination or changed payload requires a new O linked to R, not mutation of an existing authorization. A=(home issuer,O,server-issued sequence) identifies one potentially billable invocation. An explicitly approved retry uses a new A under the same unchanged O; it never reuses an uncertain A. A client idempotency key is scoped to principal and project: the same key and manifest returns the existing O/status, while a conflicting manifest is rejected. Identifiers convey no authority. Sensitive manifests, keyed digests, status responses and deduplication records remain access-controlled inside approved domains.

review.rationale: Accepted as conditional model definitions. Separating root task, immutable logical operation and potentially billable attempt prevents retries from becoming extra useful completions and prevents authorization reuse after changing a destination or payload.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Define root tasks, operations and attempts

reasoning_steps.argument: Use a proposed home-campus transaction authority that linearizes policy changes, identity/project revocations, operation cancellation, attempt transitions and all relevant ledger updates. Preliminary approval and reservation are not permission to transmit. The final CommitDispatch(A) transaction is the authorization ordering point L(A). An applicable revocation Rv ordered before L(A) must prevent that grant; L(A) ordered before Rv authorizes only that immutable attempt, even if its already-designated sender transmits later. Concurrent events take their committed order; a campus receives a revocation-effective acknowledgement only after its transaction commits. An invocation that begins after that acknowledgement cannot be ordered before revocation. A partitioned replica cannot commit new grants from cached approval. This chooses decision-time semantics explicitly; campuses requiring no transmission, execution or retention after revocation must reject this specification or require additional recipient/enforcement controls.

review.rationale: Accepted as an explicit authority and campus-acceptance premise, not established policy. Linearization gives revocation and grant a definite order while expressly allowing later transmission from an earlier grant; disconnected cached approval cannot create a new commit.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Define authority and exact authorization ordering

reasoning_steps.argument: An operation is OPEN or CLOSED with a recorded reason such as cancellation or accepted completion. Attempt states are VALIDATED, RESERVED, COMMITTED, IN_FLIGHT, UNCERTAIN, REPORTED, SETTLED and PRE_SEND_CLOSED. Financial state is separate from task outcome: a returned answer, failure or cancellation is not settlement. Creation enters VALIDATED only after authenticated identity and authoritative classification/manifest checks; preliminary destination eligibility is advisory. Unknown classification fails closed before payload leaves an approved boundary. Restricted inputs and their prompts, outputs, embeddings, logs and caches retain applicable restrictions unless a campus-authorized process changes them. Each tool disclosure is a separate operation; an agent cannot authorize its own destination. Unsupported protocol fields, unenumerated attachments or changed content invalidate validation rather than disappearing during translation.

review.rationale: Accepted as the conditional state and trusted-validation specification. Separating financial state from task outcome avoids inferring settlement from success, failure or cancellation. Unknown classifications and unsupported request semantics fail closed rather than being silently dropped.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. States, classification and advisory eligibility

reasoning_steps.argument: For each applicable scope k—user, project, department, campus and any shared payer—maintain cap B_k, settled charges S_k and outstanding reservations H_k. An attempt has an enforceable total liability ceiling q_A,k, covering all charges attributable to it in that scope. Amounts use exact accounting units and conservative rounding. Reserve(A) atomically checks S_k+H_k+q_A,k≤B_k for every k, then adds every reservation and changes VALIDATED to RESERVED, or changes nothing. Failure at one scope cannot leave a partial reservation. The bound must include applicable tokens, cached-token treatment, tools, egress, taxes, currency exposure and unavoidable provider-side charges; a token estimate alone is insufficient. Unknown or unenforceable bounds block paid dispatch. Reservation deadlines use authority time. WDRR may choose among eligible requests but cannot override these checks. Bounded token/GPU-time quotas can use additional ledger dimensions; model fit and GPU-memory availability remain separate admission checks.

review.rationale: Accepted as the atomic-ledger and enforceable-bound premises. Checking every scope before a single state change prevents partial reservation and nested-limit bypass. The step correctly distinguishes financial admission from model fit and scheduling eligibility.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Reserve atomically before any grant

reasoning_steps.argument: CommitDispatch(A) succeeds only from RESERVED, before its reservation deadline, while O remains OPEN. In one transaction it rechecks current principal/project authority, current classification restrictions and exact manifest binding, destination/contract/retention approval, model/tool permissions, reservation coverage and the designated controlled egress path. It atomically changes A to COMMITTED, writes its protected audit event and consumes its one-use issuance right; H is unchanged. No stale preliminary approval suffices. Exactly one winning adapter invocation may initiate the bound external invocation. A duplicate transaction or status query returns state, never a fresh send right. The adapter must not retransmit an application request after uncertain delivery, and recovery must not reissue a consumed grant. This deliberately sacrifices availability in crash windows rather than assuming exactly-once execution across a network. These adapter properties are explicit implementation obligations, not consequences of a database flag alone.

review.rationale: Accepted conditionally. The single RESERVED-to-COMMITTED transition can order current authorization and consume one grant without changing its reservation. At-most-once network issuance additionally depends on the explicitly listed adapter premise, which the step does not misrepresent as a database consequence.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Final commit and one-use issuance

reasoning_steps.argument: The adapter may record IN_FLIGHT, REPORTED or UNCERTAIN after COMMITTED; none changes H. A crash after commit but before confirmed send, a lost commit response, a provider rejection without final billing evidence, or an ambiguous charged timeout leaves the entire unresolved ceiling reserved. The recovery process does not resend A. Cancellation closes O to future grants and requests best-effort termination of committed work, but cannot imply remote cancellation or a refund. There is no automatic paid retry or paid fallback escalation. A later retry requires explicit spending approval, fresh policy checks and a fresh reservation; this design blocks paid retry while a predecessor's liability remains unresolved. Changing destination creates a new operation and cannot evade cancellation, classification or spending approval.

review.rationale: Accepted as the uncertainty-handling rules. Retaining the ceiling after lost responses, uncertain send or cancellation preserves coverage of possible liability. Fresh approval and reservation for any later retry prevents timeout from becoming implicit permission to spend again.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. After commit, uncertainty preserves liability

reasoning_steps.argument: Before COMMITTED, denial, expiry or cancellation may atomically change RESERVED to PRE_SEND_CLOSED and release q, provided that transaction permanently blocks CommitDispatch for that A. If commit wins the race, the release is forbidden. After COMMITTED, neither wall-clock expiry, a cancellation acknowledgement, HTTP status nor a model response alone releases funds. Final authoritative financial reconciliation with total charge c≤q changes the attempt to SETTLED, adds c to S and removes q from H exactly once. Proven non-issuance can settle at c=0 only when the designated sender and every queued send right are durably fenced and no liability remains; mere absence of a send log is insufficient. Unresolved attempts can remain reserved indefinitely, or be conservatively booked at the full q without restoring spending headroom. Duplicate settlement events are idempotent and conflicting events are quarantined. Budget resets cannot erase liabilities; obligations remain attached to their accounting periods and any required aggregate cap. A cap reduction below S+H is rejected. Fixed commitments must already be charged or reserved.

review.rationale: Accepted as the release and reconciliation premises. Pre-send release is safe only when it atomically excludes commit; post-commit release requires final bounded liability or fenced proof of non-issuance. Idempotent settlement, preserved period liabilities and restricted cap reductions close otherwise obvious accounting escape paths.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Exact reservation release and reconciliation rules

reasoning_steps.argument: Initially there are no grants. The only transition creating a grant is CommitDispatch, which checks current authority in the same ordered transaction as grant creation. Therefore a relevant earlier revocation or cancellation prevents the grant; later events do not retrospectively change its ordering. Only the winner consumes the RESERVED-to-COMMITTED transition, and all duplicate requests are status reads rather than new issuance. Under the complete-mediation and one-use-adapter assumptions, every invocation follows one matching grant and no A is issued twice. Manifest immutability prevents substituting another destination or payload after checking. This proves the abstract decision-order and issuance invariants, not classification accuracy, absence of implementation bypass or recipient compliance.

review.rationale: Only CommitDispatch creates a grant and it checks authority in the same ordered transaction, so earlier applicable revocations prevent it. Immutable binding and the assumed one-use adapter extend this to matching, nonduplicate invocations. The conclusion remains correctly limited to the abstract model.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Policy and replay invariant

reasoning_steps.argument: Assume initially S_k+H_k≤B_k. Reserve preserves it by checking the post-reservation value atomically at every scope. Commit, send, timeout, response and cancellation of committed work do not decrease H or increase available credit. A valid pre-send close decreases H without creating liability because the same transaction blocks future commit. Final settlement changes S_k+H_k by c_k−q_k≤0. Full-ceiling conservative booking leaves the sum unchanged. Duplicate events have no financial effect, and cap changes/window transitions obey step 8. Thus all transitions preserve S_k+H_k≤B_k, including concurrent reservations serialized by the authority. Since unresolved actual liabilities are bounded by their reservations, settled charges plus unresolved liabilities also fit within the caps. At B=0, any positive paid reservation is rejected. Local execution still requires funded resources and quotas; zero paid API spending is not zero total operating cost.

review.rationale: The induction checks the relevant transitions: reservation verifies the new sum, uncertainty retains it, fenced closure decreases it without liability, and settlement changes it by c−q≤0. Serialized concurrent reservations and liability-preserving cap/window changes preserve the invariant under the stated premises.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Budget invariant by transition induction

reasoning_steps.argument:
Every row is an EXPECTED RESULT, NOT AN EXECUTED TEST. Notation: V=VALIDATED, Q=RESERVED, G=COMMITTED, X=PRE_SEND_CLOSED; '<' denotes authoritative order.
Case | Schedule | Expected state and consequence
Revocation before grant | V→Q; revoke destination; CommitDispatch | Final check denies; Q→X and releases its reservation atomically; no send right exists.
Revocation after grant but before physical send | V→Q→G; revoke; sender transmits | The previously granted attempt may transmit under decision-time semantics; its liability stays reserved. This is a counterexample to claiming that decision ordering prevents all post-revocation transmission.
Concurrent revocation and commit | Both contend at the authority | Revocation first means denial; commit first means one prior grant. There is no third cached-policy success path.
Cancellation before grant | V→Q; Cancel(O); CommitDispatch | O closes; reservation release and pre-send closure prevent later grant, including by a stale worker.
Cancellation after grant | V→Q→G; Cancel(O) | O closes to new grants; remote termination is best effort and q remains held until final reconciliation. Cancellation is not reported as a guaranteed refund.
Reservation expiry versus commit | Both contend | Expiry first tombstones A and releases q; commit first consumes the right and expiry cannot release q.
WAN partition before final commit | Q; home authority unreachable | No new grant; defer or pre-send close through the authority when reachable. Signed cached approval is insufficient.

review.rationale: The expected schedules follow the specified ordering: revocation, cancellation or expiry winning before commit blocks the grant; commit winning first retains its reservation and may permit later transmission. The partition row appropriately denies fresh disconnected authorization. No row is presented as an executed test.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Evidence boundary and four alternatives

reasoning_steps.argument: Use 100 distinct active researchers and 2,000 root tasks each month: coding 600, routine analysis 400, demanding scientific reasoning 300, multimodal/long-context 200, agentic workflows 200, campus-only sensitive analysis 200, reproducible batches 100. These are disjoint accounting bins, not a claim that sensitivity is a distinct technical task type. Proposed deadlines respectively are 30 s, 120 s, 600 s, 180 s, 900 s end-to-end, 120 s and 24 h. A useful completion must be authorized, meet its deadline, pass the frozen task rubric and contain no critical factual/security error. Rubrics use held-out coding tests, known-result/unit checks, blinded scientific review, labeled multimodal fixtures and agent root-goal/tool-boundary checks. Batch acceptance requires complete provenance and a specified numerical tolerance; it does not assume bitwise API replay. Calls, Investigator/Skeptic exchanges and retries remain descendants of one root. Correct refusal is recorded separately, not counted as delivered research. These deadlines and rubrics require campus approval.
reasoning_steps.title: 2. Common hypothetical workload and usefulness definition

reasoning_steps.argument: For this scenario only, the campus approves all 2,000 roots locally, approves 1,800 non-sensitive roots at one named API destination, and approves only coding, routine analysis and batches at a named partner campus: 1,100 partner-eligible roots. The 200 sensitive roots remain campus-only. Thus policy-eligible counts are L=2,000, A=1,800, G=2,000 and F=2,000; federation does not increase eligibility by default. Separately, assume local model/context/memory requirements admit only coding, routine, sensitive analysis and batch work: 1,300 technically suitable roots. The other 700 require capabilities unavailable in this hypothetical local installation. Assume the approved API can technically serve all 1,800 eligible roots. These are proposed domain and capability assumptions, not university policy or model benchmark findings. Restricted, student, patient, controlled, sponsor-restricted and unpublished content, including derived prompts, outputs, logs, embeddings and cache, stays inside its approved domains; ambiguous classification gets no execution destination until resolved.
reasoning_steps.title: 3. Keep policy eligibility separate from capability

reasoning_steps.argument: Assume local deadline-feasible admission capacity K=1,000 roots/month after interactive/batch scheduling, maintenance and queue headroom. Reserve capacity first for the 200 campus-only roots; an illustrative remaining allocation is coding 400, routine 300 and batches 100. Local overflow is coding 200 and routine 100. Assume useful fractions among admitted roots are q_L=0.80 locally and q_A=0.90 at the API, including both quality and end-to-end deadline failures; these are joint fractions, not products of independent events. Before API budget limits, the worksheet is: L admits 1,000 local roots and yields 800 useful; A admits up to 1,800 API roots and yields up to 1,620 useful but no sensitive completions; G admits 1,000 local plus up to 1,000 API roots and yields up to 1,700 useful. G's external candidate set is the 700 capability-demanding roots plus 300 overflow roots, with no double counting. Actual admitted counts and quality must later be reported by stratum; these aggregate fractions do not establish any individual stratum's service guarantee.
reasoning_steps.title: 4. Base admission and useful-completion worksheet

reasoning_steps.argument: For one named provider/model/region/contract, leave these fields blank pending a dated quote: p_in[d], p_cached[d], p_out[d] in dollars per million tokens; p_tools[d] per billable tool unit; p_embed[d] per million embedding tokens; p_egress[d] per GB; any request fees, taxes and monthly minimum M[d]. Here d is the actual price-effective/access date, currently unavailable. A hypothetical root envelope allows at most eight total calls, including Investigator/Skeptic turns and retries, and at most 128,000 uncached input, 32,000 cached input and 16,000 output tokens summed across those calls. Let h[d] be an enforceable maximum for all ancillary root charges, including multimodal charges, tools, embeddings, egress and applicable tax exposure. A candidate reservation is r=0.128p_in[d]+0.032p_cached[d]+0.016p_out[d]+h[d]. Cache misses must be bounded at the uncached rate; otherwise this expression is not a valid upper bound. Different provider tokenization, vision/audio billing and unbounded tools require revised envelopes or refusal. Actual monthly usage V_j is the sum of actual charges across all admitted descendants, not the number of useful roots times a single-call price.
reasoning_steps.title: 5. API price placeholders and root-level amplification

reasoning_steps.argument: Assume r>0 is enforceable, no opening unresolved liability or minimum commitment, and use a conservative monthly plan that does not reuse reservation savings. Then n_A=min(1800,floor(B/r)); n_G=min(1000,floor(B/r)). This is a reproducible worst-case plan, not maximum achievable throughput under rolling reconciliation. The four cap columns B=$0/$2,000/$4,000/$8,000 give G API admissions 0/min(1000,floor(2000/r))/min(1000,floor(4000/r))/min(1000,floor(8000/r)); useful counts are 800+0.9n_G. A uses the same expressions with ceiling 1,800 and useful counts 0.9n_A. All 1,000 G API candidates fit only if r <= $2/$4/$8 at the three positive caps. All 1,800 A candidates fit only if r <= $1.111.../$2.222.../$4.444..., respectively. These numbers are allowable liability thresholds, not quoted API prices. With B=0, neither free credits nor an unapproved destination is assumed. If no finite charging bound can be established, paid admission is disabled even for positive B. For a contractual minimum, replace usage billing by the actual contractual function, reserve the minimum and outstanding liabilities first, and recompute admissions; do not add a minimum to usage if it already includes that usage.
reasoning_steps.title: 6. Hard-cap admission worksheet without invented rates

reasoning_steps.argument: Hypothetical local monthly/annual equivalent ledger: installed GPU/host asset $48,000, zero residual, four-year life gives depreciation $1,000/$12,000; storage including approved audit storage $200/$2,400; network $100/$1,200; hardware support $200/$2,400; operations staff including audit operations $1,400/$16,800; procurement labor excluding operations $100/$1,200. These fixed ownership rows total $3,000/$36,000. Assume aggregate IT power 0.4 kW idle and 1.2 kW busy, utilization u, PUE 1.25 and electricity $0.10/kWh. Annual-average monthly energy is 730×1.25×[0.4+0.8u]×0.10 = $36.50+$73u, including cooling electricity once. At u=0.50 this is $73/month or $876/year, making C_L=$3,073/month and $36,876/year. Procurement, staff and support have distinct scopes. Installed purchase is a cash outlay, not added again to depreciation. Replacement at year four is represented by the useful life; a future $48,000 replacement cash scenario is disclosed separately, not another annual expense. No utilization discount removes idle ownership costs. All amounts, power and life assumptions are illustrative, not quotes or measurements.
reasoning_steps.title: 7. Non-overlapping local ownership ledger

reasoning_steps.argument: For stand-alone service attribution, A has monthly identity/audit infrastructure $100, operations $300 and procurement/contract labor $50: C_A=$450+V_A, annual $5,400+12V_A. G retains the local ledger and adds external-connector infrastructure $50, operations $300 and procurement/contract work $50, all outside local staff scopes: C_G=$3,473+V_G, annual $41,676+12V_G. F retains G and adds agreement/security setup $7,200 amortized over this one-year study ($600/month), federation identity operations $400, incremental WAN $200 and incident/coordination labor $300: C_F=$4,973+V_F, annual $59,676+12V_F. These F rows total $1,500/month or $18,000/year; setup cash occurs when paid rather than monthly. Remote compute/support charges, if any, must be added separately; the no-usable-peer scenario incurs none. Campus payments to partners are expenses in this home-campus account, while internal transfers cancel only in a consolidated multi-campus account that includes the partner's resource costs. Annual formulas assume the same monthly demand and prices for twelve months, not observed seasonality. L is $3,073/$36,876 as above.
reasoning_steps.title: 8. Four-baseline fully loaded monthly and annual worksheet

reasoning_steps.argument: For an existing funded local platform that would remain powered idle without this study, treat the purchase as sunk and assume the listed staff, support, storage, network and procurement commitments cannot be avoided during the year. Its common idle ownership account is $3,036.50/month. Incremental costs above that same counterfactual are L=$36.50/month ($438/year); A=$450+V_A ($5,400+12V_A/year); G=$436.50+V_G ($5,238+12V_G/year); F=$1,936.50+V_F ($23,238+12V_F/year), using u=0.50 when local service runs. These are not additional rows to add to the fully loaded totals. Adding the common idle account to each incremental option gives the retained-platform campus account; in particular A then costs $3,486.50+V_A rather than its stand-alone $450+V_A. If the hardware and staff can actually be retired or reassigned, that counterfactual changes. New-purchase decisions require the fully loaded ledger and an acquisition/replacement cash schedule, not the small incremental energy figure. With zero new money, L is feasible only if existing energy, staffing and quotas already have funding; zero frontier budget is not zero operating cost.
reasoning_steps.title: 9. Sunk versus incremental decision, with an explicit counterfactual

reasoning_steps.argument: Since V_j <= n_j r <= B under this scenario, positive cap ceilings $2,000/$4,000/$8,000 imply stand-alone monthly/annual upper bounds: A $2,450/$29,400; $4,450/$53,400; $8,450/$101,400. G $5,473/$65,676; $7,473/$89,676; $11,473/$137,676. F with G's admissions and usage $6,973/$83,676; $8,973/$107,676; $12,973/$155,676. These are upper bounds, not expected expenditures, and may be loose when candidate demand is small. At B=0 the configured fixed costs remain A=$450, G=$3,473 and F=$4,973 monthly; closing unused components can instead avoid their optional costs. For the same 100 distinct researchers throughout the year, monthly cost per researcher is C_j/100 and annual cost per researcher is 12C_j/100. Thus L is $30.73/month and $368.76/year per researcher. Monthly useful-task cost is L=3073/800=$3.84125; A=(450+V_A)/(0.9n_A); G=(3473+V_G)/(800+0.9n_G); F is analogous. A's ratio is undefined at n_A=0. Annual useful counts and costs both multiply by twelve, so useful-task ratios do not change. Overall coverage, sensitive coverage and policy refusals remain separate from those ratios.
reasoning_steps.title: 10. Cap ceilings, researcher denominators and useful-task denominators

reasoning_steps.argument: For this worksheet, propose mandatory service of the campus-only stratum with at least 160 useful results out of 200, plus at least 1,400 useful roots overall (70%), using the per-task quality and deadline rules already defined. Among baselines satisfying those gates, minimize fully loaded cost; also report the incremental comparison. These are illustrative planning targets, not approved service policy. L gives 800 overall and fails. A can give 1,620 overall but fails the campus-only requirement at every cap. G reaches the overall gate iff 800+0.9n_G >= 1400, hence integer n_G >= 667. Consequently G needs r <= B/667: approximately $2.9985/$5.9970/$11.9940 at caps $2,000/$4,000/$8,000. At $0, no alternative in the base scenario meets the whole target. At a positive cap, G is the least-cost feasible alternative among these four whenever that inequality holds and F has no usable additional capacity. If it fails, report no feasible baseline rather than silently relaxing classification or increasing the cap. For public-only workloads A can instead be preferred; comparing it with G requires their actual V values and coverage, not an assumed provider rate.
reasoning_steps.title: 11. State the decision target before choosing a winner

reasoning_steps.argument: Assume the partner's spare GPUs occur off peak, while the partner-eligible coding/routine deadlines coincide with its own teaching peak; its batch window is also fully reserved. Thus additional policy-authorized, deadline-feasible peer admission is zero despite nominal federation capacity. Let F keep G's local/API dispatches and incur the itemized $1,500 monthly coordination overhead. Then S_F=S_G and V_F=V_G, whereas C_F=C_G+1500. For every S_G>0, C_F/S_G exceeds C_G/S_G by 1500/S_G, and F also has greater specified administrative cost. This is strict dominance on these worksheet cost/completion measures, not a claim about unmeasured availability or all conceivable federation designs. It narrows the prior throughput counterexample to an explicit zero-usable-capacity case. More generally, writing added useful completions as ΔS and all net added costs as ΔC, cross-multiplication yields C_F/S_F<C_G/S_G iff ΔS/S_G>ΔC/C_G for positive baseline cost/completions and positive F completions. Spare capacity, lower partner overhead or outage resilience could reverse the comparison; nominal GPU count alone cannot.
reasoning_steps.title: 12. Concrete G-dominates-F scenario and its limits

reasoning_steps.argument: Keep the task mix and joint useful fractions fixed only as a bounded toy sensitivity, not an extrapolated queueing law. At demand multipliers d=0.5/1/2, with K=1000 and sensitive-first admission, local admissions are 650/1000/1000; G external candidates are 350/1000/3000; unrestricted-cap G useful totals are 835/1700/3500. A's corresponding maximum useful totals are 810/1620/3240 but still exclude sensitive work. To reach 70% of total demand, G needs at least 200/667/2223 API admissions respectively; feasibility therefore requires floor(B/r) at least those numbers. At d=1 and local K=500/1000/1300, G has local useful counts 400/800/1040, external candidates 1500/1000/700 and unrestricted-cap useful totals 1750/1700/1670. Required API admissions for the 1400 gate are 1112/667/400. The apparently higher unrestricted-cap quality with less local admission arises solely from q_A>q_L; it is a counterexample to identifying more local throughput with more useful completions. In practice model-fit pools, queues, starvation and deadlines must be remeasured whenever capacity or demand changes.
reasoning_steps.title: 13. Hand sensitivity worksheet for demand and capacity

reasoning_steps.argument: Utilization and deadline-feasible admission are separate inputs, not interchangeable measurements. Holding the ownership inventory fixed, u=0.25/0.50/0.75 yields local monthly costs $3,054.75/$3,073/$3,091.25; it does not establish K. A separate illustrative capacity experiment must determine how GPU memory fit, cold starts, maintenance and queue tails change K. At K=1000, changing joint useful fractions changes the required API count to ceil((1400-1000q_L)/q_A), clipped below at zero and checked against 1000 candidates. Examples (q_L,q_A)=(0.8,0.9)/(0.9,0.9)/(0.8,0.7) need 667/556/858 API roots. If q_A=0, APIs cannot repair a local completion shortfall. Increasing all billable rates and ancillary bounds by a common factor α changes r to αr and API admission to min(candidate count,floor(B/(αr))); a price decrease has the reverse effect, only within approved contracts. Multi-call amplification or retries can similarly raise r while reducing quality or deadline success. On a matched eligible unsaturated stratum with cost F_L+vD versus F_A+aD and useful fractions q_L,q_A>0, local cost per useful task is lower exactly when F_L/q_L-F_A/q_A < D(a/q_A-v/q_L). This is the break-even rule, not a numerical price claim or a law valid through saturation.
reasoning_steps.title: 14. Utilization, quality and price sensitivity

reasoning_steps.argument: Propose identity/classification -> eligible-destination filter -> model/context/memory check -> capacity and atomic budget reservation -> queued task -> fresh dispatch authorization -> execution -> reconciliation. The home campus owns each root ID, policy epoch and financial reservation; a partner owns a distinct capacity hold, not a second spendable copy of the budget. Before any payload leaves, bind destination, classification, retention contract, root/attempt ID and current authorization to that attempt. Queued work is rechecked; revocation before dispatch invalidates the authorization and releases only holds proven uncharged. Retries are new attempts within the workflow envelope or require new reservations and fresh policy checks. Timeout/cancellation enters an unresolved state retaining financial liability; only authoritative reconciliation releases it. Unknown policy freshness, WAN partition, quota contention, provider rejection, outage or cost exhaustion produces defer/refuse, never a broader destination. After dispatch, revocation cannot undo disclosure; campuses must approve in-flight handling. This is a proposed state machine, not an implemented safety guarantee. G can use a separately approved portal, but all paid activity must still be financially mediated if claiming a shared hard cap.
reasoning_steps.title: 15. Minimal architecture and explicit fail-closed transitions

reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied peer extracts are unverified and partly truncated; their original saved artifacts were not available for inspection. Adopt as constraints to test, not certified premises: the sovereignty branch's revocation/partition concern and the reliability branch's complete financial mediation requirement. The partition concern also follows directly in the narrow model: if a disconnected peer sees identical cached state whether the home campus has revoked or not, its admission decision cannot distinguish those histories; admitting in the unchanged history also risks admitting in the revoked history. Immediate new-request revocation therefore requires authoritative contact or deferral, unless the campus explicitly accepts weaker lease semantics. This affects F's usable capacity and availability accounting, not local MindRouter's published behavior. Reject treating cached approval or a separately approved account as sufficient evidence of current authorization or budget mediation. Leave recipient compliance, replay prevention, atomic nested ledgers and deployment enforcement unresolved. These peer concerns strengthen the worksheet's uncertainty register but do not establish that federation is generally uneconomic.
reasoning_steps.title: 16. Peer evidence changes the usable-capacity and enforcement tests

reasoning_steps.argument: Proposed 90-day next action: days 1–30 obtain actual source versions/access dates, asset and staff ledgers, provider prices/charging bounds, policy approvals and workload bins; days 31–60 compare paired authorized roots on L/A/G with randomized order, frozen rubrics and root-level token/call/provenance records; days 61–90 test F only with agreements and incremental labor metering. Include maintenance/peak weeks and batch/interactive strata, queue/cold-start/service times, GPU memory fit, quality, availability, starvation and per-campus administrative hours. Fault-inject stale policy, malicious tenant/quota races, WAN/campus/provider outage, rejection, ambiguous charged timeout, cancellation and unsafe-fallback attempts. Proposed immediate stop: unauthorized disclosure, policy bypass or cap violation. Proposed F go: approved mandatory coverage and service gates plus a conservative paired uncertainty bound supporting its net-benefit threshold; otherwise no-go or inconclusive. A starter sample is not a precision guarantee: use an initial authorized variance estimate to size paired root/project-day samples within the budget, and retain inconclusive outcomes. Ask computing whether peer spare capacity overlaps demand; security whether derived artifacts and revocation semantics are acceptable; procurement whether every charge is bounded and which commitments are unavoidable; faculty whether local/frontier results pass the same scientific rubric and provenance requirements; students whether queue shares and deadlines are equitable. These measurements could reverse both G-versus-F and local-versus-API rankings.
reasoning_steps.title: 17. Bounded next measurements and decision gates

artifacts.method: Hypothesis: policy exclusions, deadline-feasible capacity, workflow amplification and coordination overhead can make campus service plus separately approved frontier access preferable to federation. Construct a common hypothetical monthly cohort, distinguish policy eligibility from technical/capacity admission and from useful completion, and reconcile itemized monthly costs to annual equivalents. Leave provider prices as dated-source placeholders. Use worst-case reservations to derive cap-dependent admission thresholds without inventing API rates. The discriminating outcome is whether an authorized baseline satisfies mandatory coverage and quality/latency gates at lower cost; for F versus G, additionally test whether added useful completions exceed the success-adjusted overhead threshold. All numerical inputs are scenario assumptions or hand arithmetic. No source retrieval, computation, workload experiment or pilot occurred. The supplied prior extract establishes continuity but is not independent verification; the worksheet advances its missing four-baseline comparison rather than repeating its aggregate example.
artifacts.next_question: Repair the worksheet's feasibility inference without repeating its valid ledger: add per-stratum admissions and useful-completion parameters, show explicitly why aggregate q_L=0.80 does not imply 160/200 sensitive successes, and state the additional hypothetical sensitive-stratum assumption needed for G to pass. Distinguish imposed scenario totals from expected counts and realized-service guarantees; then recompute the cap-dependent feasible-baseline rule and retain the scoped G-over-F dominance result. Keep API prices unknown, ensure the reservation envelope covers cache misses at uncached rates, and identify the authorization-to-dispatch ordering still requiring implementation and campus approval. No source access, computation or pilot should be implied.
artifacts.note: Unverified research note. Any Investigator Python or SageMath execution, including its source, status, output, and captured artifacts, is recorded below and is not proof by itself.
objections: Material, recoverable inference error: cycle 2 step 11 treats aggregate q_L = 0.80 as establishing sensitive-stratum usefulness. Counterexample: 0/200 sensitive successes and 800/800 other local successes preserve 800/1,000 aggregate usefulness but fail the mandatory gate.

Material, recoverable interpretation gap: useful fractions must be identified as imposed exact scenario fractions, expected probabilities, or empirical estimates. Expected completion counts alone do not guarantee realized coverage or latency/quality service levels.

Material, recoverable enforcement gap: fresh authorization checks and reservation ownership are now described, but their ordering against concurrent revocation, dispatch and recovery is not established. A proposed state machine is not an implemented safety result.
Evidence limitation: published features, current prices and billing bounds, institutional approvals, actual costs, comparative performance and stakeholder responses remain unverified.

argument_steps.title: 7. Non-overlapping local ownership ledger

argument_steps.argument: For stand-alone service attribution, A has monthly identity/audit infrastructure $100, operations $300 and procurement/contract labor $50: C_A=$450+V_A, annual $5,400+12V_A. G retains the local ledger and adds external-connector infrastructure $50, operations $300 and procurement/contract work $50, all outside local staff scopes: C_G=$3,473+V_G, annual $41,676+12V_G. F retains G and adds agreement/security setup $7,200 amortized over this one-year study ($600/month), federation identity operations $400, incremental WAN $200 and incident/coordination labor $300: C_F=$4,973+V_F, annual $59,676+12V_F. These F rows total $1,500/month or $18,000/year; setup cash occurs when paid rather than monthly. Remote compute/support charges, if any, must be added separately; the no-usable-peer scenario incurs none. Campus payments to partners are expenses in this home-campus account, while internal transfers cancel only in a consolidated multi-campus account that includes the partner's resource costs. Annual formulas assume the same monthly demand and prices for twelve months, not observed seasonality. L is $3,073/$36,876 as above.

review.rationale: The connector adds $400/month and federation adds $1,500/month, producing the stated monthly and annual totals. Partner transfers are distinguished from consolidated resource costs, and absent remote charges are restricted to the zero-usable-peer scenario.

argument_steps.title: 8. Four-baseline fully loaded monthly and annual worksheet

argument_steps.argument: For an existing funded local platform that would remain powered idle without this study, treat the purchase as sunk and assume the listed staff, support, storage, network and procurement commitments cannot be avoided during the year. Its common idle ownership account is $3,036.50/month. Incremental costs above that same counterfactual are L=$36.50/month ($438/year); A=$450+V_A ($5,400+12V_A/year); G=$436.50+V_G ($5,238+12V_G/year); F=$1,936.50+V_F ($23,238+12V_F/year), using u=0.50 when local service runs. These are not additional rows to add to the fully loaded totals. Adding the common idle account to each incremental option gives the retained-platform campus account; in particular A then costs $3,486.50+V_A rather than its stand-alone $450+V_A. If the hardware and staff can actually be retired or reassigned, that counterfactual changes. New-purchase decisions require the fully loaded ledger and an acquisition/replacement cash schedule, not the small incremental energy figure. With zero new money, L is feasible only if existing energy, staffing and quotas already have funding; zero frontier budget is not zero operating cost.

review.rationale: Relative to the explicitly retained idle-platform counterfactual, busy energy adds $36.50/month and the connector/federation increments reconcile to the ownership accounts. The different stand-alone and retained-platform A costs are correctly separated rather than mixed.

argument_steps.title: 9. Sunk versus incremental decision, with an explicit counterfactual

argument_steps.argument: Since V_j <= n_j r <= B under this scenario, positive cap ceilings $2,000/$4,000/$8,000 imply stand-alone monthly/annual upper bounds: A $2,450/$29,400; $4,450/$53,400; $8,450/$101,400. G $5,473/$65,676; $7,473/$89,676; $11,473/$137,676. F with G's admissions and usage $6,973/$83,676; $8,973/$107,676; $12,973/$155,676. These are upper bounds, not expected expenditures, and may be loose when candidate demand is small. At B=0 the configured fixed costs remain A=$450, G=$3,473 and F=$4,973 monthly; closing unused components can instead avoid their optional costs. For the same 100 distinct researchers throughout the year, monthly cost per researcher is C_j/100 and annual cost per researcher is 12C_j/100. Thus L is $30.73/month and $368.76/year per researcher. Monthly useful-task cost is L=3073/800=$3.84125; A=(450+V_A)/(0.9n_A); G=(3473+V_G)/(800+0.9n_G); F is analogous. A's ratio is undefined at n_A=0. Annual useful counts and costs both multiply by twelve, so useful-task ratios do not change. Overall coverage, sensitive coverage and policy refusals remain separate from those ratios.

review.rationale: Each cap upper bound adds B to the relevant fixed total, and its annual equivalent multiplies by twelve. Researcher denominators use the fixed distinct cohort, and 3073/800 equals 3.84125. The bounds are not presented as expected spending.

argument_steps.title: 10. Cap ceilings, researcher denominators and useful-task denominators

argument_steps.argument: For this worksheet, propose mandatory service of the campus-only stratum with at least 160 useful results out of 200, plus at least 1,400 useful roots overall (70%), using the per-task quality and deadline rules already defined. Among baselines satisfying those gates, minimize fully loaded cost; also report the incremental comparison. These are illustrative planning targets, not approved service policy. L gives 800 overall and fails. A can give 1,620 overall but fails the campus-only requirement at every cap. G reaches the overall gate iff 800+0.9n_G >= 1400, hence integer n_G >= 667. Consequently G needs r <= B/667: approximately $2.9985/$5.9970/$11.9940 at caps $2,000/$4,000/$8,000. At $0, no alternative in the base scenario meets the whole target. At a positive cap, G is the least-cost feasible alternative among these four whenever that inequality holds and F has no usable additional capacity. If it fails, report no feasible baseline rather than silently relaxing classification or increasing the cap. For public-only workloads A can instead be preferred; comparing it with G requires their actual V values and coverage, not an assumed provider rate.

review.objection: With all 200 sensitive local roots failing and all 800 other admitted local roots succeeding, q_L remains 0.80. G may pass aggregate coverage while failing sensitive coverage. Add a sensitive-stratum usefulness premise before calling G feasible or least-cost feasible; distinguish expected counts from guaranteed outcomes.
review.rationale: The aggregate inequality gives integer n>=667, and A necessarily fails a campus-only requirement. However, G's sensitive-stratum success is not entailed by the aggregate useful fraction.

argument_steps.title: 11. State the decision target before choosing a winner

argument_steps.argument: Assume the partner's spare GPUs occur off peak, while the partner-eligible coding/routine deadlines coincide with its own teaching peak; its batch window is also fully reserved. Thus additional policy-authorized, deadline-feasible peer admission is zero despite nominal federation capacity. Let F keep G's local/API dispatches and incur the itemized $1,500 monthly coordination overhead. Then S_F=S_G and V_F=V_G, whereas C_F=C_G+1500. For every S_G>0, C_F/S_G exceeds C_G/S_G by 1500/S_G, and F also has greater specified administrative cost. This is strict dominance on these worksheet cost/completion measures, not a claim about unmeasured availability or all conceivable federation designs. It narrows the prior throughput counterexample to an explicit zero-usable-capacity case. More generally, writing added useful completions as ΔS and all net added costs as ΔC, cross-multiplication yields C_F/S_F<C_G/S_G iff ΔS/S_G>ΔC/C_G for positive baseline cost/completions and positive F completions. Spare capacity, lower partner overhead or outage resilience could reverse the comparison; nominal GPU count alone cannot.

review.rationale: Identical dispatches imply identical usage and completions in this imposed scenario, while the ledger adds $1,500. For positive completions the unit-cost disadvantage is exactly 1500/S_G. The broader relative-gain threshold also follows by positive-denominator cross-multiplication and is appropriately not generalized to availability.

argument_steps.title: 12. Concrete G-dominates-F scenario and its limits

argument_steps.argument: Keep the task mix and joint useful fractions fixed only as a bounded toy sensitivity, not an extrapolated queueing law. At demand multipliers d=0.5/1/2, with K=1000 and sensitive-first admission, local admissions are 650/1000/1000; G external candidates are 350/1000/3000; unrestricted-cap G useful totals are 835/1700/3500. A's corresponding maximum useful totals are 810/1620/3240 but still exclude sensitive work. To reach 70% of total demand, G needs at least 200/667/2223 API admissions respectively; feasibility therefore requires floor(B/r) at least those numbers. At d=1 and local K=500/1000/1300, G has local useful counts 400/800/1040, external candidates 1500/1000/700 and unrestricted-cap useful totals 1750/1700/1670. Required API admissions for the 1400 gate are 1112/667/400. The apparently higher unrestricted-cap quality with less local admission arises solely from q_A>q_L; it is a counterexample to identifying more local throughput with more useful completions. In practice model-fit pools, queues, starvation and deadlines must be remeasured whenever capacity or demand changes.

review.rationale: The demand and capacity sensitivity arithmetic checks: the stated admissions partition each workload, useful totals use 0.8 and 0.9 consistently, and the ceiling calculations produce 200/667/2223 and 1112/667/400. These concern aggregate planning coverage only.

argument_steps.title: 13. Hand sensitivity worksheet for demand and capacity

argument_steps.argument: Utilization and deadline-feasible admission are separate inputs, not interchangeable measurements. Holding the ownership inventory fixed, u=0.25/0.50/0.75 yields local monthly costs $3,054.75/$3,073/$3,091.25; it does not establish K. A separate illustrative capacity experiment must determine how GPU memory fit, cold starts, maintenance and queue tails change K. At K=1000, changing joint useful fractions changes the required API count to ceil((1400-1000q_L)/q_A), clipped below at zero and checked against 1000 candidates. Examples (q_L,q_A)=(0.8,0.9)/(0.9,0.9)/(0.8,0.7) need 667/556/858 API roots. If q_A=0, APIs cannot repair a local completion shortfall. Increasing all billable rates and ancillary bounds by a common factor α changes r to αr and API admission to min(candidate count,floor(B/(αr))); a price decrease has the reverse effect, only within approved contracts. Multi-call amplification or retries can similarly raise r while reducing quality or deadline success. On a matched eligible unsaturated stratum with cost F_L+vD versus F_A+aD and useful fractions q_L,q_A>0, local cost per useful task is lower exactly when F_L/q_L-F_A/q_A < D(a/q_A-v/q_L). This is the break-even rule, not a numerical price claim or a law valid through saturation.

review.rationale: The utilization costs and quality-dependent admission ceilings are correct. Scaling every charge bound by alpha scales r likewise. The crossover inequality follows by multiplying costs per useful task by positive demand and retains its unsaturated-range restriction.

argument_steps.title: 14. Utilization, quality and price sensitivity

argument_steps.argument: Propose identity/classification -> eligible-destination filter -> model/context/memory check -> capacity and atomic budget reservation -> queued task -> fresh dispatch authorization -> execution -> reconciliation. The home campus owns each root ID, policy epoch and financial reservation; a partner owns a distinct capacity hold, not a second spendable copy of the budget. Before any payload leaves, bind destination, classification, retention contract, root/attempt ID and current authorization to that attempt. Queued work is rechecked; revocation before dispatch invalidates the authorization and releases only holds proven uncharged. Retries are new attempts within the workflow envelope or require new reservations and fresh policy checks. Timeout/cancellation enters an unresolved state retaining financial liability; only authoritative reconciliation releases it. Unknown policy freshness, WAN partition, quota contention, provider rejection, outage or cost exhaustion produces defer/refuse, never a broader destination. After dispatch, revocation cannot undo disclosure; campuses must approve in-flight handling. This is a proposed state machine, not an implemented safety guarantee. G can use a separately approved portal, but all paid activity must still be financially mediated if claiming a shared hard cap.

review.objection: Specify the authorization/dispatch linearization point and concurrent-revocation behavior, including partitions between the fresh check and payload release. Durable idempotent reservation transitions and recipient enforcement still need implementation tests and approved semantics.
review.rationale: The proposal now identifies home financial ownership, separate partner capacity holds, fresh checks and unresolved liabilities. This addresses missing exposition but does not establish enforcement.

argument_steps.title: 15. Minimal architecture and explicit fail-closed transitions

argument_steps.argument: The supplied peer extracts are unverified and partly truncated; their original saved artifacts were not available for inspection. Adopt as constraints to test, not certified premises: the sovereignty branch's revocation/partition concern and the reliability branch's complete financial mediation requirement. The partition concern also follows directly in the narrow model: if a disconnected peer sees identical cached state whether the home campus has revoked or not, its admission decision cannot distinguish those histories; admitting in the unchanged history also risks admitting in the revoked history. Immediate new-request revocation therefore requires authoritative contact or deferral, unless the campus explicitly accepts weaker lease semantics. This affects F's usable capacity and availability accounting, not local MindRouter's published behavior. Reject treating cached approval or a separately approved account as sufficient evidence of current authorization or budget mediation. Leave recipient compliance, replay prevention, atomic nested ledgers and deployment enforcement unresolved. These peer concerns strengthen the worksheet's uncertainty register but do not establish that federation is generally uneconomic.

review.rationale: Under the supplied peer's explicit no-distinguishing-information and no-prior-authorization assumptions, identical disconnected observations cannot distinguish revocation histories. Deferral or weaker approved semantics follows in that narrow model. The financial-mediation requirement also matches the supplied ledger assumptions, without establishing implementation.

argument_steps.title: 16. Peer evidence changes the usable-capacity and enforcement tests

argument_steps.argument: Proposed 90-day next action: days 1–30 obtain actual source versions/access dates, asset and staff ledgers, provider prices/charging bounds, policy approvals and workload bins; days 31–60 compare paired authorized roots on L/A/G with randomized order, frozen rubrics and root-level token/call/provenance records; days 61–90 test F only with agreements and incremental labor metering. Include maintenance/peak weeks and batch/interactive strata, queue/cold-start/service times, GPU memory fit, quality, availability, starvation and per-campus administrative hours. Fault-inject stale policy, malicious tenant/quota races, WAN/campus/provider outage, rejection, ambiguous charged timeout, cancellation and unsafe-fallback attempts. Proposed immediate stop: unauthorized disclosure, policy bypass or cap violation. Proposed F go: approved mandatory coverage and service gates plus a conservative paired uncertainty bound supporting its net-benefit threshold; otherwise no-go or inconclusive. A starter sample is not a precision guarantee: use an initial authorized variance estimate to size paired root/project-day samples within the budget, and retain inconclusive outcomes. Ask computing whether peer spare capacity overlaps demand; security whether derived artifacts and revocation semantics are acceptable; procurement whether every charge is bounded and which commitments are unavoidable; faculty whether local/frontier results pass the same scientific rubric and provenance requirements; students whether queue shares and deadlines are equitable. These measurements could reverse both G-versus-F and local-versus-API rankings.

review.rationale: As an approval-dependent plan rather than evidence, the sequence includes paired roots, peak and maintenance periods, fault injection, root/project-day dependence and inconclusive outcomes. It correctly treats a starter sample as insufficient to guarantee precision.

objective_review.argument_summary: Cycle 2 supplies consistent accounting: local fixed ownership is $3,000/month, energy at u=0.5 is $73/month, and the L/G/F fixed totals are $3,073/$3,473/$4,973. Conservative reservations yield min(candidate count, floor(B/r)) admissions under the stated enforceable-bound assumptions. Positive-denominator algebra supports the aggregate 667-admission threshold and the $1,500 zero-gain federation disadvantage. Cycle 1 artifact 5c8fdc17-0ce8-4ea3-b8dc-79e05f97d0db, reasoning steps 5–8, supplies the scoped crossover, federation threshold, synthetic throughput counterexample and conditional ledger argument. Their supplied derivations remain usable, agent-reviewed only. Cycle 2 does not supply the stratum-level premise needed to infer sensitive coverage from aggregate local usefulness.
