reasoning_steps.argument: L means campus-local inference only; A means approved frontier API only; G means campus gateway plus separately approved external access; F means a proposed federation added to G. The project attributes OpenAI/Ollama/Anthropic client translation, Ollama/vLLM backends, WDRR scheduling, per-user quotas, audit logging and GPU telemetry to MindRouter's published campus gateway. These are project-supplied descriptions of published claims, not independently measured capabilities here. Starting references are https://mindrouter.ai/documentation.html and https://ai4ra.uidaho.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Sheneman_MindRouter_PEARC26_Short_Paper.pdf. Their reported historical review date is 2026-10-31; this session has no access date because neither was accessed. No current or changed claim is verified. Neither frontier routing nor federation is represented as an existing MindRouter feature. Only the supplied bounded extract of the prior artifact was reviewed, not its saved original.

review.rationale: The baseline definitions preserve the distinction between the published campus gateway and hypothetical extensions. Feature statements are explicitly attributed to project text, and the historical review date is not misrepresented as a new access date.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Evidence boundary and four alternatives

reasoning_steps.argument: Use 100 distinct active researchers and 2,000 root tasks each month: coding 600, routine analysis 400, demanding scientific reasoning 300, multimodal/long-context 200, agentic workflows 200, campus-only sensitive analysis 200, reproducible batches 100. These are disjoint accounting bins, not a claim that sensitivity is a distinct technical task type. Proposed deadlines respectively are 30 s, 120 s, 600 s, 180 s, 900 s end-to-end, 120 s and 24 h. A useful completion must be authorized, meet its deadline, pass the frozen task rubric and contain no critical factual/security error. Rubrics use held-out coding tests, known-result/unit checks, blinded scientific review, labeled multimodal fixtures and agent root-goal/tool-boundary checks. Batch acceptance requires complete provenance and a specified numerical tolerance; it does not assume bitwise API replay. Calls, Investigator/Skeptic exchanges and retries remain descendants of one root. Correct refusal is recorded separately, not counted as delivered research. These deadlines and rubrics require campus approval.

review.rationale: The workload bins sum to 2,000 roots. Root-level counting, joint quality/deadline acceptance and separate refusal accounting define a coherent hypothetical experiment under the listed workload and approval-dependent rubric assumptions.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Common hypothetical workload and usefulness definition

reasoning_steps.argument: For this scenario only, the campus approves all 2,000 roots locally, approves 1,800 non-sensitive roots at one named API destination, and approves only coding, routine analysis and batches at a named partner campus: 1,100 partner-eligible roots. The 200 sensitive roots remain campus-only. Thus policy-eligible counts are L=2,000, A=1,800, G=2,000 and F=2,000; federation does not increase eligibility by default. Separately, assume local model/context/memory requirements admit only coding, routine, sensitive analysis and batch work: 1,300 technically suitable roots. The other 700 require capabilities unavailable in this hypothetical local installation. Assume the approved API can technically serve all 1,800 eligible roots. These are proposed domain and capability assumptions, not university policy or model benchmark findings. Restricted, student, patient, controlled, sponsor-restricted and unpublished content, including derived prompts, outputs, logs, embeddings and cache, stays inside its approved domains; ambiguous classification gets no execution destination until resolved.

review.rationale: Under the explicitly hypothetical approval matrix, API eligibility is 2,000 minus 200, partner eligibility is 600+400+100, and local technical suitability is 600+400+200+100. Policy permission and model fit are correctly separated.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Keep policy eligibility separate from capability

reasoning_steps.argument: Assume local deadline-feasible admission capacity K=1,000 roots/month after interactive/batch scheduling, maintenance and queue headroom. Reserve capacity first for the 200 campus-only roots; an illustrative remaining allocation is coding 400, routine 300 and batches 100. Local overflow is coding 200 and routine 100. Assume useful fractions among admitted roots are q_L=0.80 locally and q_A=0.90 at the API, including both quality and end-to-end deadline failures; these are joint fractions, not products of independent events. Before API budget limits, the worksheet is: L admits 1,000 local roots and yields 800 useful; A admits up to 1,800 API roots and yields up to 1,620 useful but no sensitive completions; G admits 1,000 local plus up to 1,000 API roots and yields up to 1,700 useful. G's external candidate set is the 700 capability-demanding roots plus 300 overflow roots, with no double counting. Actual admitted counts and quality must later be reported by stratum; these aggregate fractions do not establish any individual stratum's service guarantee.

review.rationale: The local allocation sums to 1,000, leaving 300 locally suitable overflow roots and 700 capability-demanding roots for G's 1,000 external candidates. Multiplication by the imposed aggregate useful fractions gives the stated aggregate totals. The step correctly disclaims individual-stratum guarantees.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Base admission and useful-completion worksheet

reasoning_steps.argument: For one named provider/model/region/contract, leave these fields blank pending a dated quote: p_in[d], p_cached[d], p_out[d] in dollars per million tokens; p_tools[d] per billable tool unit; p_embed[d] per million embedding tokens; p_egress[d] per GB; any request fees, taxes and monthly minimum M[d]. Here d is the actual price-effective/access date, currently unavailable. A hypothetical root envelope allows at most eight total calls, including Investigator/Skeptic turns and retries, and at most 128,000 uncached input, 32,000 cached input and 16,000 output tokens summed across those calls. Let h[d] be an enforceable maximum for all ancillary root charges, including multimodal charges, tools, embeddings, egress and applicable tax exposure. A candidate reservation is r=0.128p_in[d]+0.032p_cached[d]+0.016p_out[d]+h[d]. Cache misses must be bounded at the uncached rate; otherwise this expression is not a valid upper bound. Different provider tokenization, vision/audio billing and unbounded tools require revised envelopes or refusal. Actual monthly usage V_j is the sum of actual charges across all admitted descendants, not the number of useful roots times a single-call price.

review.rationale: The token coefficients correctly convert the proposed envelope to millions of tokens. This is only a candidate reservation expression under the listed enforceable-r assumption; the text explicitly recognizes that cache misses and ancillary billing can invalidate it.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. API price placeholders and root-level amplification

reasoning_steps.argument: Assume r>0 is enforceable, no opening unresolved liability or minimum commitment, and use a conservative monthly plan that does not reuse reservation savings. Then n_A=min(1800,floor(B/r)); n_G=min(1000,floor(B/r)). This is a reproducible worst-case plan, not maximum achievable throughput under rolling reconciliation. The four cap columns B=$0/$2,000/$4,000/$8,000 give G API admissions 0/min(1000,floor(2000/r))/min(1000,floor(4000/r))/min(1000,floor(8000/r)); useful counts are 800+0.9n_G. A uses the same expressions with ceiling 1,800 and useful counts 0.9n_A. All 1,000 G API candidates fit only if r <= $2/$4/$8 at the three positive caps. All 1,800 A candidates fit only if r <= $1.111.../$2.222.../$4.444..., respectively. These numbers are allowable liability thresholds, not quoted API prices. With B=0, neither free credits nor an unapproved destination is assumed. If no finite charging bound can be established, paid admission is disabled even for positive B. For a contractual minimum, replace usage billing by the actual contractual function, reserve the minimum and outstanding liabilities first, and recompute admissions; do not add a minimum to usage if it already includes that usage.

review.rationale: With positive enforceable r, no opening liabilities or commitment, and no recycling of savings, reserving n roots requires nr<=B. The floor formulas and full-admission liability thresholds follow directly; disabling paid admission when no bound exists preserves the stated conditional scope.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Hard-cap admission worksheet without invented rates

reasoning_steps.argument: Hypothetical local monthly/annual equivalent ledger: installed GPU/host asset $48,000, zero residual, four-year life gives depreciation $1,000/$12,000; storage including approved audit storage $200/$2,400; network $100/$1,200; hardware support $200/$2,400; operations staff including audit operations $1,400/$16,800; procurement labor excluding operations $100/$1,200. These fixed ownership rows total $3,000/$36,000. Assume aggregate IT power 0.4 kW idle and 1.2 kW busy, utilization u, PUE 1.25 and electricity $0.10/kWh. Annual-average monthly energy is 730×1.25×[0.4+0.8u]×0.10 = $36.50+$73u, including cooling electricity once. At u=0.50 this is $73/month or $876/year, making C_L=$3,073/month and $36,876/year. Procurement, staff and support have distinct scopes. Installed purchase is a cash outlay, not added again to depreciation. Replacement at year four is represented by the useful life; a future $48,000 replacement cash scenario is disclosed separately, not another annual expense. No utilization discount removes idle ownership costs. All amounts, power and life assumptions are illustrative, not quotes or measurements.

review.rationale: The fixed rows total $3,000/month. The power model yields $36.50+$73u, hence $73 at u=0.5 and $36,876 annual local ownership. Purchase and depreciation are not added twice, and cooling electricity is counted once.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Non-overlapping local ownership ledger

reasoning_steps.argument: For stand-alone service attribution, A has monthly identity/audit infrastructure $100, operations $300 and procurement/contract labor $50: C_A=$450+V_A, annual $5,400+12V_A. G retains the local ledger and adds external-connector infrastructure $50, operations $300 and procurement/contract work $50, all outside local staff scopes: C_G=$3,473+V_G, annual $41,676+12V_G. F retains G and adds agreement/security setup $7,200 amortized over this one-year study ($600/month), federation identity operations $400, incremental WAN $200 and incident/coordination labor $300: C_F=$4,973+V_F, annual $59,676+12V_F. These F rows total $1,500/month or $18,000/year; setup cash occurs when paid rather than monthly. Remote compute/support charges, if any, must be added separately; the no-usable-peer scenario incurs none. Campus payments to partners are expenses in this home-campus account, while internal transfers cancel only in a consolidated multi-campus account that includes the partner's resource costs. Annual formulas assume the same monthly demand and prices for twelve months, not observed seasonality. L is $3,073/$36,876 as above.

review.rationale: The connector adds $400/month and federation adds $1,500/month, producing the stated monthly and annual totals. Partner transfers are distinguished from consolidated resource costs, and absent remote charges are restricted to the zero-usable-peer scenario.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Four-baseline fully loaded monthly and annual worksheet

reasoning_steps.argument: For an existing funded local platform that would remain powered idle without this study, treat the purchase as sunk and assume the listed staff, support, storage, network and procurement commitments cannot be avoided during the year. Its common idle ownership account is $3,036.50/month. Incremental costs above that same counterfactual are L=$36.50/month ($438/year); A=$450+V_A ($5,400+12V_A/year); G=$436.50+V_G ($5,238+12V_G/year); F=$1,936.50+V_F ($23,238+12V_F/year), using u=0.50 when local service runs. These are not additional rows to add to the fully loaded totals. Adding the common idle account to each incremental option gives the retained-platform campus account; in particular A then costs $3,486.50+V_A rather than its stand-alone $450+V_A. If the hardware and staff can actually be retired or reassigned, that counterfactual changes. New-purchase decisions require the fully loaded ledger and an acquisition/replacement cash schedule, not the small incremental energy figure. With zero new money, L is feasible only if existing energy, staffing and quotas already have funding; zero frontier budget is not zero operating cost.

review.rationale: Relative to the explicitly retained idle-platform counterfactual, busy energy adds $36.50/month and the connector/federation increments reconcile to the ownership accounts. The different stand-alone and retained-platform A costs are correctly separated rather than mixed.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Sunk versus incremental decision, with an explicit counterfactual

reasoning_steps.argument: Since V_j <= n_j r <= B under this scenario, positive cap ceilings $2,000/$4,000/$8,000 imply stand-alone monthly/annual upper bounds: A $2,450/$29,400; $4,450/$53,400; $8,450/$101,400. G $5,473/$65,676; $7,473/$89,676; $11,473/$137,676. F with G's admissions and usage $6,973/$83,676; $8,973/$107,676; $12,973/$155,676. These are upper bounds, not expected expenditures, and may be loose when candidate demand is small. At B=0 the configured fixed costs remain A=$450, G=$3,473 and F=$4,973 monthly; closing unused components can instead avoid their optional costs. For the same 100 distinct researchers throughout the year, monthly cost per researcher is C_j/100 and annual cost per researcher is 12C_j/100. Thus L is $30.73/month and $368.76/year per researcher. Monthly useful-task cost is L=3073/800=$3.84125; A=(450+V_A)/(0.9n_A); G=(3473+V_G)/(800+0.9n_G); F is analogous. A's ratio is undefined at n_A=0. Annual useful counts and costs both multiply by twelve, so useful-task ratios do not change. Overall coverage, sensitive coverage and policy refusals remain separate from those ratios.

review.rationale: Each cap upper bound adds B to the relevant fixed total, and its annual equivalent multiplies by twelve. Researcher denominators use the fixed distinct cohort, and 3073/800 equals 3.84125. The bounds are not presented as expected spending.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Cap ceilings, researcher denominators and useful-task denominators

reasoning_steps.argument: For this worksheet, propose mandatory service of the campus-only stratum with at least 160 useful results out of 200, plus at least 1,400 useful roots overall (70%), using the per-task quality and deadline rules already defined. Among baselines satisfying those gates, minimize fully loaded cost; also report the incremental comparison. These are illustrative planning targets, not approved service policy. L gives 800 overall and fails. A can give 1,620 overall but fails the campus-only requirement at every cap. G reaches the overall gate iff 800+0.9n_G >= 1400, hence integer n_G >= 667. Consequently G needs r <= B/667: approximately $2.9985/$5.9970/$11.9940 at caps $2,000/$4,000/$8,000. At $0, no alternative in the base scenario meets the whole target. At a positive cap, G is the least-cost feasible alternative among these four whenever that inequality holds and F has no usable additional capacity. If it fails, report no feasible baseline rather than silently relaxing classification or increasing the cap. For public-only workloads A can instead be preferred; comparing it with G requires their actual V values and coverage, not an assumed provider rate.

review.objection: With all 200 sensitive local roots failing and all 800 other admitted local roots succeeding, q_L remains 0.80. G may pass aggregate coverage while failing sensitive coverage. Add a sensitive-stratum usefulness premise before calling G feasible or least-cost feasible; distinguish expected counts from guaranteed outcomes.
review.rationale: The aggregate inequality gives integer n>=667, and A necessarily fails a campus-only requirement. However, G's sensitive-stratum success is not entailed by the aggregate useful fraction.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. State the decision target before choosing a winner

reasoning_steps.argument: Assume the partner's spare GPUs occur off peak, while the partner-eligible coding/routine deadlines coincide with its own teaching peak; its batch window is also fully reserved. Thus additional policy-authorized, deadline-feasible peer admission is zero despite nominal federation capacity. Let F keep G's local/API dispatches and incur the itemized $1,500 monthly coordination overhead. Then S_F=S_G and V_F=V_G, whereas C_F=C_G+1500. For every S_G>0, C_F/S_G exceeds C_G/S_G by 1500/S_G, and F also has greater specified administrative cost. This is strict dominance on these worksheet cost/completion measures, not a claim about unmeasured availability or all conceivable federation designs. It narrows the prior throughput counterexample to an explicit zero-usable-capacity case. More generally, writing added useful completions as ΔS and all net added costs as ΔC, cross-multiplication yields C_F/S_F<C_G/S_G iff ΔS/S_G>ΔC/C_G for positive baseline cost/completions and positive F completions. Spare capacity, lower partner overhead or outage resilience could reverse the comparison; nominal GPU count alone cannot.

review.rationale: Identical dispatches imply identical usage and completions in this imposed scenario, while the ledger adds $1,500. For positive completions the unit-cost disadvantage is exactly 1500/S_G. The broader relative-gain threshold also follows by positive-denominator cross-multiplication and is appropriately not generalized to availability.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Concrete G-dominates-F scenario and its limits

reasoning_steps.argument: Keep the task mix and joint useful fractions fixed only as a bounded toy sensitivity, not an extrapolated queueing law. At demand multipliers d=0.5/1/2, with K=1000 and sensitive-first admission, local admissions are 650/1000/1000; G external candidates are 350/1000/3000; unrestricted-cap G useful totals are 835/1700/3500. A's corresponding maximum useful totals are 810/1620/3240 but still exclude sensitive work. To reach 70% of total demand, G needs at least 200/667/2223 API admissions respectively; feasibility therefore requires floor(B/r) at least those numbers. At d=1 and local K=500/1000/1300, G has local useful counts 400/800/1040, external candidates 1500/1000/700 and unrestricted-cap useful totals 1750/1700/1670. Required API admissions for the 1400 gate are 1112/667/400. The apparently higher unrestricted-cap quality with less local admission arises solely from q_A>q_L; it is a counterexample to identifying more local throughput with more useful completions. In practice model-fit pools, queues, starvation and deadlines must be remeasured whenever capacity or demand changes.

review.rationale: The demand and capacity sensitivity arithmetic checks: the stated admissions partition each workload, useful totals use 0.8 and 0.9 consistently, and the ceiling calculations produce 200/667/2223 and 1112/667/400. These concern aggregate planning coverage only.

reasoning_steps.title: 13. Hand sensitivity worksheet for demand and capacity

reasoning_steps.argument: Utilization and deadline-feasible admission are separate inputs, not interchangeable measurements. Holding the ownership inventory fixed, u=0.25/0.50/0.75 yields local monthly costs $3,054.75/$3,073/$3,091.25; it does not establish K. A separate illustrative capacity experiment must determine how GPU memory fit, cold starts, maintenance and queue tails change K. At K=1000, changing joint useful fractions changes the required API count to ceil((1400-1000q_L)/q_A), clipped below at zero and checked against 1000 candidates. Examples (q_L,q_A)=(0.8,0.9)/(0.9,0.9)/(0.8,0.7) need 667/556/858 API roots. If q_A=0, APIs cannot repair a local completion shortfall. Increasing all billable rates and ancillary bounds by a common factor α changes r to αr and API admission to min(candidate count,floor(B/(αr))); a price decrease has the reverse effect, only within approved contracts. Multi-call amplification or retries can similarly raise r while reducing quality or deadline success. On a matched eligible unsaturated stratum with cost F_L+vD versus F_A+aD and useful fractions q_L,q_A>0, local cost per useful task is lower exactly when F_L/q_L-F_A/q_A < D(a/q_A-v/q_L). This is the break-even rule, not a numerical price claim or a law valid through saturation.

review.rationale: The utilization costs and quality-dependent admission ceilings are correct. Scaling every charge bound by alpha scales r likewise. The crossover inequality follows by multiplying costs per useful task by positive demand and retains its unsaturated-range restriction.

reasoning_steps.title: 14. Utilization, quality and price sensitivity

reasoning_steps.argument: Propose identity/classification -> eligible-destination filter -> model/context/memory check -> capacity and atomic budget reservation -> queued task -> fresh dispatch authorization -> execution -> reconciliation. The home campus owns each root ID, policy epoch and financial reservation; a partner owns a distinct capacity hold, not a second spendable copy of the budget. Before any payload leaves, bind destination, classification, retention contract, root/attempt ID and current authorization to that attempt. Queued work is rechecked; revocation before dispatch invalidates the authorization and releases only holds proven uncharged. Retries are new attempts within the workflow envelope or require new reservations and fresh policy checks. Timeout/cancellation enters an unresolved state retaining financial liability; only authoritative reconciliation releases it. Unknown policy freshness, WAN partition, quota contention, provider rejection, outage or cost exhaustion produces defer/refuse, never a broader destination. After dispatch, revocation cannot undo disclosure; campuses must approve in-flight handling. This is a proposed state machine, not an implemented safety guarantee. G can use a separately approved portal, but all paid activity must still be financially mediated if claiming a shared hard cap.

review.objection: Specify the authorization/dispatch linearization point and concurrent-revocation behavior, including partitions between the fresh check and payload release. Durable idempotent reservation transitions and recipient enforcement still need implementation tests and approved semantics.
review.rationale: The proposal now identifies home financial ownership, separate partner capacity holds, fresh checks and unresolved liabilities. This addresses missing exposition but does not establish enforcement.

reasoning_steps.title: 15. Minimal architecture and explicit fail-closed transitions

reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied peer extracts are unverified and partly truncated; their original saved artifacts were not available for inspection. Adopt as constraints to test, not certified premises: the sovereignty branch's revocation/partition concern and the reliability branch's complete financial mediation requirement. The partition concern also follows directly in the narrow model: if a disconnected peer sees identical cached state whether the home campus has revoked or not, its admission decision cannot distinguish those histories; admitting in the unchanged history also risks admitting in the revoked history. Immediate new-request revocation therefore requires authoritative contact or deferral, unless the campus explicitly accepts weaker lease semantics. This affects F's usable capacity and availability accounting, not local MindRouter's published behavior. Reject treating cached approval or a separately approved account as sufficient evidence of current authorization or budget mediation. Leave recipient compliance, replay prevention, atomic nested ledgers and deployment enforcement unresolved. These peer concerns strengthen the worksheet's uncertainty register but do not establish that federation is generally uneconomic.

review.rationale: Under the supplied peer's explicit no-distinguishing-information and no-prior-authorization assumptions, identical disconnected observations cannot distinguish revocation histories. Deferral or weaker approved semantics follows in that narrow model. The financial-mediation requirement also matches the supplied ledger assumptions, without establishing implementation.

reasoning_steps.title: 16. Peer evidence changes the usable-capacity and enforcement tests

reasoning_steps.argument: Proposed 90-day next action: days 1–30 obtain actual source versions/access dates, asset and staff ledgers, provider prices/charging bounds, policy approvals and workload bins; days 31–60 compare paired authorized roots on L/A/G with randomized order, frozen rubrics and root-level token/call/provenance records; days 61–90 test F only with agreements and incremental labor metering. Include maintenance/peak weeks and batch/interactive strata, queue/cold-start/service times, GPU memory fit, quality, availability, starvation and per-campus administrative hours. Fault-inject stale policy, malicious tenant/quota races, WAN/campus/provider outage, rejection, ambiguous charged timeout, cancellation and unsafe-fallback attempts. Proposed immediate stop: unauthorized disclosure, policy bypass or cap violation. Proposed F go: approved mandatory coverage and service gates plus a conservative paired uncertainty bound supporting its net-benefit threshold; otherwise no-go or inconclusive. A starter sample is not a precision guarantee: use an initial authorized variance estimate to size paired root/project-day samples within the budget, and retain inconclusive outcomes. Ask computing whether peer spare capacity overlaps demand; security whether derived artifacts and revocation semantics are acceptable; procurement whether every charge is bounded and which commitments are unavoidable; faculty whether local/frontier results pass the same scientific rubric and provenance requirements; students whether queue shares and deadlines are equitable. These measurements could reverse both G-versus-F and local-versus-API rankings.

review.rationale: As an approval-dependent plan rather than evidence, the sequence includes paired roots, peak and maintenance periods, fault injection, root/project-day dependence and inconclusive outcomes. It correctly treats a starter sample as insufficient to guarantee precision.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Evidence boundary and changes from the previous proposal

reasoning_steps.argument: G provides campus-local inference through the gateway and a separately approved external workflow; F adds approved remote-campus execution. Federation and frontier routing remain hypothetical extensions, not asserted MindRouter features. Both arms use identical home-campus classification, identity, retention, audit and destination rules, local resource allocations, paid-access entitlements and parent-task spending limits. F receives the declared additional remote capacity, whose operating and agreement costs are counted rather than treated as free. Separate external access must still have complete financial mediation if the earlier hard-cap argument is invoked. Approval alone is insufficient. No outage, model mismatch, better score, cancellation or budget exhaustion authorizes a new destination. Ambiguous classification fails closed. Revalidate policy and reserve funds before every billable subcall; retain unresolved liabilities. Public or synthetic tasks are used until all relevant campuses approve real-data processing.
reasoning_steps.title: 2. Arms, policy boundaries and comparable resources

reasoning_steps.argument: A parent task is one registered research objective with an input snapshot, requested output, rubric, deadline, policy classification, provenance requirements and total resource envelope. Agent calls, tools, retries and reproducibility repeats are children, not additional tasks. Before routing, register every submitted parent task and distinguish: N_requested, all requests; N_authorized, requests with adequate classification and home-campus permission for at least one studied path; N_pair, authorized tasks permitted to undergo both G and F evaluation under the signed study manifest; and N_admitted,b, actual admissions in arm b. Primary success rates use the same fixed N_pair in both arms, not only admitted or completed tasks. Model fit, queue rejection, paid-cap exhaustion and outages are outcomes, not post hoc exclusions. Permission to enter both arms does not require that a compatible remote GPU exists. Tasks prohibited from paired evaluation are reported with reason and arm-specific coverage, never exported merely for comparability. This estimand is limited to the declared paired population; report N_pair/N_requested so selective eligibility is visible.
reasoning_steps.title: 3. Parent-task registry and denominators

reasoning_steps.argument: For parent i in arm b define Y_ib=1 only if the final artifact satisfies its frozen quality rubric, required provenance record, authorized processing and end-to-end deadline; otherwise Y_ib=0. Proposed deadlines for approval are coding 120 seconds, routine analysis 5 minutes, demanding scientific reasoning 30 minutes, multimodal/long-context work 15 minutes, agentic workflows 60 minutes and reproducible batches 24 hours. They are illustrative service targets, not measurements or university policy. Sensitive-data tasks inherit their functional deadline and stricter domain restrictions. Coding requires registered tests and critical-correctness checks; analysis requires domain-specific numerical checks; scientific reasoning requires expert assessment of the substantive conclusion and evidence; multimodal work requires task-specific references; agents must meet the objective without unauthorized actions; reproducible batches require a registered rerun/tolerance criterion. Faculty and students must approve explicit pass rules and critical-failure criteria before enrollment. Two blinded assessors score artifacts independently, with a third adjudicator resolving disagreement; report agreement and ambiguous judgments. Latency starts at submission to the assigned workflow and includes approval handling, queueing, cold starts, tools, retries and recovery, ending at delivery of the completed artifact, not the first streamed token. Later human grading does not extend delivery latency. Required provenance includes available model/version, configuration, prompts, tools and retrieval snapshots; a version label alone does not establish reproducibility.
reasoning_steps.title: 4. Define success before viewing results

reasoning_steps.argument: Each primary parent receives one G execution and one F execution with the same input and rubric. Randomize execution order within campus, task class, policy class and load block using a preregistered seed. Prevent answer sharing and shared cross-arm caches. Use isolated capacity slices with identical registered background arrivals, or separate matched replay windows; do not let duplicate study calls compete in one queue and then claim ordinary-service latency. Include declared peak, cold-start and maintenance conditions rather than reporting only warmed idle service. Lock model and workflow versions where possible and record changes. Repeats assess reproducibility separately and do not enlarge N_pair. Budget rejection, timeout, provider rejection, post-dispatch cancellation and non-delivery by the deadline remain failures in the primary requested-service analysis. Pre-dispatch withdrawal after enrollment remains in that denominator, with a separate withdrawal analysis; do not replace difficult tasks selectively. Missing required grading/provenance records count as not demonstrated successful in the primary analysis, accompanied by best/worst-case sensitivity. End enrollment sufficiently early for the longest deadline and grading before day 90. An early safety stop ends the efficacy claim as inconclusive; it does not justify analyzing only favorable completed pairs.
reasoning_steps.title: 5. Pairing, load, stopping and missing outcomes

reasoning_steps.argument: Within the frozen primary population let p10=P(Y_F=1,Y_G=0), p01=P(Y_F=0,Y_G=1), q=p10+p01 and Δ=E(Y_F−Y_G)=p10−p01. Thus Δ=0.10 means ten additional useful, on-time completions per 100 eligible parent tasks, net of tasks harmed by federation; it is neither a 10% relative increase nor a token-throughput gain. With n pairs and counts n10,n01, estimate Δ by (n10−n01)/n. Let D=Y_F−Y_G, taking values −1,0,1. Since D²=1 exactly on discordant pairs, E(D²)=q and Var(D)=q−Δ². For independent pairs, Var(mean D)=(q−Δ²)/n. This derivation explains why uncertainty depends on discordance rather than on two independent-arm binomial variances. Both-concordant outcomes still belong in n.
reasoning_steps.title: 6. The paired estimand and its variance

reasoning_steps.argument: For the single primary stratum use α=0.05. Obtain a two-sided Clopper–Pearson binomial interval [L10,U10] for n10 out of n with confidence 1−α/2, and independently calculate [L01,U01] at the same confidence level. Each marginal count is binomial under independent identically sampled pairs; the two counts need not be independent. The union bound gives joint coverage at least 1−α. Therefore [max(−1,L10−U01), min(1,U10−L01)] covers Δ with probability at least 0.95. Compute each binomial interval by inverting the binomial tails, with lower endpoint zero for zero successes and upper endpoint one for n successes. These endpoint conventions handle all-concordant and boundary samples; n=0 yields no inference. This procedure uses the paired discordance categories and is conservative. A sign/McNemar test alone is not the decision procedure because testing Δ=0 does not supply evidence that Δ exceeds 0.10. Do not substitute a zero-width Wald interval when no discordances occur.
reasoning_steps.title: 7. Prespecified paired uncertainty procedure

reasoning_steps.argument: For planning only, set true Δ=0.10 and hypothetical q values 0.20, 0.40 and 0.60. These imply valid (p10,p01) values (0.15,0.05), (0.25,0.15) and (0.35,0.25). The efficient large-sample paired-normal half-width is approximately 1.96 sqrt((q−0.01)/n). At n=30 these are about 0.156, 0.223 and 0.275; at n=400 they are about 0.043, 0.061 and 0.075. To target half-width 0.05, this approximation gives n≥ceil(1.96²(q−0.01)/0.05²), namely 292, 600 and 907 pairs. These are optimistic reference calculations, not the sample requirements of the conservative primary interval. For that interval, away from boundaries its approximate half-width is 2.2414[ sqrt(p10(1−p10))+sqrt(p01(1−p01)) ]/sqrt(n), because each marginal interval has 97.5% confidence. This gives roughly 665, 1,255 and 1,665 pairs for half-width 0.05 in the three scenarios. Values are hand-evaluated approximations; binomial discreteness and finite-sample corrections require exact evaluation before enrollment. None is a measured discordance rate, power result or guarantee.
reasoning_steps.title: 8. Explicitly hypothetical precision scenarios

reasoning_steps.argument: If the true Δ equals 0.10, a valid 95% interval can put its lower endpoint above 0.10 only on a coverage failure, with probability at most 0.05 under the stated model. No sample-size increase gives 80% power to establish a strict improvement beyond a margin when truth lies exactly on that margin. Power planning must posit a larger benefit. For illustration, under true Δ=0.20 and hypothetical q=0.40, p10=0.30, p01=0.10 and Var(D)=0.36. A normal approximation to the actual conservative gate gives n approximately [(2.2414(sqrt(0.21)+sqrt(0.09))+0.84 sqrt(0.36))/(0.20−0.10)]², about 486 pairs for 80% power. This is not exact. The exact planning calculation sums the multinomial probabilities for (n10,n01,n−n10−n01), with probabilities p10,p01,1−q, over count combinations whose interval lower bound exceeds 0.10. That finite calculation, plus affordability and dependence checks, must be completed before a fixed N is signed. A provisional planning envelope is up to 1,700 primary pairs to explore five-point precision in these scenarios; it is not a promise that the 90-day budget or capacity can support them. If the affordable N is smaller, register the attainable precision and allow an explicitly inconclusive pilot rather than weaken the gate after observation.
reasoning_steps.title: 9. Precision is not power to exceed the margin

reasoning_steps.argument: Many prompts from one researcher, templates, repeat executions and tasks exposed to the same outage are not independent new evidence. Before collection, define workload blocks and researcher/template clusters; seek distinct parent objectives rather than many variants of one prompt. The exact binomial procedure is confirmatory only if the independent-pair sampling model is defensible for the stated population. Otherwise use a prespecified independent-block analysis: for each block form its average paired difference X_j in [−1,1], retain equal block weights as the target estimand, and use the finite-sample interval mean(X) ± sqrt(2 log(2/α)/m), clipped to [−1,1], for m independent blocks. Hoeffding's inequality gives coverage at least 1−α because each block average has range two. This changes the estimand to the average block effect and must be declared, not silently substituted for task weighting. For m=30 and α=0.05 the half-width is about 0.496; about 2,952 independent blocks are sufficient for half-width at most 0.05 under this conservative bound. If even block independence is unsupported, report finite-window paired differences descriptively without a population confidence claim. Controlled replay and live-service results remain separate: neither proves the other's generality.
reasoning_steps.title: 10. Dependence and limits of population inference

reasoning_steps.argument: Before outcome collection choose one primary underserved campus/task/policy population from inventory and expressed research needs, not observed federation wins. For mutually exclusive task classes, assign the principal deliverable before routing; sensitive status, campus and interactive/batch status are additional registered tags. Report all requested task categories, including those with no lawful paired sample. The primary comparison uses its single 95% interval. Secondary strata are descriptive unless a confirmatory family of K strata is signed in advance; for simultaneous family coverage use the same interval construction with α/K per stratum. An exploratory successful subgroup cannot replace a failed primary population. Provisional bounded-scope go requires the primary lower bound >0.10, at least 80% observed useful/on-time success in the supported primary stratum, the service and safety gates, and campus-approved incremental and fully loaded administrative-cost ceilings. Report uncertainty around absolute success and availability as well; these observed operational gates are not population guarantees. If the upper bound is ≤0.10, the registered >10-point benefit criterion is not met; if the interval crosses 0.10, data are missing, or independent sample size is inadequate, classify efficacy as inconclusive. An upper bound below zero supports harm in that population. Any authorization or accounting violation triggers immediate remote-routing suspension regardless of efficacy. For both no-go and inconclusive outcomes retain G as the default, without claiming federation is universally inferior. No efficacy peeking or optional stopping; continuous safety monitoring is mandatory.
reasoning_steps.title: 11. Strata, multiplicity and the three-way decision

reasoning_steps.argument: Evaluate fairness separately within compatible GPU/model/memory pools and registered interactive/batch capacity partitions; raw tokens across heterogeneous models are not comparable service units. Computing records charged GPU-seconds, estimation errors, backlog, fit, weights and home-campus quotas. Integrate a frozen hierarchical weighted, demand-limited reference allocation over time: department entitlement first, project within department, user within project. Only policy-eligible, funded, compatible backlog earns entitlement, using the declared capacity offered to that service; do not erase outages or maintenance from the accompanying availability denominator. Measure actual service S and reference entitlement E, including boundary-crossing jobs and scheduler deficits. Evaluate rolling seven-calendar-day windows daily only when they contain at least 40 declared service hours, compatible available-service time at least ten times the maximum permitted non-preemptive blocking time, and E at least 100 maximum scheduling quanta for the tenant under review. Otherwise extend to 14 and then 28 days; if still insufficient, label fairness unassessed rather than passed. These are proposed diagnostic windows, not WDRR guarantees. Flag S/E<0.80 for investigation, report every deadline violation and maximum no-service backlog age, and inspect daily so a weekly average cannot hide interactive starvation. If blocking or work size cannot be bounded, do not claim a positive waiting-time guarantee. Also report policy-ineligible, unfunded and unfit demand separately; excluding it from share fairness must not conceal lack of useful access.
reasoning_steps.title: 12. Fairness denominator and observation window

reasoning_steps.argument: Days 1–15: computing inventories compatible GPU memory, model fit, queues and maintenance; security/legal define approved domains and classification; procurement/finance establish dated prices, liability bounds and reconciliation; faculty/students approve rubrics, deadlines and accessibility. Days 16–30: instrument both workflows, test public/synthetic tasks and the fault matrix, choose the primary population without outcome-based subgroup selection, evaluate exact sample-size scenarios and sign fixed N, analysis, budgets and administrative ceilings. Days 31–60: measure local-only, approved-API-only and G descriptively under their lawful scopes, and prepare approved federation capacity. Earlier G observations are not substitutes for contemporaneous primary pairs. Days 61–90: conduct the registered F/G paired comparison only if approvals and fault gates pass, ending enrollment before all deadlines and grading must close. Computing owns latency, throughput, availability and fairness; faculty own blinded quality; security owns egress/retention checks; finance owns settled charges and held liabilities; service management logs staff hours, agreements and incidents. Proposed operational gates retain at least 99% observed availability during declared service hours, with maintenance additionally counted against the full requested window, and zero observed unauthorized transmissions or cap violations. Test stale policy, malicious identities, WAN/home/remote/provider outages, charged timeouts, cancellation, concurrent reservations and prohibited fallback. Zero observed failures remains bounded evidence, not a safety proof. Funding must cover both executions and all child calls; study duplication is separately attributed and not hidden in ordinary cost-per-task. Zero paid budget permits no positive-charge admission, even to reach a sample-size target.

reasoning_steps.title: 14. Cost, peer evidence and source verification remain separate gates

artifacts.method: Hypothesis: adding an approved cooperative federation to a campus gateway with separately approved external access increases useful, on-time parent-task completion by more than 10 percentage points in one preregistered underserved population without violating home-campus authority or exceeding approved costs. Compare G, the gateway-plus-separate-access baseline, with F, the same service plus hypothetical federation. Use paired parent tasks, matched entitlements and load conditions, blinded quality adjudication, an exact conservative interval based on paired discordance counts, and a fixed final analysis. A discriminating positive outcome is a lower confidence bound above 0.10 plus all operational gates; an interval crossing 0.10 is inconclusive, not equivalence. Derive precision scenarios by hand, with hypothetical discordance probabilities rather than invented traces. Statistical coverage assumes independent, identically sampled parent-task pairs within the declared target stratum; shared researchers, templates, queues or outages can invalidate that assumption and require the cluster procedure described below. Neither external access nor a runtime is available; no experiment or source verification occurred.
artifacts.next_question: Without runtime or external access, derive a conservative fixed-sample sufficient bound for achieving at least 80% power under the explicitly hypothetical alternative Δ=0.20, q=0.40 using the actual conservative confidence-bound gate L>0.10, or clearly bound that gate by an analytically tractable sufficient event. State the independent sampling unit and a pre-enrollment rule for underpowered or unaffordable designs; express resource feasibility symbolically without inventing prices or campus capacity. Preserve source verification, approvals and empirical results as pending.

argument_steps.title: 1. Evidence boundary and changes from the previous proposal

argument_steps.argument: G provides campus-local inference through the gateway and a separately approved external workflow; F adds approved remote-campus execution. Federation and frontier routing remain hypothetical extensions, not asserted MindRouter features. Both arms use identical home-campus classification, identity, retention, audit and destination rules, local resource allocations, paid-access entitlements and parent-task spending limits. F receives the declared additional remote capacity, whose operating and agreement costs are counted rather than treated as free. Separate external access must still have complete financial mediation if the earlier hard-cap argument is invoked. Approval alone is insufficient. No outage, model mismatch, better score, cancellation or budget exhaustion authorizes a new destination. Ambiguous classification fails closed. Revalidate policy and reserve funds before every billable subcall; retain unresolved liabilities. Public or synthetic tasks are used until all relevant campuses approve real-data processing.

review.rationale: As a proposed comparison, matching non-federation entitlements isolates the addition of remote capacity. Explicit financial mediation and policy-first eligibility avoid treating approval or failure as sufficient authorization.

argument_steps.title: 2. Arms, policy boundaries and comparable resources

argument_steps.argument: A parent task is one registered research objective with an input snapshot, requested output, rubric, deadline, policy classification, provenance requirements and total resource envelope. Agent calls, tools, retries and reproducibility repeats are children, not additional tasks. Before routing, register every submitted parent task and distinguish: N_requested, all requests; N_authorized, requests with adequate classification and home-campus permission for at least one studied path; N_pair, authorized tasks permitted to undergo both G and F evaluation under the signed study manifest; and N_admitted,b, actual admissions in arm b. Primary success rates use the same fixed N_pair in both arms, not only admitted or completed tasks. Model fit, queue rejection, paid-cap exhaustion and outages are outcomes, not post hoc exclusions. Permission to enter both arms does not require that a compatible remote GPU exists. Tasks prohibited from paired evaluation are reported with reason and arm-specific coverage, never exported merely for comparability. This estimand is limited to the declared paired population; report N_pair/N_requested so selective eligibility is visible.

review.rationale: A common preregistered paired denominator prevents admission and completion filtering from inflating arm success. Reporting requested, authorized, paired and admitted counts exposes eligibility selection and limits the estimand's scope.

argument_steps.title: 3. Parent-task registry and denominators

argument_steps.argument: For parent i in arm b define Y_ib=1 only if the final artifact satisfies its frozen quality rubric, required provenance record, authorized processing and end-to-end deadline; otherwise Y_ib=0. Proposed deadlines for approval are coding 120 seconds, routine analysis 5 minutes, demanding scientific reasoning 30 minutes, multimodal/long-context work 15 minutes, agentic workflows 60 minutes and reproducible batches 24 hours. They are illustrative service targets, not measurements or university policy. Sensitive-data tasks inherit their functional deadline and stricter domain restrictions. Coding requires registered tests and critical-correctness checks; analysis requires domain-specific numerical checks; scientific reasoning requires expert assessment of the substantive conclusion and evidence; multimodal work requires task-specific references; agents must meet the objective without unauthorized actions; reproducible batches require a registered rerun/tolerance criterion. Faculty and students must approve explicit pass rules and critical-failure criteria before enrollment. Two blinded assessors score artifacts independently, with a third adjudicator resolving disagreement; report agreement and ambiguous judgments. Latency starts at submission to the assigned workflow and includes approval handling, queueing, cold starts, tools, retries and recovery, ending at delivery of the completed artifact, not the first streamed token. Later human grading does not extend delivery latency. Required provenance includes available model/version, configuration, prompts, tools and retrieval snapshots; a version label alone does not establish reproducibility.

review.rationale: Success is conjunctive in quality, provenance, authorization and delivery deadline. End-to-end latency includes workflow delays rather than only generation time. The numerical deadlines and incomplete pass rules are correctly presented as proposals awaiting approval.

argument_steps.title: 4. Define success before viewing results

argument_steps.argument: Each primary parent receives one G execution and one F execution with the same input and rubric. Randomize execution order within campus, task class, policy class and load block using a preregistered seed. Prevent answer sharing and shared cross-arm caches. Use isolated capacity slices with identical registered background arrivals, or separate matched replay windows; do not let duplicate study calls compete in one queue and then claim ordinary-service latency. Include declared peak, cold-start and maintenance conditions rather than reporting only warmed idle service. Lock model and workflow versions where possible and record changes. Repeats assess reproducibility separately and do not enlarge N_pair. Budget rejection, timeout, provider rejection, post-dispatch cancellation and non-delivery by the deadline remain failures in the primary requested-service analysis. Pre-dispatch withdrawal after enrollment remains in that denominator, with a separate withdrawal analysis; do not replace difficult tasks selectively. Missing required grading/provenance records count as not demonstrated successful in the primary analysis, accompanied by best/worst-case sensitivity. End enrollment sufficiently early for the longest deadline and grading before day 90. An early safety stop ends the efficacy claim as inconclusive; it does not justify analyzing only favorable completed pairs.

review.rationale: The pairing, cache isolation and matched-load requirements address leakage and interference. Keeping rejection, non-delivery and missing required evidence in the primary denominator prevents favorable complete-case selection. These remain proposed controls, not demonstrated execution fidelity.

argument_steps.title: 5. Pairing, load, stopping and missing outcomes

argument_steps.argument: Within the frozen primary population let p10=P(Y_F=1,Y_G=0), p01=P(Y_F=0,Y_G=1), q=p10+p01 and Δ=E(Y_F−Y_G)=p10−p01. Thus Δ=0.10 means ten additional useful, on-time completions per 100 eligible parent tasks, net of tasks harmed by federation; it is neither a 10% relative increase nor a token-throughput gain. With n pairs and counts n10,n01, estimate Δ by (n10−n01)/n. Let D=Y_F−Y_G, taking values −1,0,1. Since D²=1 exactly on discordant pairs, E(D²)=q and Var(D)=q−Δ². For independent pairs, Var(mean D)=(q−Δ²)/n. This derivation explains why uncertainty depends on discordance rather than on two independent-arm binomial variances. Both-concordant outcomes still belong in n.

review.rationale: D takes values −1, 0 and 1, so E(D²)=p10+p01=q and Var(D)=q−Δ². Dividing by n is justified for independent identically sampled pairs, not arbitrary live-service observations.

argument_steps.title: 6. The paired estimand and its variance

argument_steps.argument: For the single primary stratum use α=0.05. Obtain a two-sided Clopper–Pearson binomial interval [L10,U10] for n10 out of n with confidence 1−α/2, and independently calculate [L01,U01] at the same confidence level. Each marginal count is binomial under independent identically sampled pairs; the two counts need not be independent. The union bound gives joint coverage at least 1−α. Therefore [max(−1,L10−U01), min(1,U10−L01)] covers Δ with probability at least 0.95. Compute each binomial interval by inverting the binomial tails, with lower endpoint zero for zero successes and upper endpoint one for n successes. These endpoint conventions handle all-concordant and boundary samples; n=0 yields no inference. This procedure uses the paired discordance categories and is conservative. A sign/McNemar test alone is not the decision procedure because testing Δ=0 does not supply evidence that Δ exceeds 0.10. Do not substitute a zero-width Wald interval when no discordances occur.

review.rationale: Each discordance count has a binomial marginal under the stated model. Two intervals with failure probability α/2 each have joint coverage at least 1−α by the union bound, regardless of their dependence; subtracting endpoints therefore gives valid conservative coverage for Δ.

argument_steps.title: 7. Prespecified paired uncertainty procedure

argument_steps.argument: For planning only, set true Δ=0.10 and hypothetical q values 0.20, 0.40 and 0.60. These imply valid (p10,p01) values (0.15,0.05), (0.25,0.15) and (0.35,0.25). The efficient large-sample paired-normal half-width is approximately 1.96 sqrt((q−0.01)/n). At n=30 these are about 0.156, 0.223 and 0.275; at n=400 they are about 0.043, 0.061 and 0.075. To target half-width 0.05, this approximation gives n≥ceil(1.96²(q−0.01)/0.05²), namely 292, 600 and 907 pairs. These are optimistic reference calculations, not the sample requirements of the conservative primary interval. For that interval, away from boundaries its approximate half-width is 2.2414[ sqrt(p10(1−p10))+sqrt(p01(1−p01)) ]/sqrt(n), because each marginal interval has 97.5% confidence. This gives roughly 665, 1,255 and 1,665 pairs for half-width 0.05 in the three scenarios. Values are hand-evaluated approximations; binomial discreteness and finite-sample corrections require exact evaluation before enrollment. None is a measured discordance rate, power result or guarantee.

review.rationale: The proposed probabilities are valid and have Δ=0.10. Substitution into the variance and normal-width formulas reproduces the reported rounded values and approximate sample sizes. The text properly separates these hand approximations from exact interval requirements and measured discordance.

argument_steps.title: 8. Explicitly hypothetical precision scenarios

argument_steps.argument: If the true Δ equals 0.10, a valid 95% interval can put its lower endpoint above 0.10 only on a coverage failure, with probability at most 0.05 under the stated model. No sample-size increase gives 80% power to establish a strict improvement beyond a margin when truth lies exactly on that margin. Power planning must posit a larger benefit. For illustration, under true Δ=0.20 and hypothetical q=0.40, p10=0.30, p01=0.10 and Var(D)=0.36. A normal approximation to the actual conservative gate gives n approximately [(2.2414(sqrt(0.21)+sqrt(0.09))+0.84 sqrt(0.36))/(0.20−0.10)]², about 486 pairs for 80% power. This is not exact. The exact planning calculation sums the multinomial probabilities for (n10,n01,n−n10−n01), with probabilities p10,p01,1−q, over count combinations whose interval lower bound exceeds 0.10. That finite calculation, plus affordability and dependence checks, must be completed before a fixed N is signed. A provisional planning envelope is up to 1,700 primary pairs to explore five-point precision in these scenarios; it is not a promise that the 90-day budget or capacity can support them. If the affordable N is smaller, register the attainable precision and allow an explicitly inconclusive pilot rather than weaken the gate after observation.

review.objection: The inference is valid as an approximation and planning method, but the actual gate's power and an affordable fixed N remain unresolved; this step does not make the protocol enrollment-ready.
review.rationale: At truth Δ=0.10, a lower confidence bound above 0.10 entails noncoverage, so high power at the boundary is impossible for a valid interval. The alternative probabilities and approximate 486-pair calculation are internally consistent, and multinomial summation describes the exact gate-power calculation.

argument_steps.title: 9. Precision is not power to exceed the margin

argument_steps.argument: Many prompts from one researcher, templates, repeat executions and tasks exposed to the same outage are not independent new evidence. Before collection, define workload blocks and researcher/template clusters; seek distinct parent objectives rather than many variants of one prompt. The exact binomial procedure is confirmatory only if the independent-pair sampling model is defensible for the stated population. Otherwise use a prespecified independent-block analysis: for each block form its average paired difference X_j in [−1,1], retain equal block weights as the target estimand, and use the finite-sample interval mean(X) ± sqrt(2 log(2/α)/m), clipped to [−1,1], for m independent blocks. Hoeffding's inequality gives coverage at least 1−α because each block average has range two. This changes the estimand to the average block effect and must be declared, not silently substituted for task weighting. For m=30 and α=0.05 the half-width is about 0.496; about 2,952 independent blocks are sufficient for half-width at most 0.05 under this conservative bound. If even block independence is unsupported, report finite-window paired differences descriptively without a population confidence claim. Controlled replay and live-service results remain separate: neither proves the other's generality.

review.rationale: For independent block averages in [−1,1], Hoeffding gives radius sqrt(2 log(2/α)/m). The stated approximately 0.496 radius and 2,952-block sufficient count follow. The change to equal-block weighting and the absence of inference without defensible independence are explicit.

argument_steps.title: 10. Dependence and limits of population inference

argument_steps.argument: Before outcome collection choose one primary underserved campus/task/policy population from inventory and expressed research needs, not observed federation wins. For mutually exclusive task classes, assign the principal deliverable before routing; sensitive status, campus and interactive/batch status are additional registered tags. Report all requested task categories, including those with no lawful paired sample. The primary comparison uses its single 95% interval. Secondary strata are descriptive unless a confirmatory family of K strata is signed in advance; for simultaneous family coverage use the same interval construction with α/K per stratum. An exploratory successful subgroup cannot replace a failed primary population. Provisional bounded-scope go requires the primary lower bound >0.10, at least 80% observed useful/on-time success in the supported primary stratum, the service and safety gates, and campus-approved incremental and fully loaded administrative-cost ceilings. Report uncertainty around absolute success and availability as well; these observed operational gates are not population guarantees. If the upper bound is ≤0.10, the registered >10-point benefit criterion is not met; if the interval crosses 0.10, data are missing, or independent sample size is inadequate, classify efficacy as inconclusive. An upper bound below zero supports harm in that population. Any authorization or accounting violation triggers immediate remote-routing suspension regardless of efficacy. For both no-go and inconclusive outcomes retain G as the default, without claiming federation is universally inferior. No efficacy peeking or optional stopping; continuous safety monitoring is mandatory.

review.rationale: Preregistering one primary population prevents subgroup replacement. Using α/K yields simultaneous coverage by a further union bound. The three-way decision separates demonstrated margin benefit, failure to meet that criterion and inconclusive evidence; observed operational gates are not promoted to population guarantees.

argument_steps.title: 14. Cost, peer evidence and source verification remain separate gates

objective_review.argument_summary: For paired outcomes D=Y_F−Y_G, D² indicates discordance, giving Δ=p10−p01 and Var(D)=q−Δ². Marginal binomial intervals for the two discordance probabilities, combined by a union bound, yield a conservative interval for Δ without assuming independence between discordance counts. Requiring its lower endpoint to exceed 0.10 is stronger than requiring an interval to exclude zero. The planning examples demonstrate the weakness of 30-pair precision, while the independent-block Hoeffding interval exposes the cost of weaker dependence assumptions. Parent-task denominators, missing-outcome rules, contemporaneous pairing and bounded fairness windows improve the design, but final sample feasibility and operational approvals remain open.
assumptions: Probability coverage and independent-pair planning require independent, identically sampled paired parent tasks within the declared population; correlated live workloads are not automatically covered.
The block interval requires independent bounded block averages and targets an equal-block effect, not an automatically equivalent task-weighted effect.
Interpretability requires faithful arm execution, matched non-federation entitlements, fixed parent tasks, blinded adjudication, complete accounting and no cross-arm leakage.
Discordance rates, deadlines, operational thresholds and the planning envelope are hypothetical proposed inputs, not measured values or university policy.
objective_review.claim: The proposed paired pilot distinguishes an any-benefit decision from a greater-than-10-percentage-point decision, and the supplied hand calculations show that 30 pairs do not provide five-percentage-point precision in the illustrative scenarios. The study specification does not establish federation benefit, deployment safety or affordable useful campus access.
