reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied bounded extract of cc14dcfd-f2c0-41f7-92f4-768a1511e7f2 was reviewed, not its saved original. It contains a conditional reservation argument, counterexamples to releasing ambiguous liabilities and to unconditional WDRR latency guarantees, and an underspecified pilot. Preserve those negative constraints: do not release a hold merely after timeout/cancellation, and do not infer starvation freedom from scheduling weights. Replace its exploratory target of 30 tasks per stratum and its point-estimate-at-least-10-points/interval-excluding-zero gate with the stronger confidence-bound gate below. This is a deliberate tightening, not an interpretation that the earlier gate already established a true benefit exceeding 10 points. All recorded source, approval, implementation, cost and empirical obligations remain unresolved.

review.rationale: The supplied cycle-1 extract contains the stated reservation and scheduling examples. The current proposal explicitly tightens, rather than retrospectively reinterprets, the earlier federation gate and preserves its open requirements.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Evidence boundary and changes from the previous proposal

reasoning_steps.argument: G provides campus-local inference through the gateway and a separately approved external workflow; F adds approved remote-campus execution. Federation and frontier routing remain hypothetical extensions, not asserted MindRouter features. Both arms use identical home-campus classification, identity, retention, audit and destination rules, local resource allocations, paid-access entitlements and parent-task spending limits. F receives the declared additional remote capacity, whose operating and agreement costs are counted rather than treated as free. Separate external access must still have complete financial mediation if the earlier hard-cap argument is invoked. Approval alone is insufficient. No outage, model mismatch, better score, cancellation or budget exhaustion authorizes a new destination. Ambiguous classification fails closed. Revalidate policy and reserve funds before every billable subcall; retain unresolved liabilities. Public or synthetic tasks are used until all relevant campuses approve real-data processing.

review.rationale: As a proposed comparison, matching non-federation entitlements isolates the addition of remote capacity. Explicit financial mediation and policy-first eligibility avoid treating approval or failure as sufficient authorization.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Arms, policy boundaries and comparable resources

reasoning_steps.argument: A parent task is one registered research objective with an input snapshot, requested output, rubric, deadline, policy classification, provenance requirements and total resource envelope. Agent calls, tools, retries and reproducibility repeats are children, not additional tasks. Before routing, register every submitted parent task and distinguish: N_requested, all requests; N_authorized, requests with adequate classification and home-campus permission for at least one studied path; N_pair, authorized tasks permitted to undergo both G and F evaluation under the signed study manifest; and N_admitted,b, actual admissions in arm b. Primary success rates use the same fixed N_pair in both arms, not only admitted or completed tasks. Model fit, queue rejection, paid-cap exhaustion and outages are outcomes, not post hoc exclusions. Permission to enter both arms does not require that a compatible remote GPU exists. Tasks prohibited from paired evaluation are reported with reason and arm-specific coverage, never exported merely for comparability. This estimand is limited to the declared paired population; report N_pair/N_requested so selective eligibility is visible.

review.rationale: A common preregistered paired denominator prevents admission and completion filtering from inflating arm success. Reporting requested, authorized, paired and admitted counts exposes eligibility selection and limits the estimand's scope.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Parent-task registry and denominators

reasoning_steps.argument: For parent i in arm b define Y_ib=1 only if the final artifact satisfies its frozen quality rubric, required provenance record, authorized processing and end-to-end deadline; otherwise Y_ib=0. Proposed deadlines for approval are coding 120 seconds, routine analysis 5 minutes, demanding scientific reasoning 30 minutes, multimodal/long-context work 15 minutes, agentic workflows 60 minutes and reproducible batches 24 hours. They are illustrative service targets, not measurements or university policy. Sensitive-data tasks inherit their functional deadline and stricter domain restrictions. Coding requires registered tests and critical-correctness checks; analysis requires domain-specific numerical checks; scientific reasoning requires expert assessment of the substantive conclusion and evidence; multimodal work requires task-specific references; agents must meet the objective without unauthorized actions; reproducible batches require a registered rerun/tolerance criterion. Faculty and students must approve explicit pass rules and critical-failure criteria before enrollment. Two blinded assessors score artifacts independently, with a third adjudicator resolving disagreement; report agreement and ambiguous judgments. Latency starts at submission to the assigned workflow and includes approval handling, queueing, cold starts, tools, retries and recovery, ending at delivery of the completed artifact, not the first streamed token. Later human grading does not extend delivery latency. Required provenance includes available model/version, configuration, prompts, tools and retrieval snapshots; a version label alone does not establish reproducibility.

review.rationale: Success is conjunctive in quality, provenance, authorization and delivery deadline. End-to-end latency includes workflow delays rather than only generation time. The numerical deadlines and incomplete pass rules are correctly presented as proposals awaiting approval.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Define success before viewing results

reasoning_steps.argument: Each primary parent receives one G execution and one F execution with the same input and rubric. Randomize execution order within campus, task class, policy class and load block using a preregistered seed. Prevent answer sharing and shared cross-arm caches. Use isolated capacity slices with identical registered background arrivals, or separate matched replay windows; do not let duplicate study calls compete in one queue and then claim ordinary-service latency. Include declared peak, cold-start and maintenance conditions rather than reporting only warmed idle service. Lock model and workflow versions where possible and record changes. Repeats assess reproducibility separately and do not enlarge N_pair. Budget rejection, timeout, provider rejection, post-dispatch cancellation and non-delivery by the deadline remain failures in the primary requested-service analysis. Pre-dispatch withdrawal after enrollment remains in that denominator, with a separate withdrawal analysis; do not replace difficult tasks selectively. Missing required grading/provenance records count as not demonstrated successful in the primary analysis, accompanied by best/worst-case sensitivity. End enrollment sufficiently early for the longest deadline and grading before day 90. An early safety stop ends the efficacy claim as inconclusive; it does not justify analyzing only favorable completed pairs.

review.rationale: The pairing, cache isolation and matched-load requirements address leakage and interference. Keeping rejection, non-delivery and missing required evidence in the primary denominator prevents favorable complete-case selection. These remain proposed controls, not demonstrated execution fidelity.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Pairing, load, stopping and missing outcomes

reasoning_steps.argument: Within the frozen primary population let p10=P(Y_F=1,Y_G=0), p01=P(Y_F=0,Y_G=1), q=p10+p01 and Δ=E(Y_F−Y_G)=p10−p01. Thus Δ=0.10 means ten additional useful, on-time completions per 100 eligible parent tasks, net of tasks harmed by federation; it is neither a 10% relative increase nor a token-throughput gain. With n pairs and counts n10,n01, estimate Δ by (n10−n01)/n. Let D=Y_F−Y_G, taking values −1,0,1. Since D²=1 exactly on discordant pairs, E(D²)=q and Var(D)=q−Δ². For independent pairs, Var(mean D)=(q−Δ²)/n. This derivation explains why uncertainty depends on discordance rather than on two independent-arm binomial variances. Both-concordant outcomes still belong in n.

review.rationale: D takes values −1, 0 and 1, so E(D²)=p10+p01=q and Var(D)=q−Δ². Dividing by n is justified for independent identically sampled pairs, not arbitrary live-service observations.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. The paired estimand and its variance

reasoning_steps.argument: For the single primary stratum use α=0.05. Obtain a two-sided Clopper–Pearson binomial interval [L10,U10] for n10 out of n with confidence 1−α/2, and independently calculate [L01,U01] at the same confidence level. Each marginal count is binomial under independent identically sampled pairs; the two counts need not be independent. The union bound gives joint coverage at least 1−α. Therefore [max(−1,L10−U01), min(1,U10−L01)] covers Δ with probability at least 0.95. Compute each binomial interval by inverting the binomial tails, with lower endpoint zero for zero successes and upper endpoint one for n successes. These endpoint conventions handle all-concordant and boundary samples; n=0 yields no inference. This procedure uses the paired discordance categories and is conservative. A sign/McNemar test alone is not the decision procedure because testing Δ=0 does not supply evidence that Δ exceeds 0.10. Do not substitute a zero-width Wald interval when no discordances occur.

review.rationale: Each discordance count has a binomial marginal under the stated model. Two intervals with failure probability α/2 each have joint coverage at least 1−α by the union bound, regardless of their dependence; subtracting endpoints therefore gives valid conservative coverage for Δ.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Prespecified paired uncertainty procedure

reasoning_steps.argument: For planning only, set true Δ=0.10 and hypothetical q values 0.20, 0.40 and 0.60. These imply valid (p10,p01) values (0.15,0.05), (0.25,0.15) and (0.35,0.25). The efficient large-sample paired-normal half-width is approximately 1.96 sqrt((q−0.01)/n). At n=30 these are about 0.156, 0.223 and 0.275; at n=400 they are about 0.043, 0.061 and 0.075. To target half-width 0.05, this approximation gives n≥ceil(1.96²(q−0.01)/0.05²), namely 292, 600 and 907 pairs. These are optimistic reference calculations, not the sample requirements of the conservative primary interval. For that interval, away from boundaries its approximate half-width is 2.2414[ sqrt(p10(1−p10))+sqrt(p01(1−p01)) ]/sqrt(n), because each marginal interval has 97.5% confidence. This gives roughly 665, 1,255 and 1,665 pairs for half-width 0.05 in the three scenarios. Values are hand-evaluated approximations; binomial discreteness and finite-sample corrections require exact evaluation before enrollment. None is a measured discordance rate, power result or guarantee.

review.rationale: The proposed probabilities are valid and have Δ=0.10. Substitution into the variance and normal-width formulas reproduces the reported rounded values and approximate sample sizes. The text properly separates these hand approximations from exact interval requirements and measured discordance.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Explicitly hypothetical precision scenarios

reasoning_steps.argument: If the true Δ equals 0.10, a valid 95% interval can put its lower endpoint above 0.10 only on a coverage failure, with probability at most 0.05 under the stated model. No sample-size increase gives 80% power to establish a strict improvement beyond a margin when truth lies exactly on that margin. Power planning must posit a larger benefit. For illustration, under true Δ=0.20 and hypothetical q=0.40, p10=0.30, p01=0.10 and Var(D)=0.36. A normal approximation to the actual conservative gate gives n approximately [(2.2414(sqrt(0.21)+sqrt(0.09))+0.84 sqrt(0.36))/(0.20−0.10)]², about 486 pairs for 80% power. This is not exact. The exact planning calculation sums the multinomial probabilities for (n10,n01,n−n10−n01), with probabilities p10,p01,1−q, over count combinations whose interval lower bound exceeds 0.10. That finite calculation, plus affordability and dependence checks, must be completed before a fixed N is signed. A provisional planning envelope is up to 1,700 primary pairs to explore five-point precision in these scenarios; it is not a promise that the 90-day budget or capacity can support them. If the affordable N is smaller, register the attainable precision and allow an explicitly inconclusive pilot rather than weaken the gate after observation.

review.objection: The inference is valid as an approximation and planning method, but the actual gate's power and an affordable fixed N remain unresolved; this step does not make the protocol enrollment-ready.
review.rationale: At truth Δ=0.10, a lower confidence bound above 0.10 entails noncoverage, so high power at the boundary is impossible for a valid interval. The alternative probabilities and approximate 486-pair calculation are internally consistent, and multinomial summation describes the exact gate-power calculation.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Precision is not power to exceed the margin

reasoning_steps.argument: Many prompts from one researcher, templates, repeat executions and tasks exposed to the same outage are not independent new evidence. Before collection, define workload blocks and researcher/template clusters; seek distinct parent objectives rather than many variants of one prompt. The exact binomial procedure is confirmatory only if the independent-pair sampling model is defensible for the stated population. Otherwise use a prespecified independent-block analysis: for each block form its average paired difference X_j in [−1,1], retain equal block weights as the target estimand, and use the finite-sample interval mean(X) ± sqrt(2 log(2/α)/m), clipped to [−1,1], for m independent blocks. Hoeffding's inequality gives coverage at least 1−α because each block average has range two. This changes the estimand to the average block effect and must be declared, not silently substituted for task weighting. For m=30 and α=0.05 the half-width is about 0.496; about 2,952 independent blocks are sufficient for half-width at most 0.05 under this conservative bound. If even block independence is unsupported, report finite-window paired differences descriptively without a population confidence claim. Controlled replay and live-service results remain separate: neither proves the other's generality.

review.rationale: For independent block averages in [−1,1], Hoeffding gives radius sqrt(2 log(2/α)/m). The stated approximately 0.496 radius and 2,952-block sufficient count follow. The change to equal-block weighting and the absence of inference without defensible independence are explicit.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Dependence and limits of population inference

reasoning_steps.argument: Before outcome collection choose one primary underserved campus/task/policy population from inventory and expressed research needs, not observed federation wins. For mutually exclusive task classes, assign the principal deliverable before routing; sensitive status, campus and interactive/batch status are additional registered tags. Report all requested task categories, including those with no lawful paired sample. The primary comparison uses its single 95% interval. Secondary strata are descriptive unless a confirmatory family of K strata is signed in advance; for simultaneous family coverage use the same interval construction with α/K per stratum. An exploratory successful subgroup cannot replace a failed primary population. Provisional bounded-scope go requires the primary lower bound >0.10, at least 80% observed useful/on-time success in the supported primary stratum, the service and safety gates, and campus-approved incremental and fully loaded administrative-cost ceilings. Report uncertainty around absolute success and availability as well; these observed operational gates are not population guarantees. If the upper bound is ≤0.10, the registered >10-point benefit criterion is not met; if the interval crosses 0.10, data are missing, or independent sample size is inadequate, classify efficacy as inconclusive. An upper bound below zero supports harm in that population. Any authorization or accounting violation triggers immediate remote-routing suspension regardless of efficacy. For both no-go and inconclusive outcomes retain G as the default, without claiming federation is universally inferior. No efficacy peeking or optional stopping; continuous safety monitoring is mandatory.

review.rationale: Preregistering one primary population prevents subgroup replacement. Using α/K yields simultaneous coverage by a further union bound. The three-way decision separates demonstrated margin benefit, failure to meet that criterion and inconclusive evidence; observed operational gates are not promoted to population guarantees.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Strata, multiplicity and the three-way decision

reasoning_steps.argument: Evaluate fairness separately within compatible GPU/model/memory pools and registered interactive/batch capacity partitions; raw tokens across heterogeneous models are not comparable service units. Computing records charged GPU-seconds, estimation errors, backlog, fit, weights and home-campus quotas. Integrate a frozen hierarchical weighted, demand-limited reference allocation over time: department entitlement first, project within department, user within project. Only policy-eligible, funded, compatible backlog earns entitlement, using the declared capacity offered to that service; do not erase outages or maintenance from the accompanying availability denominator. Measure actual service S and reference entitlement E, including boundary-crossing jobs and scheduler deficits. Evaluate rolling seven-calendar-day windows daily only when they contain at least 40 declared service hours, compatible available-service time at least ten times the maximum permitted non-preemptive blocking time, and E at least 100 maximum scheduling quanta for the tenant under review. Otherwise extend to 14 and then 28 days; if still insufficient, label fairness unassessed rather than passed. These are proposed diagnostic windows, not WDRR guarantees. Flag S/E<0.80 for investigation, report every deadline violation and maximum no-service backlog age, and inspect daily so a weekly average cannot hide interactive starvation. If blocking or work size cannot be bounded, do not claim a positive waiting-time guarantee. Also report policy-ineligible, unfunded and unfit demand separately; excluding it from share fairness must not conceal lack of useful access.

review.rationale: Compatible-pool accounting avoids treating heterogeneous tokens as interchangeable service. Explicit minimum exposure, window extension and an unassessed outcome prevent unsupported fairness passes. Daily backlog diagnostics address failures that weekly averages could hide; the reference allocation still needs executable specification.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Fairness denominator and observation window

reasoning_steps.argument: Days 1–15: computing inventories compatible GPU memory, model fit, queues and maintenance; security/legal define approved domains and classification; procurement/finance establish dated prices, liability bounds and reconciliation; faculty/students approve rubrics, deadlines and accessibility. Days 16–30: instrument both workflows, test public/synthetic tasks and the fault matrix, choose the primary population without outcome-based subgroup selection, evaluate exact sample-size scenarios and sign fixed N, analysis, budgets and administrative ceilings. Days 31–60: measure local-only, approved-API-only and G descriptively under their lawful scopes, and prepare approved federation capacity. Earlier G observations are not substitutes for contemporaneous primary pairs. Days 61–90: conduct the registered F/G paired comparison only if approvals and fault gates pass, ending enrollment before all deadlines and grading must close. Computing owns latency, throughput, availability and fairness; faculty own blinded quality; security owns egress/retention checks; finance owns settled charges and held liabilities; service management logs staff hours, agreements and incidents. Proposed operational gates retain at least 99% observed availability during declared service hours, with maintenance additionally counted against the full requested window, and zero observed unauthorized transmissions or cap violations. Test stale policy, malicious identities, WAN/home/remote/provider outages, charged timeouts, cancellation, concurrent reservations and prohibited fallback. Zero observed failures remains bounded evidence, not a safety proof. Funding must cover both executions and all child calls; study duplication is separately attributed and not hidden in ordinary cost-per-task. Zero paid budget permits no positive-charge admission, even to reach a sample-size target.

review.rationale: The staged schedule assigns measurement owners and gates primary pairing on approvals and fault tests. It correctly excludes historical G observations as substitutes for contemporaneous pairs, accounts for duplicate study work and does not allow sample targets to override zero paid budget.

reasoning_steps.title: 13. Ninety-day execution, owners and resource feasibility

reasoning_steps.argument: Report paired gains alongside monthly and annual sunk, incremental and fully loaded costs, active-researcher counts and cost per successful parent task; a statistically positive gain is not automatically economical. The supplied peer extract 5c8fdc17-0ce8-4ea3-b8dc-79e05f97d0db emphasizes this distinction, but its original and numerical example were not inspected and are not adopted as measured evidence. The supplied peer extract bfcf812f-b3a9-46ff-862c-4d0b4cd76978 concerns disconnected remote authorization with immediate home-campus revocation and no fresh information. Its warning is compatible with fail-closed remote admission; it does not prove all locally authorized egress or weaker approved lease models unavailable. Adopt both extracts only as prompts for cost and partition tests; leave their broader claims unverified. The project's descriptions of MindRouter protocol translation, WDRR, quotas, audit and telemetry are unverified background here. The required documentation and PEARC'26 paper still need actual access dates and version checks at https://mindrouter.ai/documentation.html and https://ai4ra.uidaho.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Sheneman_MindRouter_PEARC26_Short_Paper.pdf. The date 2026-10-31 is project-reported prior review, not this session's access date. This design adds statistical and operational specificity; novelty against established evaluation methods and empirical generality are not assessed.

review.rationale: The supplied peer scopes support treating economics and disconnected authorization as separate constraints, not empirical validation. The proposal does not transfer the partition limitation to models with fresh local authorization or approved weaker leases, and correctly leaves source access and novelty unassessed.

reasoning_steps.title: 14. Cost, peer evidence and source verification remain separate gates

skeptic_output.argument_summary: For paired outcomes D=Y_F−Y_G, D² indicates discordance, giving Δ=p10−p01 and Var(D)=q−Δ². Marginal binomial intervals for the two discordance probabilities, combined by a union bound, yield a conservative interval for Δ without assuming independence between discordance counts. Requiring its lower endpoint to exceed 0.10 is stronger than requiring an interval to exclude zero. The planning examples demonstrate the weakness of 30-pair precision, while the independent-block Hoeffding interval exposes the cost of weaker dependence assumptions. Parent-task denominators, missing-outcome rules, contemporaneous pairing and bounded fairness windows improve the design, but final sample feasibility and operational approvals remain open.
assumptions_reviewed: Probability coverage and independent-pair planning require independent, identically sampled paired parent tasks within the declared population; correlated live workloads are not automatically covered.
The block interval requires independent bounded block averages and targets an equal-block effect, not an automatically equivalent task-weighted effect.
Interpretability requires faithful arm execution, matched non-federation entitlements, fixed parent tasks, blinded adjudication, complete accounting and no cross-arm leakage.
Discordance rates, deadlines, operational thresholds and the planning envelope are hypothetical proposed inputs, not measured values or university policy.
skeptic_output.contribution_rationale: The branch materially improves the pilot through fixed parent-task denominators, a clear margin estimand, a conservative paired interval, explicit dependence limitations, three-way decisions and measurable fairness windows. These are standard analytical and evaluation techniques applied usefully to the project, not demonstrated methodological novelty. Empirical generality, deployment usefulness and economic superiority remain unassessed.

D takes values −1, 0 and 1, so E(D²)=p10+p01=q and Var(D)=q−Δ². Dividing by n is justified for independent identically sampled pairs, not arbitrary live-service observations.

Each discordance count has a binomial marginal under the stated model. Two intervals with failure probability α/2 each have joint coverage at least 1−α by the union bound, regardless of their dependence; subtracting endpoints therefore gives valid conservative coverage for Δ.

The proposed probabilities are valid and have Δ=0.10. Substitution into the variance and normal-width formulas reproduces the reported rounded values and approximate sample sizes. The text properly separates these hand approximations from exact interval requirements and measured discordance.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Evidence boundary and retained negative constraints

reasoning_steps.argument: Proposed protected tables: Operation(home_id, issuer_epoch, root_task_id, operation_id, principal, project, department, scoped_client_key, canonicalization_version, immutable_manifest_ref, keyed_manifest_digest, classification_authority/version, OPEN/CLOSED, close_reason); Attempt(operation_id, attempt_sequence, state, row_version, reservation_deadline, bound_destination/account/model/tool/contract_profile, liability_profile_version, sender_id, sender_incarnation, sender_epoch, handler_nonce, grant_commit_id, grant_commit_time, policy_versions, consumed, outcome_observations); Sender(sender_id, incarnation, epoch, ACTIVE/FENCED, workload_identity). The immutable manifest binds the complete translated wire request, attachment bytes or immutable approved-domain references, destination identity, resource limits and retention requirements. Translation and attachment resolution occur before freezing; unknown fields or mutable content invalidate validation. Classifications cover derived prompts, outputs, logs, caches and embeddings. A digest is a binding aid, not proof of correct classification. Identifiers and status responses convey no sending authority.
reasoning_steps.title: 2. Durable identity, immutable request and sender records

reasoning_steps.argument: LedgerScope(scope_id, period_id, currency/unit, cap_B, settled_S, held_H, version) and Reservation(attempt_id, scope_id, period_id, maximum_q, HELD/SETTLED, settled_charge, settlement_event_id) record all applicable user/project/department/campus/shared-payer obligations. SettlementEvidence records provider/account identity, attempt correlation, evidence version and digest, finality basis, total charge and reconciliation authority. Protected audit events include transaction ID, actor, policy versions, old/new state and reason; they exclude unnecessary raw payload. Unique keys cover attempt identity, scoped client idempotency keys, reservation rows and settlement events. Exact integer accounting units and conservative rounding avoid floating-point admission errors. Policy, cancellation, sender registry, attempt and scope rows must participate in the same authoritative serializable transaction domain; asynchronous policy replicas or audit exports cannot substitute for this domain.
reasoning_steps.title: 3. Durable ledger and audit fields

reasoning_steps.argument: Reserve locks the attempt and all applicable scope rows in a stable order, checks VALIDATED and every post-reservation balance, inserts all reservation rows, updates held balances and writes the audit event in one durable transaction. It maps to VALIDATED→RESERVED. A conditional close transaction checks state=RESERVED and consumed=false, writes PRE_SEND_CLOSED plus its permanent replay marker, and removes the holds atomically. It maps to the abstract pre-send close. A competing commit either precedes that close or fails its state predicate; no partially released reservation or partial multi-scope admission is allowed. A failed eligibility check may close in the same transaction, or leave RESERVED for a later conditional close; it must not create a send right.
reasoning_steps.title: 4. Reserve and close transactions map directly to the abstract machine

reasoning_steps.argument: Place the final trusted sender inside the controlled egress service, not in a tenant worker or recoverable job queue. Before committing, one handler creates a fresh incarnation-bound nonce and registers one local continuation. CommitDispatch locks the attempt, operation, relevant current policy/identity rows, sender registry and reservations. It verifies RESERVED, deadline, OPEN operation, exact manifest, current approvals and ACTIVE matching sender incarnation/epoch; then writes COMMITTED, consumed=true, the complete sender binding, grant commit ID and audit event atomically, leaving holds unchanged. This is exactly the abstract CommitDispatch ordering point. A duplicate CommitDispatch request returns state only, even to the same sender. There is no transferable bearer grant and no API for claiming an already committed attempt. Policy and sender changes must conflict with these reads rather than race through a stale cache.
reasoning_steps.title: 5. Grant-to-sender binding and authoritative commit

reasoning_steps.argument: Only the original live handler receiving an unambiguous successful acknowledgement of its own consuming transaction may proceed. That acknowledgement is matched to its pending transaction, handler nonce and sender incarnation; a duplicate acknowledgement is ignored by a local one-shot latch. The handler flips that latch before invoking the HTTP transport once, using only the frozen request. It never obtains permission through a subsequent database read. A restart, handler exception, lost commit acknowledgement or process replacement destroys the continuation permanently. No checkpoint/VM clone may restore it. There is no recoverable outbox for COMMITTED requests. Because the durable RESERVED→COMMITTED transition has one winner, only that winner's original continuation can qualify; because its latch is single-use and recovery cannot qualify, at most one transport invocation can be initiated under these implementation premises. A crash after the latch but before transport sacrifices the request rather than risking a second initiation.
reasoning_steps.title: 6. The non-recoverable sender continuation supplies the missing one-use mechanism

reasoning_steps.argument: The proposed transport profile disables SDK retry loops, agent retries, HTTP authentication replays, automatic redirects, hedging, service-mesh/proxy retries, durable-job redelivery and reconnect-based request resubmission. Disable TLS early data and library replay after HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 connection errors; streaming resume must not issue a new invocation. The database driver must not turn an ambiguous commit into an automatically retried grant operation. Connection setup may occur before commit without request content, but any error after commit ends this attempt's sending path. Ordinary TCP retransmission within one connection is not a second adapter invocation; provider-side duplication or repeated charging remains outside that guarantee. An explicitly approved later paid retry requires a new attempt, fresh reservation and authorization, and is blocked while its predecessor's liability remains unresolved in this design. Tools and embeddings are separately mediated operations, not hidden SDK side effects.
reasoning_steps.title: 7. Disable retries at every request-replaying layer

reasoning_steps.argument: Database fencing increments the sender epoch or marks its incarnation FENCED, preventing that incarnation from committing any new grant. It never transfers its consumed grants to a replacement. A paused sender that already received a grant might still send after database fencing; this is consistent with decision-time authorization but is not evidence of physical exclusion. Where physical exclusion is required, a separate control must remove that workload identity's egress permission, terminate its existing connections and prevent credential reuse at the last controlled network hop. An expired lease or changed database epoch alone cannot stop an already-open socket. Packets already beyond that hop may still arrive. The design therefore does not financially release a committed attempt merely because a fence was requested or acknowledged.
reasoning_steps.title: 8. Fencing has separate database and network meanings

reasoning_steps.argument: Keep every unresolved financial record and every live-attempt binding. After closure or settlement, retain an access-controlled tombstone keyed by issuer epoch and attempt identity for as long as that identity can be presented. If no finite replay horizon is established, retain the rejection information indefinitely; payload retention need not be indefinite. Compaction may instead retire an entire issuer epoch permanently, provided all creation/commit entry points reject old-epoch identifiers and credentials and new epochs never reuse their namespace. Unresolved accounting remains available to a separate reconciliation path. Client idempotency-key lifetime must be explicit: an expired old key is rejected, not silently interpreted as a fresh paid task. A stale backup cannot resume admissions until reconciled with the authoritative consumed/rejection history, or isolated behind a newly fenced namespace and credentials that cannot revive old grants. Database durability without rollback protection is insufficient.
reasoning_steps.title: 9. Replay lifetime, retirement and backup restoration

reasoning_steps.argument: Recovery reads records to report status, close genuinely RESERVED attempts, collect final evidence and reconcile ledgers; it never sends COMMITTED work. COMMITTED with missing observations becomes UNCERTAIN, and REPORTED is not settlement. For this concrete candidate, remove the optional post-commit local 'proof of non-issuance' release optimization: every committed attempt needs authoritative final liability evidence before releasing any headroom, even if local logs suggest it never sent. This is stricter than the abstract machine, not a reuse of its unimplemented fencing shortcut. Final total c≤q settles all scope rows atomically, changing each S to S+c and H to H−q once. Duplicate evidence is a no-op; conflicting evidence is quarantined. Alternatively, book the full q conservatively without increasing headroom, explicitly marking it as a conservative charge rather than measured billing. Timeout, cancellation, rejection status, absent packets in a partial capture and ordinary billing-period rollover are not final evidence.
reasoning_steps.title: 10. Recovery and financial reconciliation narrow the zero-charge shortcut

reasoning_steps.argument: Successful validation maps to VALIDATED; durable reservation and grant consumption map as in steps 4–5. Sender latch changes, packet activity and provisional observation writes do not alter the financial abstraction. An acknowledged send observation can map to IN_FLIGHT; a provisional response maps to REPORTED; an ambiguous result maps to UNCERTAIN. Missing observation writes cannot undo COMMITTED. Conditional pre-grant closure maps to PRE_SEND_CLOSED; authoritative settlement maps to SETTLED. Status queries, duplicate requests, duplicate final evidence and rejected old epochs are stuttering transitions. Conservative full-ceiling booking preserves coverage without claiming a final measured charge. The refinement deliberately omits delivery guarantees and recovery retransmission; thus it is not an exactly-once transactional-outbox design.
reasoning_steps.title: 11. Remaining abstraction map

reasoning_steps.argument:
All schedules here are EXPECTED, NOT EXECUTED.
A. Crash before grant transaction: state remains RESERVED or an in-progress transaction resolves through the authority. Recovery sends nothing. If definitively still RESERVED, conditional close releases q and permanently blocks commit.
B. Transaction commits, but database acknowledgement to the sender is lost: state=COMMITTED, consumed=true, hold=q. The original handler takes its error path; status returns COMMITTED but no send permission. Recovery marks uncertainty and does not resend or release.
C. Positive commit acknowledgement arrives; crash before the latch, or after the latch but before transport: restart has no qualifying continuation. The grant remains consumed and q remains covered despite possibly zero real charge.
D. Transport starts; crash before or after request delivery: the same durable state may be observed in both histories. Recovery cannot distinguish them, so neither resend nor release follows.
E. Provider completes, but the response to the client or the local observation write is lost: client replay returns the existing operation status. It creates no new attempt. Authoritative final charge evidence later permits settlement, not retransmission.

B. RESERVED expiry races with commit. Close first means PRE_SEND_CLOSED and released hold, so commit fails; commit first means consumed=true, so close cannot release. No wall-clock cleanup may bypass this predicate.
C. Destination revocation precedes commit: the current-policy transaction denies. Commit precedes revocation: later sending remains possible; no post-revocation-delivery claim is made.
D. A duplicate commit acknowledgement reaches W1 twice: only the original pending continuation accepts the first, and its latch rejects the second. W1 restart accepts neither.
E. Settled A is replayed after compaction: its tombstone or permanently retired issuer epoch rejects commit. Restoring a pre-consumption backup without namespace fencing would reopen a replay path and is a forbidden recovery procedure.

argument_steps.title: 1. Evidence boundary and retained negative constraints

argument_steps.argument: Proposed protected tables: Operation(home_id, issuer_epoch, root_task_id, operation_id, principal, project, department, scoped_client_key, canonicalization_version, immutable_manifest_ref, keyed_manifest_digest, classification_authority/version, OPEN/CLOSED, close_reason); Attempt(operation_id, attempt_sequence, state, row_version, reservation_deadline, bound_destination/account/model/tool/contract_profile, liability_profile_version, sender_id, sender_incarnation, sender_epoch, handler_nonce, grant_commit_id, grant_commit_time, policy_versions, consumed, outcome_observations); Sender(sender_id, incarnation, epoch, ACTIVE/FENCED, workload_identity). The immutable manifest binds the complete translated wire request, attachment bytes or immutable approved-domain references, destination identity, resource limits and retention requirements. Translation and attachment resolution occur before freezing; unknown fields or mutable content invalidate validation. Classifications cover derived prompts, outputs, logs, caches and embeddings. A digest is a binding aid, not proof of correct classification. Identifiers and status responses convey no sending authority.

review.rationale: Accepted as a proposed specification premise, not an implemented property. The records bind identity, destination and frozen content, and the explicit classification premise is necessary because a digest alone cannot establish policy correctness.

argument_steps.title: 2. Durable identity, immutable request and sender records

argument_steps.argument: LedgerScope(scope_id, period_id, currency/unit, cap_B, settled_S, held_H, version) and Reservation(attempt_id, scope_id, period_id, maximum_q, HELD/SETTLED, settled_charge, settlement_event_id) record all applicable user/project/department/campus/shared-payer obligations. SettlementEvidence records provider/account identity, attempt correlation, evidence version and digest, finality basis, total charge and reconciliation authority. Protected audit events include transaction ID, actor, policy versions, old/new state and reason; they exclude unnecessary raw payload. Unique keys cover attempt identity, scoped client idempotency keys, reservation rows and settlement events. Exact integer accounting units and conservative rounding avoid floating-point admission errors. Policy, cancellation, sender registry, attempt and scope rows must participate in the same authoritative serializable transaction domain; asynchronous policy replicas or audit exports cannot substitute for this domain.

review.rationale: Accepted as a conditional schema and transaction-domain premise. Unique reservation and settlement keys plus exact accounting units support deterministic admission accounting, provided the stated serialization and complete-scope coverage actually hold.

argument_steps.title: 3. Durable ledger and audit fields

argument_steps.argument: Reserve locks the attempt and all applicable scope rows in a stable order, checks VALIDATED and every post-reservation balance, inserts all reservation rows, updates held balances and writes the audit event in one durable transaction. It maps to VALIDATED→RESERVED. A conditional close transaction checks state=RESERVED and consumed=false, writes PRE_SEND_CLOSED plus its permanent replay marker, and removes the holds atomically. It maps to the abstract pre-send close. A competing commit either precedes that close or fails its state predicate; no partially released reservation or partial multi-scope admission is allowed. A failed eligibility check may close in the same transaction, or leave RESERVED for a later conditional close; it must not create a send right.

review.rationale: Under the stated atomic transaction premise, commit and pre-send closure cannot both win the same state predicate. Releasing holds only in the winning closure transaction prevents a partially released committed reservation.

argument_steps.title: 4. Reserve and close transactions map directly to the abstract machine

argument_steps.argument: Place the final trusted sender inside the controlled egress service, not in a tenant worker or recoverable job queue. Before committing, one handler creates a fresh incarnation-bound nonce and registers one local continuation. CommitDispatch locks the attempt, operation, relevant current policy/identity rows, sender registry and reservations. It verifies RESERVED, deadline, OPEN operation, exact manifest, current approvals and ACTIVE matching sender incarnation/epoch; then writes COMMITTED, consumed=true, the complete sender binding, grant commit ID and audit event atomically, leaving holds unchanged. This is exactly the abstract CommitDispatch ordering point. A duplicate CommitDispatch request returns state only, even to the same sender. There is no transferable bearer grant and no API for claiming an already committed attempt. Policy and sender changes must conflict with these reads rather than race through a stale cache.

review.rationale: Accepted as a conditional design premise. A consuming state transition bound to one sender incarnation and nonce, with duplicate calls returning status only, supplies a unique logical grant ordering point. Policy freshness additionally requires the declared conflicting authoritative reads.

argument_steps.title: 5. Grant-to-sender binding and authoritative commit

argument_steps.argument: Only the original live handler receiving an unambiguous successful acknowledgement of its own consuming transaction may proceed. That acknowledgement is matched to its pending transaction, handler nonce and sender incarnation; a duplicate acknowledgement is ignored by a local one-shot latch. The handler flips that latch before invoking the HTTP transport once, using only the frozen request. It never obtains permission through a subsequent database read. A restart, handler exception, lost commit acknowledgement or process replacement destroys the continuation permanently. No checkpoint/VM clone may restore it. There is no recoverable outbox for COMMITTED requests. Because the durable RESERVED→COMMITTED transition has one winner, only that winner's original continuation can qualify; because its latch is single-use and recovery cannot qualify, at most one transport invocation can be initiated under these implementation premises. A crash after the latch but before transport sacrifices the request rather than risking a second initiation.

review.rationale: The inference follows under the explicit no-cloning, original-acknowledgement and single-use-latch premises: one commit winner can qualify one continuation, and that continuation can initiate transport once. Crashes can suppress the only initiation; they cannot authorize recovery initiation.

argument_steps.title: 6. The non-recoverable sender continuation supplies the missing one-use mechanism

argument_steps.argument: The proposed transport profile disables SDK retry loops, agent retries, HTTP authentication replays, automatic redirects, hedging, service-mesh/proxy retries, durable-job redelivery and reconnect-based request resubmission. Disable TLS early data and library replay after HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 connection errors; streaming resume must not issue a new invocation. The database driver must not turn an ambiguous commit into an automatically retried grant operation. Connection setup may occur before commit without request content, but any error after commit ends this attempt's sending path. Ordinary TCP retransmission within one connection is not a second adapter invocation; provider-side duplication or repeated charging remains outside that guarantee. An explicitly approved later paid retry requires a new attempt, fresh reservation and authorization, and is blocked while its predecessor's liability remains unresolved in this design. Tools and embeddings are separately mediated operations, not hidden SDK side effects.

review.rationale: Accepted as a proposed sender and transport premise, not observed configuration. The listed replay sources must be disabled for the adapter-initiation claim; ordinary TCP retransmission does not itself create a second application invocation. Provider duplication remains explicitly outside scope.

argument_steps.title: 7. Disable retries at every request-replaying layer

argument_steps.argument: Database fencing increments the sender epoch or marks its incarnation FENCED, preventing that incarnation from committing any new grant. It never transfers its consumed grants to a replacement. A paused sender that already received a grant might still send after database fencing; this is consistent with decision-time authorization but is not evidence of physical exclusion. Where physical exclusion is required, a separate control must remove that workload identity's egress permission, terminate its existing connections and prevent credential reuse at the last controlled network hop. An expired lease or changed database epoch alone cannot stop an already-open socket. Packets already beyond that hop may still arrive. The design therefore does not financially release a committed attempt merely because a fence was requested or acknowledged.

review.rationale: Database fencing prevents new commits but cannot revoke a continuation already holding authority or stop an existing socket. The distinction between logical fencing, physical egress exclusion and packets already beyond campus control is sound.

argument_steps.title: 8. Fencing has separate database and network meanings

argument_steps.argument: Keep every unresolved financial record and every live-attempt binding. After closure or settlement, retain an access-controlled tombstone keyed by issuer epoch and attempt identity for as long as that identity can be presented. If no finite replay horizon is established, retain the rejection information indefinitely; payload retention need not be indefinite. Compaction may instead retire an entire issuer epoch permanently, provided all creation/commit entry points reject old-epoch identifiers and credentials and new epochs never reuse their namespace. Unresolved accounting remains available to a separate reconciliation path. Client idempotency-key lifetime must be explicit: an expired old key is rejected, not silently interpreted as a fresh paid task. A stale backup cannot resume admissions until reconciled with the authoritative consumed/rejection history, or isolated behind a newly fenced namespace and credentials that cannot revive old grants. Database durability without rollback protection is insufficient.

review.rationale: Permanent rejection information or epoch retirement can prevent identifier replay. However, the alternative allowing admission after stale restore merely behind a fenced namespace does not establish preservation of outstanding liabilities.

argument_steps.title: 9. Replay lifetime, retirement and backup restoration

argument_steps.argument: Recovery reads records to report status, close genuinely RESERVED attempts, collect final evidence and reconcile ledgers; it never sends COMMITTED work. COMMITTED with missing observations becomes UNCERTAIN, and REPORTED is not settlement. For this concrete candidate, remove the optional post-commit local 'proof of non-issuance' release optimization: every committed attempt needs authoritative final liability evidence before releasing any headroom, even if local logs suggest it never sent. Duplicate evidence is a no-op; conflicting evidence is quarantined. Alternatively, book the full q conservatively without increasing headroom, explicitly marking it as a conservative charge rather than measured billing. Timeout, cancellation, rejection status, absent packets in a partial capture and ordinary billing-period rollover are not final evidence.

review.rationale: The accounting deduction is valid conditional on authoritative evidence fixing total liability, including any later effect of a delayed sender. Replacing hold q with final charge c no greater than q cannot increase covered exposure; booking q conservatively restores no headroom. The operational evidence predicate remains unestablished.

argument_steps.title: 10. Recovery and financial reconciliation narrow the zero-charge shortcut

argument_steps.argument: Successful validation maps to VALIDATED; durable reservation and grant consumption map as in steps 4–5. Sender latch changes, packet activity and provisional observation writes do not alter the financial abstraction. An acknowledged send observation can map to IN_FLIGHT; a provisional response maps to REPORTED; an ambiguous result maps to UNCERTAIN. Missing observation writes cannot undo COMMITTED. Conditional pre-grant closure maps to PRE_SEND_CLOSED; authoritative settlement maps to SETTLED. Status queries, duplicate requests, duplicate final evidence and rejected old epochs are stuttering transitions. Conservative full-ceiling booking preserves coverage without claiming a final measured charge. The refinement deliberately omits delivery guarantees and recovery retransmission; thus it is not an exactly-once transactional-outbox design.

argument_steps.title: 11. Remaining abstraction map

All schedules here are EXPECTED, NOT EXECUTED.

objective_review.argument_summary: The unique RESERVED-to-COMMITTED transaction identifies one eligible continuation; its one-shot latch and prohibition on recovery sends prevent a second adapter initiation under the sender premises. Conditional closure competes atomically with commit, while unresolved committed liabilities remain covered. Final settlement preserves the accounting inequality when evidence truly fixes total liability. Expected schedules illustrate these rules but are not execution evidence. Namespace retirement blocks replay, yet cannot by itself reconstruct liabilities lost from a stale restore. Exact correspondence to the prior abstract machine is unresolved because its definitions are absent.
assumptions: The home transaction domain is durable, linearizable/serializable for the stated conflicting operations, initially within every cap, and protected against admission from stale restores or split-brain authorities.

Campus authorities correctly classify and bind complete immutable requests and derived content, and explicitly accept decision-time authorization rather than a guarantee of no later transmission, receipt or execution.

The trusted sender and database driver follow the specified single-continuation, one-shot-latch and no-recovery-send procedure; process/VM cloning, checkpoint resumption and automatic request-replaying layers are excluded.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Evidence boundary and retained negative constraints

reasoning_steps.argument: Proposed protected tables: Operation(home_id, issuer_epoch, root_task_id, operation_id, principal, project, department, scoped_client_key, canonicalization_version, immutable_manifest_ref, keyed_manifest_digest, classification_authority/version, OPEN/CLOSED, close_reason); Attempt(operation_id, attempt_sequence, state, row_version, reservation_deadline, bound_destination/account/model/tool/contract_profile, liability_profile_version, sender_id, sender_incarnation, sender_epoch, handler_nonce, grant_commit_id, grant_commit_time, policy_versions, consumed, outcome_observations); Sender(sender_id, incarnation, epoch, ACTIVE/FENCED, workload_identity). The immutable manifest binds the complete translated wire request, attachment bytes or immutable approved-domain references, destination identity, resource limits and retention requirements. Translation and attachment resolution occur before freezing; unknown fields or mutable content invalidate validation. Classifications cover derived prompts, outputs, logs, caches and embeddings. A digest is a binding aid, not proof of correct classification. Identifiers and status responses convey no sending authority.

review.rationale: Accepted as a proposed specification premise, not an implemented property. The records bind identity, destination and frozen content, and the explicit classification premise is necessary because a digest alone cannot establish policy correctness.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Durable identity, immutable request and sender records

reasoning_steps.argument: LedgerScope(scope_id, period_id, currency/unit, cap_B, settled_S, held_H, version) and Reservation(attempt_id, scope_id, period_id, maximum_q, HELD/SETTLED, settled_charge, settlement_event_id) record all applicable user/project/department/campus/shared-payer obligations. SettlementEvidence records provider/account identity, attempt correlation, evidence version and digest, finality basis, total charge and reconciliation authority. Protected audit events include transaction ID, actor, policy versions, old/new state and reason; they exclude unnecessary raw payload. Unique keys cover attempt identity, scoped client idempotency keys, reservation rows and settlement events. Exact integer accounting units and conservative rounding avoid floating-point admission errors. Policy, cancellation, sender registry, attempt and scope rows must participate in the same authoritative serializable transaction domain; asynchronous policy replicas or audit exports cannot substitute for this domain.

review.rationale: Accepted as a conditional schema and transaction-domain premise. Unique reservation and settlement keys plus exact accounting units support deterministic admission accounting, provided the stated serialization and complete-scope coverage actually hold.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Durable ledger and audit fields

reasoning_steps.argument: Reserve locks the attempt and all applicable scope rows in a stable order, checks VALIDATED and every post-reservation balance, inserts all reservation rows, updates held balances and writes the audit event in one durable transaction. It maps to VALIDATED→RESERVED. A conditional close transaction checks state=RESERVED and consumed=false, writes PRE_SEND_CLOSED plus its permanent replay marker, and removes the holds atomically. It maps to the abstract pre-send close. A competing commit either precedes that close or fails its state predicate; no partially released reservation or partial multi-scope admission is allowed. A failed eligibility check may close in the same transaction, or leave RESERVED for a later conditional close; it must not create a send right.

review.rationale: Under the stated atomic transaction premise, commit and pre-send closure cannot both win the same state predicate. Releasing holds only in the winning closure transaction prevents a partially released committed reservation.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Reserve and close transactions map directly to the abstract machine

reasoning_steps.argument: Place the final trusted sender inside the controlled egress service, not in a tenant worker or recoverable job queue. Before committing, one handler creates a fresh incarnation-bound nonce and registers one local continuation. CommitDispatch locks the attempt, operation, relevant current policy/identity rows, sender registry and reservations. It verifies RESERVED, deadline, OPEN operation, exact manifest, current approvals and ACTIVE matching sender incarnation/epoch; then writes COMMITTED, consumed=true, the complete sender binding, grant commit ID and audit event atomically, leaving holds unchanged. This is exactly the abstract CommitDispatch ordering point. A duplicate CommitDispatch request returns state only, even to the same sender. There is no transferable bearer grant and no API for claiming an already committed attempt. Policy and sender changes must conflict with these reads rather than race through a stale cache.

review.rationale: Accepted as a conditional design premise. A consuming state transition bound to one sender incarnation and nonce, with duplicate calls returning status only, supplies a unique logical grant ordering point. Policy freshness additionally requires the declared conflicting authoritative reads.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Grant-to-sender binding and authoritative commit

reasoning_steps.argument: Only the original live handler receiving an unambiguous successful acknowledgement of its own consuming transaction may proceed. That acknowledgement is matched to its pending transaction, handler nonce and sender incarnation; a duplicate acknowledgement is ignored by a local one-shot latch. The handler flips that latch before invoking the HTTP transport once, using only the frozen request. It never obtains permission through a subsequent database read. A restart, handler exception, lost commit acknowledgement or process replacement destroys the continuation permanently. No checkpoint/VM clone may restore it. There is no recoverable outbox for COMMITTED requests. Because the durable RESERVED→COMMITTED transition has one winner, only that winner's original continuation can qualify; because its latch is single-use and recovery cannot qualify, at most one transport invocation can be initiated under these implementation premises. A crash after the latch but before transport sacrifices the request rather than risking a second initiation.

review.rationale: The inference follows under the explicit no-cloning, original-acknowledgement and single-use-latch premises: one commit winner can qualify one continuation, and that continuation can initiate transport once. Crashes can suppress the only initiation; they cannot authorize recovery initiation.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. The non-recoverable sender continuation supplies the missing one-use mechanism

reasoning_steps.argument: The proposed transport profile disables SDK retry loops, agent retries, HTTP authentication replays, automatic redirects, hedging, service-mesh/proxy retries, durable-job redelivery and reconnect-based request resubmission. Disable TLS early data and library replay after HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 connection errors; streaming resume must not issue a new invocation. The database driver must not turn an ambiguous commit into an automatically retried grant operation. Connection setup may occur before commit without request content, but any error after commit ends this attempt's sending path. Ordinary TCP retransmission within one connection is not a second adapter invocation; provider-side duplication or repeated charging remains outside that guarantee. An explicitly approved later paid retry requires a new attempt, fresh reservation and authorization, and is blocked while its predecessor's liability remains unresolved in this design. Tools and embeddings are separately mediated operations, not hidden SDK side effects.

review.rationale: Accepted as a proposed sender and transport premise, not observed configuration. The listed replay sources must be disabled for the adapter-initiation claim; ordinary TCP retransmission does not itself create a second application invocation. Provider duplication remains explicitly outside scope.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Disable retries at every request-replaying layer

reasoning_steps.argument: Database fencing increments the sender epoch or marks its incarnation FENCED, preventing that incarnation from committing any new grant. It never transfers its consumed grants to a replacement. A paused sender that already received a grant might still send after database fencing; this is consistent with decision-time authorization but is not evidence of physical exclusion. Where physical exclusion is required, a separate control must remove that workload identity's egress permission, terminate its existing connections and prevent credential reuse at the last controlled network hop. An expired lease or changed database epoch alone cannot stop an already-open socket. Packets already beyond that hop may still arrive. The design therefore does not financially release a committed attempt merely because a fence was requested or acknowledged.

review.rationale: Database fencing prevents new commits but cannot revoke a continuation already holding authority or stop an existing socket. The distinction between logical fencing, physical egress exclusion and packets already beyond campus control is sound.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Fencing has separate database and network meanings

reasoning_steps.argument: Keep every unresolved financial record and every live-attempt binding. After closure or settlement, retain an access-controlled tombstone keyed by issuer epoch and attempt identity for as long as that identity can be presented. If no finite replay horizon is established, retain the rejection information indefinitely; payload retention need not be indefinite. Compaction may instead retire an entire issuer epoch permanently, provided all creation/commit entry points reject old-epoch identifiers and credentials and new epochs never reuse their namespace. Unresolved accounting remains available to a separate reconciliation path. Client idempotency-key lifetime must be explicit: an expired old key is rejected, not silently interpreted as a fresh paid task. A stale backup cannot resume admissions until reconciled with the authoritative consumed/rejection history, or isolated behind a newly fenced namespace and credentials that cannot revive old grants. Database durability without rollback protection is insufficient.

review.objection: Require both replay isolation and financial reconciliation or conservative exposure coverage. An old liability of 6 missing from a cap-10 backup plus a new reservation of 6 exceeds the cap despite entirely fresh identifiers and credentials.
review.rationale: Permanent rejection information or epoch retirement can prevent identifier replay. However, the alternative allowing admission after stale restore merely behind a fenced namespace does not establish preservation of outstanding liabilities.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Replay lifetime, retirement and backup restoration

reasoning_steps.argument: Recovery reads records to report status, close genuinely RESERVED attempts, collect final evidence and reconcile ledgers; it never sends COMMITTED work. COMMITTED with missing observations becomes UNCERTAIN, and REPORTED is not settlement. For this concrete candidate, remove the optional post-commit local 'proof of non-issuance' release optimization: every committed attempt needs authoritative final liability evidence before releasing any headroom, even if local logs suggest it never sent. This is stricter than the abstract machine, not a reuse of its unimplemented fencing shortcut. Final total c≤q settles all scope rows atomically, changing each S to S+c and H to H−q once. Duplicate evidence is a no-op; conflicting evidence is quarantined. Alternatively, book the full q conservatively without increasing headroom, explicitly marking it as a conservative charge rather than measured billing. Timeout, cancellation, rejection status, absent packets in a partial capture and ordinary billing-period rollover are not final evidence.

review.rationale: The accounting deduction is valid conditional on authoritative evidence fixing total liability, including any later effect of a delayed sender. Replacing hold q with final charge c no greater than q cannot increase covered exposure; booking q conservatively restores no headroom. The operational evidence predicate remains unestablished.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Recovery and financial reconciliation narrow the zero-charge shortcut

reasoning_steps.argument: Successful validation maps to VALIDATED; durable reservation and grant consumption map as in steps 4–5. Sender latch changes, packet activity and provisional observation writes do not alter the financial abstraction. An acknowledged send observation can map to IN_FLIGHT; a provisional response maps to REPORTED; an ambiguous result maps to UNCERTAIN. Missing observation writes cannot undo COMMITTED. Conditional pre-grant closure maps to PRE_SEND_CLOSED; authoritative settlement maps to SETTLED. Status queries, duplicate requests, duplicate final evidence and rejected old epochs are stuttering transitions. Conservative full-ceiling booking preserves coverage without claiming a final measured charge. The refinement deliberately omits delivery guarantees and recovery retransmission; thus it is not an exactly-once transactional-outbox design.

review.objection: Supply the earlier state and transition definitions, including settlement, uncertainty and conservative-booking semantics. No repeat of the invariant proof is necessary.
review.rationale: The proposed local abstraction is coherent: observations cannot undo consumption, and status reads supply no send right. Exact refinement to the earlier abstract machine cannot be checked from pointer-only source material.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Remaining abstraction map

reasoning_steps.argument:
All schedules here are EXPECTED, NOT EXECUTED.
A. Crash before grant transaction: state remains RESERVED or an in-progress transaction resolves through the authority. Recovery sends nothing. If definitively still RESERVED, conditional close releases q and permanently blocks commit.
B. Transaction commits, but database acknowledgement to the sender is lost: state=COMMITTED, consumed=true, hold=q. The original handler takes its error path; status returns COMMITTED but no send permission. Recovery marks uncertainty and does not resend or release.
C. Positive commit acknowledgement arrives; crash before the latch, or after the latch but before transport: restart has no qualifying continuation. The grant remains consumed and q remains covered despite possibly zero real charge.
D. Transport starts; crash before or after request delivery: the same durable state may be observed in both histories. Recovery cannot distinguish them, so neither resend nor release follows.
E. Provider completes, but the response to the client or the local observation write is lost: client replay returns the existing operation status. It creates no new attempt. Authoritative final charge evidence later permits settlement, not retransmission.
F. Commit definitively aborts: no grant exists. Close the still-RESERVED attempt transactionally; do not treat an ambiguous outcome as a definitive abort.

review.rationale: As expected schedules, these distinguish definite abort from ambiguous commit and correctly prohibit status-driven sending. Each crash location either leaves a conditional pre-grant close available or retains the consumed grant and financial coverage.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Expected, not executed: commit-response loss and crash schedules

reasoning_steps.argument:
All schedules here are EXPECTED, NOT EXECUTED.
A. Sender W1 commits A; pauses; replacement W2 starts under a new incarnation. W2 cannot claim A; a duplicate commit sees consumed=true. W1 may still initiate its sole previously granted invocation unless physically fenced. The hold remains in either case.
B. RESERVED expiry races with commit. Close first means PRE_SEND_CLOSED and released hold, so commit fails; commit first means consumed=true, so close cannot release. No wall-clock cleanup may bypass this predicate.
C. Destination revocation precedes commit: the current-policy transaction denies. Commit precedes revocation: later sending remains possible; no post-revocation-delivery claim is made.
D. A duplicate commit acknowledgement reaches W1 twice: only the original pending continuation accepts the first, and its latch rejects the second. W1 restart accepts neither.
E. Settled A is replayed after compaction: its tombstone or permanently retired issuer epoch rejects commit. Restoring a pre-consumption backup without namespace fencing would reopen a replay path and is a forbidden recovery procedure.

review.rationale: The schedules correctly serialize closure against commit and distinguish revocation before authorization from revocation after authorization. Replacements cannot claim consumed attempts. The backup example correctly identifies unfenced replay risk but does not repair step 9's separate financial-recovery gap.

reasoning_steps.title: 13. Expected, not executed: fencing, replay and concurrent closure

reasoning_steps.argument: All amounts are hypothetical accounting units; all schedules are EXPECTED, NOT EXECUTED. Let B=10, S=0, and reserve q=6. After commit-response loss, timeout, crash or rejection without final evidence, H=6 and available headroom=4; an independent q=6 request is denied. Authoritative final c=4 produces S=4, H=0, headroom=6. A duplicate settlement leaves those values unchanged. Conservative booking at q=6 instead gives S=6, H=0, headroom=4: it resolves the hold administratively but does not manufacture credit. With cap zero, a positive paid reservation fails before grant creation. Unsafe controls remain locally refuted: timeout release can permit two charges totaling 12 against cap 10; redelivering a committed outbox entry can issue the same attempt again; using lease expiry as zero-charge evidence can release funds before an old sender or already-delivered request incurs liability. These counterexamples block those candidates, not the project.

review.rationale: The hypothetical arithmetic checks: a hold of 6 under cap 10 leaves 4; settlement at 4 leaves 6; conservative booking at 6 leaves 4. Timeout release followed by another liability of 6 permits total liability 12. These are analytical examples, not measured outcomes.

reasoning_steps.title: 14. Expected, not executed: financial headroom and unsafe controls

reasoning_steps.argument: I examined the supplied incomplete extract of source 1e89585c-2b17-49bd-bb1e-dc1df98ba8ca and the available pointer and ledger scope for target bfcf812f-b3a9-46ff-862c-4d0b4cd76978; neither original was inspected. The source concerns a hypothetical cost/workload comparison, including a scenario with zero additional usable peer capacity. The target's recorded domain concerns new disconnected admissions with neither fresh revocation information nor prior request-specific authorization. These domains overlap only when peer capacity requires such a fresh disconnected admission. A GPU can be nominally idle yet unusable for this request because authorization, approved domain, model fit, connectivity, reservation or deadline eligibility is absent. That logical distinction does not imply that all federation capacity is unusable, or establish economic disadvantage. I adopt it as an admission-accounting requirement, reject transfer of numerical/economic conclusions into this branch, and leave the source's scenario results unverified. It changes the next test: record denial reasons and authorized usable capacity separately from GPU telemetry, without assuming the source's zero-capacity scenario is typical.

This does not establish the peer's numerical scenario, typical utilization or federation's economic disadvantage.

reasoning_steps.title: 15. Ownership-cost handoff: adopt only the authorized-capacity distinction

reasoning_steps.argument: I examined the supplied incomplete extract of source 2fef1213-38ff-4acf-9af2-a0c28b89b0da and the target's supplied pointer/ledger scope, not the originals. Its proposed paired pilot and statistical gates are not evidence that this adapter is safe. Its partition rationale matches this design only for an admission point lacking authoritative fresh information and an earlier request-specific grant. EXPECTED, NOT EXECUTED paired schedules: (a) a disconnected peer sees identical cached approval in histories with and without a later home revocation; with no prior grant, this design denies both fresh commits; (b) a reachable home authority approving local work is not in that indistinguishable-information domain and may admit it; (c) a grant already committed before partition is not a fresh disconnected authorization, although delivery may fail and liability remains held. Explicitly approved weaker lease semantics would change the revocation contract and require a separate model; they are not adopted here.
