argument_steps.title: Budget scenarios and the corrected feasible-baseline rule

argument_steps.argument: For a fixed admission plan with expected local usefulness μ_L=a_S q_L,S+a_N q_L,N and positive API usefulness q_A, the expected gate requires a_S q_L,S≥160 and k=max(0,ceil((1,400−μ_L)/q_A)) additional API roots. It is feasible under the conservative envelope only if k does not exceed the distinct eligible residual demand or available API capacity and rk≤B. If q_A=0, API calls cannot close a positive shortfall. If admissions or usefulness change with demand, overload, model fit or selection, recompute by stratum rather than extending the 667 threshold. Among plans passing policy, capacity, budget and declared performance gates, compare fully loaded cost; do not choose a cheap plan that fails a mandatory stratum.

review.rationale: For a fixed plan and positive selected-cohort q_A, the ceiling expression is the smallest integer admission count closing the expected shortfall. Sensitive coverage, residual demand, technical capacity and reservation feasibility remain separate necessary checks.

argument_steps.title: General rule when local strata or API quality differ

argument_steps.argument: Let C_G be cost on one explicitly chosen accounting basis and let F add overhead H>0. If F offers exactly the same usable service opportunities, approvals and non-federation entitlements as G, no additional peer service, and no offsetting reliability, scheduling or administrative benefit, G can reproduce F's useful outcomes without the federation overhead. Hence C_F=C_G+H>C_G while usefulness and feasibility are equal. For positive useful counts, G also has lower cost per useful completion. The result holds for fully loaded cost when H is fully loaded overhead; an incremental-cost claim additionally requires avoidable incremental H>0. Zero extra GPU capacity alone is insufficient if federation changes another useful service dimension. This dominance does not depend on whether the sensitive gate passes, but G's least-cost feasible status does.

review.rationale: Identical service opportunities and no offsetting benefit permit the same usefulness while positive H raises cost. The argument correctly distinguishes fully loaded overhead from avoidable incremental overhead and does not infer dominance from zero extra GPU capacity alone.

argument_steps.title: Retain only scoped G-over-F dominance

argument_steps.argument: Keep input, cached-input, output, embedding, tool and egress prices symbolic and undated until evidence is obtained. For each permitted workflow attempt j, reserve at least [I_j^max max(p_uncached,j^upper,p_cached,j^upper)+O_j^max p_output,j^upper]/10^6, plus enforceable upper ancillary charges. I_j^max includes all inputs, including candidates for caching; cache eligibility or a predicted cache hit never reduces the envelope below uncached exposure. Sum over bounded Investigator/Skeptic, agent, tool and permitted retry attempts, including repeated context, and include applicable tax, currency, commitment and other contractual liabilities without double counting. The per-root r must dominate this total. Missing finite bounds, unlimited descendants or unbounded price changes block the hard-cap argument. Actual cached discounts may lower settled cost after reconciliation, but are not assumed savings available for admission in this conservative worksheet.

review.rationale: Pricing every possible input token at the larger applicable upper rate covers uncached exposure. Summing over bounded attempts and ancillary liabilities gives a conditional envelope, not a current price estimate. Missing enforceable bounds appropriately invalidate the hard-cap argument.

argument_steps.title: Unknown prices and a cache-miss-safe reservation envelope

argument_steps.argument: A candidate ordering is: bind an immutable request manifest to authoritative identity and inherited classifications; check allowed destinations and retention/audit requirements; atomically prepare reservations at every applicable user/project/department/campus scope; then serialize current policy, cancellation/revocation state, reservation ownership and a one-use dispatch grant at a home-authority commit point. Merely checking policy before dispatch leaves a concurrent-revocation race. The system still needs crash-safe grant consumption, sender fencing, durable recovery and explicit semantics for a grant committed before revocation but transmitted later. Decision-time semantics permit that later transmission only if campus authorities explicitly accept it; they are not a no-post-revocation-delivery guarantee. Ambiguity or loss of authoritative access denies/defer new external grants. Timeout and cancellation requests do not release unresolved liability; retransmission or retry requires a bounded, authorized attempt and cannot silently escalate to paid or disallowed destinations. These transitions, including separately approved accounts, are proposed, not implemented or campus-approved.

review.rationale: As a proposed specification and explicit limitation, this is appropriately scoped: a pre-dispatch check alone does not order concurrent revocation, and a committed grant is not a delivery-time guarantee. The step leaves fencing, recovery and campus acceptance open rather than claiming safety.

reasoning_steps.argument: Let L denote campus-local only, A approved API only, G the campus gateway plus separately approved external access, and F the proposed federation extension. The supplied scenario has 2,000 monthly root tasks, including 200 sensitive campus-only roots and 1,800 API-eligible roots. Local deadline-feasible admission is 1,000 roots. reasoning_steps.title: Scope, baselines and evidence boundary

reasoning_steps.argument: Index strata s by data classification and task requirements, and destinations d by local, approved API or approved partner. Let N_s be offered roots and n_bds be distinct roots assigned to destination d under baseline b, with sum_d n_bds≤N_s. Unauthorized assignments must have n_bds=0. Let X_bdsj be 1 only if admitted root j completes through an authorized workflow and meets its prespecified quality, deadline and provenance requirements. Define q_bds as the average marginal probability of that joint event among those admissions. Then expected useful completions are μ_b=sum_s,d n_bds q_bds. No independence assumption is needed for this expectation identity. Calls, tool invocations and retries are descendants, not additional completed roots. Probabilities depend on the selected mix, load and configuration; they are not universal model constants.

review.rationale: For distinct assigned roots and a joint useful-completion indicator, summing marginal expectations gives the stated identity. Independence is unnecessary, and counting descendants separately would incorrectly inflate successes.

reasoning_steps.title: Define stratum-specific admissions and usefulness

reasoning_steps.argument: For 200 sensitive and 800 other local admissions, aggregate q_L=0.80 says only 200q_L,S+800q_L,N=800 under an expected-count interpretation. Choosing q_L,S=0 and q_L,N=1 satisfies this equation but yields zero expected sensitive completions. The same construction works as imposed exact counts: 0/200 sensitive and 800/800 other successes give 800/1,000 overall. Thus the aggregate provides no positive lower bound on sensitive successes. Sensitive-first admission does not repair this: admission priority is not task usefulness. This directly accepts the counterexample recorded in o168 and withdraws the unqualified sensitive-feasibility inference identified in o172.

review.rationale: Substitution of q_S=0 and q_N=1 gives 800 aggregate useful roots and zero sensitive usefulness. The exact-count construction has the same property, so neither interpretation supports the old sensitive-coverage inference.

reasoning_steps.title: Accept and reproduce the sensitive-stratum counterexample

reasoning_steps.argument: With n_G,local,S=200, the expected sensitive gate μ_G,S≥160 requires q_G,local,S≥0.80. If sensitive admissions instead equal a_S≤200, the condition is a_S q_G,local,S≥160; it is impossible when a_S<160. To retain the worksheet's 800 expected local completions, a simple explicit repair is q_G,local,S=q_G,local,N=0.80 with 200 and 800 admissions respectively. More generally, retaining the aggregate 800 and assuming q_G,local,S≥0.80 requires q_G,local,N=(800−200q_G,local,S)/800. The sensitive premise is additional and hypothetical, not implied by aggregate q_L.

review.rationale: The expected sensitive gate is exactly a_S q_S≥160. With 200 admissions it requires q_S≥0.80; with fewer than 160 it is impossible since probabilities cannot exceed one. The aggregate-preserving expression for the other stratum is algebraically correct.

reasoning_steps.title: Additional sensitive premise needed for G

reasoning_steps.argument: This repair interprets q values as hypothetical marginal probabilities and μ as expected counts. An imposed exact scenario could instead assign 160 sensitive, 640 other local and 900 API useful completions at 1,000 API admissions, totaling 1,700; those assigned integers describe that scenario only. Exact 0.90 fractions cannot be imposed for every integer admission count without an additional rounding convention. For actual service, let Y_b,S and Y_b be observed useful root counts: the proposed realized gate is Y_b,S≥160 and Y_b≥1,400. Expected counts alone do not imply this gate. For example, a common shock making all 200 sensitive roots succeed with probability 0.80 and all fail with probability 0.20 has the assumed marginals and expectation 160, yet fails coverage with probability 0.20. No distribution, confidence or predictive guarantee is established.

review.rationale: Assigned integer totals, expected totals and observed service gates are correctly separated. The common-shock example has marginal success probability 0.80 for each sensitive root but a 0.20 probability of zero sensitive completions, directly disproving a realized guarantee from the expectation.

reasoning_steps.title: Separate exact scenarios, expectations and realized service

reasoning_steps.argument: For L and G, retain the hypothetical local plan of 200 sensitive plus 800 other roots. G may admit up to 1,000 remaining, distinct API-eligible roots. A admits no sensitive roots and up to 1,800 eligible roots. For the cap formulas only, additionally assume average API usefulness remains 0.90 for each selected admission cohort, including cap-truncated cohorts; an aggregate API fraction at full admission would not justify this extrapolation. The illustrative F dominance case uses the same local/API plan as G and zero usable extra partner admissions. F's possible approval for some partner work is not usable capacity and does not expand sensitive permissions.

review.rationale: These are explicit conditional admission and selected-cohort usefulness premises, not deductions from aggregate quality. Requiring 0.90 for each cap-selected API cohort avoids the same aggregation error repaired locally.

These are feasibility results for the declared plans and assumptions, not an optimization over every possible routing plan.

Since 600/0.90 is 666⅔ and the residual limit is 1,000, the expected total gate is equivalent to at least 667 API admissions. The exclusion of other routing plans is explicit.

These are derived reservation thresholds, not API prices or measured average task costs. If r exceeds the applicable threshold, no baseline in this scoped comparison passes; if the sensitive premise is absent, G and F cannot be certified even when the cap is sufficient. If r is unknown or unenforceable, paid admission is not justified by this rule. Zero API budget also does not make local operation free: local service still requires approved operating resources.

reasoning_steps.argument: For a fixed admission plan with expected local usefulness μ_L=a_S q_L,S+a_N q_L,N and positive API usefulness q_A, the expected gate requires a_S q_L,S≥160 and k=max(0,ceil((1,400−μ_L)/q_A)) additional API roots. It is feasible under the conservative envelope only if k does not exceed the distinct eligible residual demand or available API capacity and rk≤B. If q_A=0, API calls cannot close a positive shortfall. If admissions or usefulness change with demand, overload, model fit or selection, recompute by stratum rather than extending the 667 threshold. Among plans passing policy, capacity, budget and declared performance gates, compare fully loaded cost; do not choose a cheap plan that fails a mandatory stratum.

review.rationale: For a fixed plan and positive selected-cohort q_A, the ceiling expression is the smallest integer admission count closing the expected shortfall. Sensitive coverage, residual demand, technical capacity and reservation feasibility remain separate necessary checks.

reasoning_steps.title: General rule when local strata or API quality differ

reasoning_steps.argument: Let C_G be cost on one explicitly chosen accounting basis and let F add overhead H>0. If F offers exactly the same usable service opportunities, approvals and non-federation entitlements as G, no additional peer service, and no offsetting reliability, scheduling or administrative benefit, G can reproduce F's useful outcomes without the federation overhead. Hence C_F=C_G+H>C_G while usefulness and feasibility are equal. For positive useful counts, G also has lower cost per useful completion. The result holds for fully loaded cost when H is fully loaded overhead; an incremental-cost claim additionally requires avoidable incremental H>0. Zero extra GPU capacity alone is insufficient if federation changes another useful service dimension. This dominance does not depend on whether the sensitive gate passes, but G's least-cost feasible status does.

review.rationale: Identical service opportunities and no offsetting benefit permit the same usefulness while positive H raises cost. The argument correctly distinguishes fully loaded overhead from avoidable incremental overhead and does not infer dominance from zero extra GPU capacity alone.

reasoning_steps.title: Retain only scoped G-over-F dominance

reasoning_steps.argument: Keep input, cached-input, output, embedding, tool and egress prices symbolic and undated until evidence is obtained. For each permitted workflow attempt j, reserve at least [I_j^max max(p_uncached,j^upper,p_cached,j^upper)+O_j^max p_output,j^upper]/10^6, plus enforceable upper ancillary charges. I_j^max includes all inputs, including candidates for caching; cache eligibility or a predicted cache hit never reduces the envelope below uncached exposure. Sum over bounded Investigator/Skeptic, agent, tool and permitted retry attempts, including repeated context, and include applicable tax, currency, commitment and other contractual liabilities without double counting. The per-root r must dominate this total. Missing finite bounds, unlimited descendants or unbounded price changes block the hard-cap argument. Actual cached discounts may lower settled cost after reconciliation, but are not assumed savings available for admission in this conservative worksheet.

review.rationale: Pricing every possible input token at the larger applicable upper rate covers uncached exposure. Summing over bounded attempts and ancillary liabilities gives a conditional envelope, not a current price estimate. Missing enforceable bounds appropriately invalidate the hard-cap argument.

reasoning_steps.title: Unknown prices and a cache-miss-safe reservation envelope

reasoning_steps.argument: A candidate ordering is: bind an immutable request manifest to authoritative identity and inherited classifications; check allowed destinations and retention/audit requirements; atomically prepare reservations at every applicable user/project/department/campus scope; then serialize current policy, cancellation/revocation state, reservation ownership and a one-use dispatch grant at a home-authority commit point. Merely checking policy before dispatch leaves a concurrent-revocation race. The system still needs crash-safe grant consumption, sender fencing, durable recovery and explicit semantics for a grant committed before revocation but transmitted later. Decision-time semantics permit that later transmission only if campus authorities explicitly accept it; they are not a no-post-revocation-delivery guarantee. Ambiguity or loss of authoritative access denies/defer new external grants. Timeout and cancellation requests do not release unresolved liability; retransmission or retry requires a bounded, authorized attempt and cannot silently escalate to paid or disallowed destinations. These transitions, including separately approved accounts, are proposed, not implemented or campus-approved.

review.rationale: As a proposed specification and explicit limitation, this is appropriately scoped: a pre-dispatch check alone does not order concurrent revocation, and a committed grant is not a delivery-time guarantee. The step leaves fencing, recovery and campus acceptance open rather than claiming safety.

skeptic_output.argument_summary: Linearity of expectation gives useful roots as the sum of stratum admissions times their joint useful-completion probabilities, without independence. The aggregate equation 200q_S+800q_N=800 admits q_S=0 and q_N=1. Explicitly setting both local strata to 0.80 instead yields 160 sensitive and 800 total expected local completions. Another 600 expected completions at API usefulness 0.90 requires ceil(600/0.90)=667 distinct API roots. The conservative reservation plan admits min(1,000,floor(B/r)) such roots. L fails the total gate; A fails sensitive coverage; scoped F shares G's expected service but adds positive cost. Correlated failures demonstrate why none of these expectations guarantees realized coverage.

### Partial finding

Conditional on: The comparison uses the supplied hypothetical 2,000-root monthly cohort, including 200 sensitive campus-only roots, with proposed gates of 160 useful sensitive roots and 1,400 useful roots overall; these are not university policy; L and G admit 200 sensitive and 800 other roots locally; G has 1,000 distinct residual API-eligible roots, A has 1,800 eligible roots, and the assumed capacities and deadlines support these admissions; For the repaired expected-count example, each local stratum has average joint authorized quality/deadline/provenance usefulness 0.80, and every selected API cohort has average usefulness 0.90. These are hypothetical probabilities, not observations or guarantees; The cap rule assumes enforceable r>0, complete financial mediation, atomic durable nested reservations, nonbinding subsidiary quotas, no opening liabilities or commitments, adequate API capacity and no recycling of reservation savings; All relevant workflow descendants and charges fit within r, including cache misses at uncached input rates, bounded retries, tools, embeddings and ancillary contractual liabilities; Scoped F dominance assumes identical useful service opportunities and non-federation entitlements, zero usable additional peer service, no offsetting benefit, and strictly positive overhead on the stated accounting basis; The economic threshold uses the same fixed workload, horizon, useful-root acceptance rules and cost basis, with C_G>0, S_G>0, ΔC>0 and S_G+ΔS>0. Conditional on the Investigator's listed hypothetical admission, stratum-usefulness, capacity, financial-enforcement and dominance assumptions, G meets the declared expected-count gates exactly when floor(B/r)≥667. This does not establish realized service. With identical usable service opportunities, no offsetting federation benefit and positive overhead on the stated accounting basis, G is cheaper than F. No campus deployment advantage is established.

Linearity of expectation gives useful roots as the sum of stratum admissions times their joint useful-completion probabilities, without independence. The aggregate equation 200q_S+800q_N=800 admits q_S=0 and q_N=1. Explicitly setting both local strata to 0.80 instead yields 160 sensitive and 800 total expected local completions. Another 600 expected completions at API usefulness 0.90 requires ceil(600/0.90)=667 distinct API roots. The conservative reservation plan admits min(1,000,floor(B/r)) such roots. L fails the total gate; A fails sensitive coverage; scoped F shares G's expected service but adds positive cost. Correlated failures demonstrate why none of these expectations guarantees realized coverage.

argument_steps.argument: Let L denote campus-local only, A approved API only, G the campus gateway plus separately approved external access, and F the proposed federation extension. The supplied scenario has 2,000 monthly root tasks, including 200 sensitive campus-only roots and 1,800 API-eligible roots. Local deadline-feasible admission is 1,000 roots. The supplied MindRouter characterization includes protocol translation, WDRR, quotas, audit logging and GPU telemetry; these descriptions are not independently verified here. Federation and frontier routing remain hypothetical extensions. The project-reported 2026-10-31 reference review is not an access date established in this session. Original artifacts 5c8fdc17-0ce8-4ea3-b8dc-79e05f97d0db and 1e89585c-2b17-49bd-bb1e-dc1df98ba8ca are pointers only; I do not claim to have checked their ledger or full derivations.

review.rationale: The baseline definitions and cohort are explicitly scenario premises, covered by the conditional claim. Published capabilities and the reported review date are appropriately treated as supplied descriptions, not independently established facts.

argument_steps.title: Scope, baselines and evidence boundary

argument_steps.argument: Index strata s by data classification and task requirements, and destinations d by local, approved API or approved partner. Let N_s be offered roots and n_bds be distinct roots assigned to destination d under baseline b, with sum_d n_bds≤N_s. Unauthorized assignments must have n_bds=0. Let X_bdsj be 1 only if admitted root j completes through an authorized workflow and meets its prespecified quality, deadline and provenance requirements. Define q_bds as the average marginal probability of that joint event among those admissions. Then expected useful completions are μ_b=sum_s,d n_bds q_bds. No independence assumption is needed for this expectation identity. Calls, tool invocations and retries are descendants, not additional completed roots. Probabilities depend on the selected mix, load and configuration; they are not universal model constants.

review.rationale: For distinct assigned roots and a joint useful-completion indicator, summing marginal expectations gives the stated identity. Independence is unnecessary, and counting descendants separately would incorrectly inflate successes.

argument_steps.title: Define stratum-specific admissions and usefulness

argument_steps.argument: For 200 sensitive and 800 other local admissions, aggregate q_L=0.80 says only 200q_L,S+800q_L,N=800 under an expected-count interpretation. Choosing q_L,S=0 and q_L,N=1 satisfies this equation but yields zero expected sensitive completions. The same construction works as imposed exact counts: 0/200 sensitive and 800/800 other successes give 800/1,000 overall. Thus the aggregate provides no positive lower bound on sensitive successes. Sensitive-first admission does not repair this: admission priority is not task usefulness. This directly accepts the counterexample recorded in o168 and withdraws the unqualified sensitive-feasibility inference identified in o172.

review.rationale: Substitution of q_S=0 and q_N=1 gives 800 aggregate useful roots and zero sensitive usefulness. The exact-count construction has the same property, so neither interpretation supports the old sensitive-coverage inference.

argument_steps.title: Accept and reproduce the sensitive-stratum counterexample

argument_steps.argument: With n_G,local,S=200, the expected sensitive gate μ_G,S≥160 requires q_G,local,S≥0.80. If sensitive admissions instead equal a_S≤200, the condition is a_S q_G,local,S≥160; it is impossible when a_S<160. To retain the worksheet's 800 expected local completions, a simple explicit repair is q_G,local,S=q_G,local,N=0.80 with 200 and 800 admissions respectively. More generally, retaining the aggregate 800 and assuming q_G,local,S≥0.80 requires q_G,local,N=(800−200q_G,local,S)/800. The sensitive premise is additional and hypothetical, not implied by aggregate q_L.

review.rationale: The expected sensitive gate is exactly a_S q_S≥160. With 200 admissions it requires q_S≥0.80; with fewer than 160 it is impossible since probabilities cannot exceed one. The aggregate-preserving expression for the other stratum is algebraically correct.

argument_steps.title: Additional sensitive premise needed for G

argument_steps.argument: This repair interprets q values as hypothetical marginal probabilities and μ as expected counts. An imposed exact scenario could instead assign 160 sensitive, 640 other local and 900 API useful completions at 1,000 API admissions, totaling 1,700; those assigned integers describe that scenario only. Exact 0.90 fractions cannot be imposed for every integer admission count without an additional rounding convention. For actual service, let Y_b,S and Y_b be observed useful root counts: the proposed realized gate is Y_b,S≥160 and Y_b≥1,400. Expected counts alone do not imply this gate. For example, a common shock making all 200 sensitive roots succeed with probability 0.80 and all fail with probability 0.20 has the assumed marginals and expectation 160, yet fails coverage with probability 0.20. No distribution, confidence or predictive guarantee is established.

review.rationale: Assigned integer totals, expected totals and observed service gates are correctly separated. The common-shock example has marginal success probability 0.80 for each sensitive root but a 0.20 probability of zero sensitive completions, directly disproving a realized guarantee from the expectation.

argument_steps.title: Separate exact scenarios, expectations and realized service

argument_steps.argument: For L and G, retain the hypothetical local plan of 200 sensitive plus 800 other roots. G may admit up to 1,000 remaining, distinct API-eligible roots. A admits no sensitive roots and up to 1,800 eligible roots. For the cap formulas only, additionally assume average API usefulness remains 0.90 for each selected admission cohort, including cap-truncated cohorts; an aggregate API fraction at full admission would not justify this extrapolation. The illustrative F dominance case uses the same local/API plan as G and zero usable extra partner admissions. F's possible approval for some partner work is not usable capacity and does not expand sensitive permissions.

review.rationale: These are explicit conditional admission and selected-cohort usefulness premises, not deductions from aggregate quality. Requiring 0.90 for each cap-selected API cohort avoids the same aggregation error repaired locally.

argument_steps.title: Make the repaired admission plans explicit

argument_steps.argument: Assume a common positive enforceable maximum API liability r per admitted root, no opening liability or commitment, nonbinding subsidiary quotas, sufficient API capacity and no recycling of reservation savings. Define m_G(B)=min(1,000,floor(B/r)) and m_A(B)=min(1,800,floor(B/r)). Then L has (μ_S,μ_total)=(160,800); A has (0,0.90m_A); G has (160,800+0.90m_G); and F has the same expected counts as G in the scoped no-extra-service case. L fails the overall 1,400 gate. A fails sensitive coverage at every cap, even though its maximum overall expectation is 1,620. G and scoped F pass both expected-count gates iff m_G≥ceil((1,400−800)/0.90)=667. These are feasibility results for the declared plans and assumptions, not an optimization over every possible routing plan.

review.rationale: Under the uniform enforceable envelope and stated quota/capacity assumptions, the admission formulas follow. Since 600/0.90 is 666⅔ and the residual limit is 1,000, the expected total gate is equivalent to at least 667 API admissions. The exclusion of other routing plans is explicit.

argument_steps.title: Derive the cap-dependent expected comparison

argument_steps.argument: At B=0, no paid roots are admitted and none of these plans passes both expected gates. At B=$2,000, $4,000 or $8,000, G and scoped F pass iff r≤B/667: respectively about $2.9985, $5.9970 or $11.9940 of maximum reserved liability per root. These are derived reservation thresholds, not API prices or measured average task costs. If r exceeds the applicable threshold, no baseline in this scoped comparison passes; if the sensitive premise is absent, G and F cannot be certified even when the cap is sufficient. If r is unknown or unenforceable, paid admission is not justified by this rule. Zero API budget also does not make local operation free: local service still requires approved operating resources.

review.rationale: For positive r, floor(B/r)≥667 is equivalent to r≤B/667. The rounded thresholds are correct, and neither an unknown liability bound nor zero API budget is represented as establishing free or authorized operation.

argument_steps.title: Budget scenarios and the corrected feasible-baseline rule

argument_steps.argument: For a fixed admission plan with expected local usefulness μ_L=a_S q_L,S+a_N q_L,N and positive API usefulness q_A, the expected gate requires a_S q_L,S≥160 and k=max(0,ceil((1,400−μ_L)/q_A)) additional API roots. It is feasible under the conservative envelope only if k does not exceed the distinct eligible residual demand or available API capacity and rk≤B. If q_A=0, API calls cannot close a positive shortfall. If admissions or usefulness change with demand, overload, model fit or selection, recompute by stratum rather than extending the 667 threshold. Among plans passing policy, capacity, budget and declared performance gates, compare fully loaded cost; do not choose a cheap plan that fails a mandatory stratum.

review.rationale: For a fixed plan and positive selected-cohort q_A, the ceiling expression is the smallest integer admission count closing the expected shortfall. Sensitive coverage, residual demand, technical capacity and reservation feasibility remain separate necessary checks.

argument_steps.title: General rule when local strata or API quality differ

argument_steps.argument: Let C_G be cost on one explicitly chosen accounting basis and let F add overhead H>0. If F offers exactly the same usable service opportunities, approvals and non-federation entitlements as G, no additional peer service, and no offsetting reliability, scheduling or administrative benefit, G can reproduce F's useful outcomes without the federation overhead. Hence C_F=C_G+H>C_G while usefulness and feasibility are equal. For positive useful counts, G also has lower cost per useful completion. The result holds for fully loaded cost when H is fully loaded overhead; an incremental-cost claim additionally requires avoidable incremental H>0. Zero extra GPU capacity alone is insufficient if federation changes another useful service dimension. This dominance does not depend on whether the sensitive gate passes, but G's least-cost feasible status does.

review.rationale: Identical service opportunities and no offsetting benefit permit the same usefulness while positive H raises cost. The argument correctly distinguishes fully loaded overhead from avoidable incremental overhead and does not infer dominance from zero extra GPU capacity alone.

argument_steps.title: Retain only scoped G-over-F dominance

argument_steps.argument: Keep input, cached-input, output, embedding, tool and egress prices symbolic and undated until evidence is obtained. For each permitted workflow attempt j, reserve at least [I_j^max max(p_uncached,j^upper,p_cached,j^upper)+O_j^max p_output,j^upper]/10^6, plus enforceable upper ancillary charges. I_j^max includes all inputs, including candidates for caching; cache eligibility or a predicted cache hit never reduces the envelope below uncached exposure. Sum over bounded Investigator/Skeptic, agent, tool and permitted retry attempts, including repeated context, and include applicable tax, currency, commitment and other contractual liabilities without double counting. The per-root r must dominate this total. Missing finite bounds, unlimited descendants or unbounded price changes block the hard-cap argument. Actual cached discounts may lower settled cost after reconciliation, but are not assumed savings available for admission in this conservative worksheet.

review.rationale: Pricing every possible input token at the larger applicable upper rate covers uncached exposure. Summing over bounded attempts and ancillary liabilities gives a conditional envelope, not a current price estimate. Missing enforceable bounds appropriately invalidate the hard-cap argument.

argument_steps.title: Unknown prices and a cache-miss-safe reservation envelope

argument_steps.argument: A candidate ordering is: bind an immutable request manifest to authoritative identity and inherited classifications; check allowed destinations and retention/audit requirements; atomically prepare reservations at every applicable user/project/department/campus scope; then serialize current policy, cancellation/revocation state, reservation ownership and a one-use dispatch grant at a home-authority commit point. Merely checking policy before dispatch leaves a concurrent-revocation race. The system still needs crash-safe grant consumption, sender fencing, durable recovery and explicit semantics for a grant committed before revocation but transmitted later. Decision-time semantics permit that later transmission only if campus authorities explicitly accept it; they are not a no-post-revocation-delivery guarantee. Ambiguity or loss of authoritative access denies/defer new external grants. Timeout and cancellation requests do not release unresolved liability; retransmission or retry requires a bounded, authorized attempt and cannot silently escalate to paid or disallowed destinations. These transitions, including separately approved accounts, are proposed, not implemented or campus-approved.

review.rationale: As a proposed specification and explicit limitation, this is appropriately scoped: a pre-dispatch check alone does not order concurrent revocation, and a committed grant is not a delivery-time guarantee. The step leaves fencing, recovery and campus acceptance open rather than claiming safety.

argument_steps.argument: For handoff b5946156-a3c9-4f8c-aba9-c809e329964f, the supplied extract of 2fef1213-38ff-4acf-9af2-a0c28b89b0da proposes paired root-task evaluation with identical non-federation entitlements and separate operational gates. Independently, for the same horizon, workload, acceptance rules and cost basis, C_G>0, S_G>0, ΔC>0 and S_G+ΔS>0 imply (C_G+ΔC)/(S_G+ΔS)<C_G/S_G iff ΔS>S_GΔC/C_G, by cross multiplication. I adopt separate measurement of incremental and fully loaded costs and paired authorized useful outcomes; I do not adopt the peer's proposed 0.10 gain gate or truncated planning numbers as an economic threshold. The next pilot specification must predeclare the estimand, sampling dependence, cost allocation and uncertainty rule. No peer result is independently verified.

review.rationale: The peer's paired or independent-block assumptions do not follow for arbitrary live workloads. Independently cross-multiplying positive denominators gives C_GΔS>S_GΔC, establishing the economic threshold without relying on truncated peer calculations or its proposed 0.10 gate.

solution_review.argument_summary: Linearity of expectation gives useful roots as the sum of stratum admissions times their joint useful-completion probabilities, without independence. The aggregate equation 200q_S+800q_N=800 admits q_S=0 and q_N=1. Explicitly setting both local strata to 0.80 instead yields 160 sensitive and 800 total expected local completions. Another 600 expected completions at API usefulness 0.90 requires ceil(600/0.90)=667 distinct API roots. The conservative reservation plan admits min(1,000,floor(B/r)) such roots. L fails the total gate; A fails sensitive coverage; scoped F shares G's expected service but adds positive cost. Correlated failures demonstrate why none of these expectations guarantees realized coverage.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Evidence boundary and retained negative constraints

reasoning_steps.argument: Proposed protected tables: Operation(home_id, issuer_epoch, root_task_id, operation_id, principal, project, department, scoped_client_key, canonicalization_version, immutable_manifest_ref, keyed_manifest_digest, classification_authority/version, OPEN/CLOSED, close_reason); Attempt(operation_id, attempt_sequence, state, row_version, reservation_deadline, bound_destination/account/model/tool/contract_profile, liability_profile_version, sender_id, sender_incarnation, sender_epoch, handler_nonce, grant_commit_id, grant_commit_time, policy_versions, consumed, outcome_observations); Sender(sender_id, incarnation, epoch, ACTIVE/FENCED, workload_identity). The immutable manifest binds the complete translated wire request, attachment bytes or immutable approved-domain references, destination identity, resource limits and retention requirements. Translation and attachment resolution occur before freezing; unknown fields or mutable content invalidate validation. Classifications cover derived prompts, outputs, logs, caches and embeddings. A digest is a binding aid, not proof of correct classification. Identifiers and status responses convey no sending authority.

review.rationale: Accepted as a proposed specification premise, not an implemented property. The records bind identity, destination and frozen content, and the explicit classification premise is necessary because a digest alone cannot establish policy correctness.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Durable identity, immutable request and sender records

reasoning_steps.argument: LedgerScope(scope_id, period_id, currency/unit, cap_B, settled_S, held_H, version) and Reservation(attempt_id, scope_id, period_id, maximum_q, HELD/SETTLED, settled_charge, settlement_event_id) record all applicable user/project/department/campus/shared-payer obligations. SettlementEvidence records provider/account identity, attempt correlation, evidence version and digest, finality basis, total charge and reconciliation authority. Protected audit events include transaction ID, actor, policy versions, old/new state and reason; they exclude unnecessary raw payload. Unique keys cover attempt identity, scoped client idempotency keys, reservation rows and settlement events. Exact integer accounting units and conservative rounding avoid floating-point admission errors. Policy, cancellation, sender registry, attempt and scope rows must participate in the same authoritative serializable transaction domain; asynchronous policy replicas or audit exports cannot substitute for this domain.

review.rationale: Accepted as a conditional schema and transaction-domain premise. Unique reservation and settlement keys plus exact accounting units support deterministic admission accounting, provided the stated serialization and complete-scope coverage actually hold.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Durable ledger and audit fields

reasoning_steps.argument: Reserve locks the attempt and all applicable scope rows in a stable order, checks VALIDATED and every post-reservation balance, inserts all reservation rows, updates held balances and writes the audit event in one durable transaction. It maps to VALIDATED→RESERVED. A conditional close transaction checks state=RESERVED and consumed=false, writes PRE_SEND_CLOSED plus its permanent replay marker, and removes the holds atomically. It maps to the abstract pre-send close. A competing commit either precedes that close or fails its state predicate; no partially released reservation or partial multi-scope admission is allowed. A failed eligibility check may close in the same transaction, or leave RESERVED for a later conditional close; it must not create a send right.

review.rationale: Under the stated atomic transaction premise, commit and pre-send closure cannot both win the same state predicate. Releasing holds only in the winning closure transaction prevents a partially released committed reservation.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Reserve and close transactions map directly to the abstract machine

reasoning_steps.argument: Place the final trusted sender inside the controlled egress service, not in a tenant worker or recoverable job queue. Before committing, one handler creates a fresh incarnation-bound nonce and registers one local continuation. CommitDispatch locks the attempt, operation, relevant current policy/identity rows, sender registry and reservations. It verifies RESERVED, deadline, OPEN operation, exact manifest, current approvals and ACTIVE matching sender incarnation/epoch; then writes COMMITTED, consumed=true, the complete sender binding, grant commit ID and audit event atomically, leaving holds unchanged. This is exactly the abstract CommitDispatch ordering point. A duplicate CommitDispatch request returns state only, even to the same sender. There is no transferable bearer grant and no API for claiming an already committed attempt. Policy and sender changes must conflict with these reads rather than race through a stale cache.

review.rationale: Accepted as a conditional design premise. A consuming state transition bound to one sender incarnation and nonce, with duplicate calls returning status only, supplies a unique logical grant ordering point. Policy freshness additionally requires the declared conflicting authoritative reads.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Grant-to-sender binding and authoritative commit

reasoning_steps.argument: Only the original live handler receiving an unambiguous successful acknowledgement of its own consuming transaction may proceed. That acknowledgement is matched to its pending transaction, handler nonce and sender incarnation; a duplicate acknowledgement is ignored by a local one-shot latch. The handler flips that latch before invoking the HTTP transport once, using only the frozen request. It never obtains permission through a subsequent database read. A restart, handler exception, lost commit acknowledgement or process replacement destroys the continuation permanently. No checkpoint/VM clone may restore it. There is no recoverable outbox for COMMITTED requests. Because the durable RESERVED→COMMITTED transition has one winner, only that winner's original continuation can qualify; because its latch is single-use and recovery cannot qualify, at most one transport invocation can be initiated under these implementation premises. A crash after the latch but before transport sacrifices the request rather than risking a second initiation.

review.rationale: The inference follows under the explicit no-cloning, original-acknowledgement and single-use-latch premises: one commit winner can qualify one continuation, and that continuation can initiate transport once. Crashes can suppress the only initiation; they cannot authorize recovery initiation.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. The non-recoverable sender continuation supplies the missing one-use mechanism

reasoning_steps.argument: The proposed transport profile disables SDK retry loops, agent retries, HTTP authentication replays, automatic redirects, hedging, service-mesh/proxy retries, durable-job redelivery and reconnect-based request resubmission. Disable TLS early data and library replay after HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 connection errors; streaming resume must not issue a new invocation. The database driver must not turn an ambiguous commit into an automatically retried grant operation. Connection setup may occur before commit without request content, but any error after commit ends this attempt's sending path. Ordinary TCP retransmission within one connection is not a second adapter invocation; provider-side duplication or repeated charging remains outside that guarantee. An explicitly approved later paid retry requires a new attempt, fresh reservation and authorization, and is blocked while its predecessor's liability remains unresolved in this design. Tools and embeddings are separately mediated operations, not hidden SDK side effects.

review.rationale: Accepted as a proposed sender and transport premise, not observed configuration. The listed replay sources must be disabled for the adapter-initiation claim; ordinary TCP retransmission does not itself create a second application invocation. Provider duplication remains explicitly outside scope.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Disable retries at every request-replaying layer

reasoning_steps.argument: Database fencing increments the sender epoch or marks its incarnation FENCED, preventing that incarnation from committing any new grant. It never transfers its consumed grants to a replacement. A paused sender that already received a grant might still send after database fencing; this is consistent with decision-time authorization but is not evidence of physical exclusion. Where physical exclusion is required, a separate control must remove that workload identity's egress permission, terminate its existing connections and prevent credential reuse at the last controlled network hop. An expired lease or changed database epoch alone cannot stop an already-open socket. Packets already beyond that hop may still arrive. The design therefore does not financially release a committed attempt merely because a fence was requested or acknowledged.

review.rationale: Database fencing prevents new commits but cannot revoke a continuation already holding authority or stop an existing socket. The distinction between logical fencing, physical egress exclusion and packets already beyond campus control is sound.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Fencing has separate database and network meanings

reasoning_steps.argument: Keep every unresolved financial record and every live-attempt binding. After closure or settlement, retain an access-controlled tombstone keyed by issuer epoch and attempt identity for as long as that identity can be presented. If no finite replay horizon is established, retain the rejection information indefinitely; payload retention need not be indefinite. Compaction may instead retire an entire issuer epoch permanently, provided all creation/commit entry points reject old-epoch identifiers and credentials and new epochs never reuse their namespace. Unresolved accounting remains available to a separate reconciliation path. Client idempotency-key lifetime must be explicit: an expired old key is rejected, not silently interpreted as a fresh paid task. A stale backup cannot resume admissions until reconciled with the authoritative consumed/rejection history, or isolated behind a newly fenced namespace and credentials that cannot revive old grants. Database durability without rollback protection is insufficient.

review.objection: Require both replay isolation and financial reconciliation or conservative exposure coverage. An old liability of 6 missing from a cap-10 backup plus a new reservation of 6 exceeds the cap despite entirely fresh identifiers and credentials.
review.rationale: Permanent rejection information or epoch retirement can prevent identifier replay. However, the alternative allowing admission after stale restore merely behind a fenced namespace does not establish preservation of outstanding liabilities.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Replay lifetime, retirement and backup restoration

reasoning_steps.argument: Recovery reads records to report status, close genuinely RESERVED attempts, collect final evidence and reconcile ledgers; it never sends COMMITTED work. COMMITTED with missing observations becomes UNCERTAIN, and REPORTED is not settlement. For this concrete candidate, remove the optional post-commit local 'proof of non-issuance' release optimization: every committed attempt needs authoritative final liability evidence before releasing any headroom, even if local logs suggest it never sent. This is stricter than the abstract machine, not a reuse of its unimplemented fencing shortcut. Final total c≤q settles all scope rows atomically, changing each S to S+c and H to H−q once. Duplicate evidence is a no-op; conflicting evidence is quarantined. Alternatively, book the full q conservatively without increasing headroom, explicitly marking it as a conservative charge rather than measured billing. Timeout, cancellation, rejection status, absent packets in a partial capture and ordinary billing-period rollover are not final evidence.

review.rationale: The accounting deduction is valid conditional on authoritative evidence fixing total liability, including any later effect of a delayed sender. Replacing hold q with final charge c no greater than q cannot increase covered exposure; booking q conservatively restores no headroom. The operational evidence predicate remains unestablished.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Recovery and financial reconciliation narrow the zero-charge shortcut

reasoning_steps.argument: Successful validation maps to VALIDATED; durable reservation and grant consumption map as in steps 4–5. Sender latch changes, packet activity and provisional observation writes do not alter the financial abstraction. An acknowledged send observation can map to IN_FLIGHT; a provisional response maps to REPORTED; an ambiguous result maps to UNCERTAIN. Missing observation writes cannot undo COMMITTED. Conditional pre-grant closure maps to PRE_SEND_CLOSED; authoritative settlement maps to SETTLED. Status queries, duplicate requests, duplicate final evidence and rejected old epochs are stuttering transitions. Conservative full-ceiling booking preserves coverage without claiming a final measured charge. The refinement deliberately omits delivery guarantees and recovery retransmission; thus it is not an exactly-once transactional-outbox design.

review.objection: Supply the earlier state and transition definitions, including settlement, uncertainty and conservative-booking semantics. No repeat of the invariant proof is necessary.
review.rationale: The proposed local abstraction is coherent: observations cannot undo consumption, and status reads supply no send right. Exact refinement to the earlier abstract machine cannot be checked from pointer-only source material.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Remaining abstraction map

reasoning_steps.argument:
All schedules here are EXPECTED, NOT EXECUTED.
A. Crash before grant transaction: state remains RESERVED or an in-progress transaction resolves through the authority. Recovery sends nothing. If definitively still RESERVED, conditional close releases q and permanently blocks commit.
B. Transaction commits, but database acknowledgement to the sender is lost: state=COMMITTED, consumed=true, hold=q. The original handler takes its error path; status returns COMMITTED but no send permission. Recovery marks uncertainty and does not resend or release.
C. Positive commit acknowledgement arrives; crash before the latch, or after the latch but before transport: restart has no qualifying continuation. The grant remains consumed and q remains covered despite possibly zero real charge.
D. Transport starts; crash before or after request delivery: the same durable state may be observed in both histories. Recovery cannot distinguish them, so neither resend nor release follows.
E. Provider completes, but the response to the client or the local observation write is lost: client replay returns the existing operation status. It creates no new attempt. Authoritative final charge evidence later permits settlement, not retransmission.
F. Commit definitively aborts: no grant exists. Close the still-RESERVED attempt transactionally; do not treat an ambiguous outcome as a definitive abort.

review.rationale: As expected schedules, these distinguish definite abort from ambiguous commit and correctly prohibit status-driven sending. Each crash location either leaves a conditional pre-grant close available or retains the consumed grant and financial coverage.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Expected, not executed: commit-response loss and crash schedules

reasoning_steps.argument:
All schedules here are EXPECTED, NOT EXECUTED.
A. Sender W1 commits A; pauses; replacement W2 starts under a new incarnation. W2 cannot claim A; a duplicate commit sees consumed=true. W1 may still initiate its sole previously granted invocation unless physically fenced. The hold remains in either case.
B. RESERVED expiry races with commit. Close first means PRE_SEND_CLOSED and released hold, so commit fails; commit first means consumed=true, so close cannot release. No wall-clock cleanup may bypass this predicate.
C. Destination revocation precedes commit: the current-policy transaction denies. Commit precedes revocation: later sending remains possible; no post-revocation-delivery claim is made.
D. A duplicate commit acknowledgement reaches W1 twice: only the original pending continuation accepts the first, and its latch rejects the second. W1 restart accepts neither.
E. Settled A is replayed after compaction: its tombstone or permanently retired issuer epoch rejects commit. Restoring a pre-consumption backup without namespace fencing would reopen a replay path and is a forbidden recovery procedure.

review.rationale: The schedules correctly serialize closure against commit and distinguish revocation before authorization from revocation after authorization. Replacements cannot claim consumed attempts. The backup example correctly identifies unfenced replay risk but does not repair step 9's separate financial-recovery gap.

reasoning_steps.title: 13. Expected, not executed: fencing, replay and concurrent closure

reasoning_steps.argument: All amounts are hypothetical accounting units; all schedules are EXPECTED, NOT EXECUTED. Let B=10, S=0, and reserve q=6. After commit-response loss, timeout, crash or rejection without final evidence, H=6 and available headroom=4; an independent q=6 request is denied. Authoritative final c=4 produces S=4, H=0, headroom=6. A duplicate settlement leaves those values unchanged. Conservative booking at q=6 instead gives S=6, H=0, headroom=4: it resolves the hold administratively but does not manufacture credit. With cap zero, a positive paid reservation fails before grant creation. Unsafe controls remain locally refuted: timeout release can permit two charges totaling 12 against cap 10; redelivering a committed outbox entry can issue the same attempt again; using lease expiry as zero-charge evidence can release funds before an old sender or already-delivered request incurs liability. These counterexamples block those candidates, not the project.

review.rationale: The hypothetical arithmetic checks: a hold of 6 under cap 10 leaves 4; settlement at 4 leaves 6; conservative booking at 6 leaves 4. Timeout release followed by another liability of 6 permits total liability 12. These are analytical examples, not measured outcomes.

reasoning_steps.title: 14. Expected, not executed: financial headroom and unsafe controls

reasoning_steps.argument: I examined the supplied incomplete extract of source 1e89585c-2b17-49bd-bb1e-dc1df98ba8ca and the available pointer and ledger scope for target bfcf812f-b3a9-46ff-862c-4d0b4cd76978; neither original was inspected. The source concerns a hypothetical cost/workload comparison, including a scenario with zero additional usable peer capacity. The target's recorded domain concerns new disconnected admissions with neither fresh revocation information nor prior request-specific authorization. These domains overlap only when peer capacity requires such a fresh disconnected admission. A GPU can be nominally idle yet unusable for this request because authorization, approved domain, model fit, connectivity, reservation or deadline eligibility is absent. That logical distinction does not imply that all federation capacity is unusable, or establish economic disadvantage. I adopt it as an admission-accounting requirement, reject transfer of numerical/economic conclusions into this branch, and leave the source's scenario results unverified. It changes the next test: record denial reasons and authorized usable capacity separately from GPU telemetry, without assuming the source's zero-capacity scenario is typical.

review.rationale: The restricted transfer follows from the supplied domains: nominal GPU capacity is not necessarily authorized, reachable, model-fit or deadline-feasible capacity for a particular request. This does not establish the peer's numerical scenario, typical utilization or federation's economic disadvantage.

reasoning_steps.title: 15. Ownership-cost handoff: adopt only the authorized-capacity distinction

reasoning_steps.argument: I examined the supplied incomplete extract of source 2fef1213-38ff-4acf-9af2-a0c28b89b0da and the target's supplied pointer/ledger scope, not the originals. Its proposed paired pilot and statistical gates are not evidence that this adapter is safe. Its partition rationale matches this design only for an admission point lacking authoritative fresh information and an earlier request-specific grant. EXPECTED, NOT EXECUTED paired schedules: (a) a disconnected peer sees identical cached approval in histories with and without a later home revocation; with no prior grant, this design denies both fresh commits; (b) a reachable home authority approving local work is not in that indistinguishable-information domain and may admit it; (c) a grant already committed before partition is not a fresh disconnected authorization, although delivery may fail and liability remains held. Explicitly approved weaker lease semantics would change the revocation contract and require a separate model; they are not adopted here. I adopt the paired partition tests, reject a universal federation-impossibility interpretation, and leave the peer's statistical/sample-size claims outside this refinement. This changes the test matrix, not the chosen decision-time semantics.

review.rationale: The proposed partition cases preserve the recorded scope: fresh disconnected admission without authoritative information differs from reachable home authorization and from an already committed grant. Weaker leases would change the contract. No statistical result is transferred.

reasoning_steps.title: 16. Fairness/reliability handoff: preserve the scoped partition distinction

reasoning_steps.argument: Network enforcement must independently prevent tenant/back-end/tool bypass, arbitrary URLs, alternate credentials, credential exfiltration and unapproved log/telemetry exports; database rows cannot do this. Sender implementation inspection must establish single-continuation execution, no cloning or restore replay, immutable serialization and the actual retry settings of every intermediary. Independent observation must correlate adapter attempts with traffic and mock-provider invocation counts, including existing connections during fencing; finite observations still cannot prove absence of all bypasses. Provider/partner contracts and behavior must establish bounded total liability, authoritative final billing, account/destination identity, retention, subprocessors, deletion and audit obligations. A provider charge above q invalidates the cap premise; detecting it later does not repair the guarantee. Stronger in-flight revocation or cancellation guarantees require additional endpoint cooperation and cannot be inferred from campus placement. Conservative holds can last indefinitely and can themselves cause denial or starvation.

review.rationale: The limitations follow from the trust boundaries: ledger records cannot enforce network mediation, endpoint retention or provider charge ceilings. A charge above the assumed bound invalidates the financial premise, and indefinite uncertainty holds can impair availability and fairness.

reasoning_steps.title: 17. Guarantees that records and schedules cannot supply

reasoning_steps.argument: Next action, when an implementation and observation environment exists: use a non-sensitive mock destination and fault injection at each durable commit/acknowledgement/latch/transport/response boundary; include duplicate acknowledgements, process pause/replacement, stale backup, old-epoch replay, nested-budget contention, fencing of existing connections and hidden SDK/proxy retries. An independent observer should compare the authority log, actual invocation initiations and ledger balances. Include cached-approval, timeout-release and outbox-redelivery negative controls. Any forbidden grant, duplicate initiation, policy bypass or unsupported release stops progression; a finite clean result is bounded support only. Measure safe-denial rates, unresolved-hold duration, suppressed tasks and operator effort. These mechanisms can serve approved API-only access or a gateway with separately approved external access without federation. Federation adds recipient and cross-campus boundaries, so its incremental benefit remains to be measured. Local-only inference still needs tool/log mediation and funded operations. No baseline superiority, affordability, quality, latency or starvation-freedom conclusion follows from this refinement.

review.rationale: Accepted as a proposed experiment and appropriately limited implication, not a result. Boundary fault injection with independent invocation and ledger observation could expose violations. These controls do not inherently require federation, and finite clean tests would provide only bounded support.

reasoning_steps.title: 18. Bounded next action and project implications

strategy_findings.skeptic_response:

A unique durable commit, acknowledgement restricted to its original live continuation, and a one-shot transport latch support at-most-one adapter invocation initiation under the stated sender assumptions. The recovery schedules correctly sacrifice availability rather than reconstruct sending authority, and the financial examples correctly retain coverage through ambiguous outcomes. None were executed.

One concrete recovery alternative remains unsafe as written: retiring an issuer namespace prevents replay but does not restore financial obligations missing from a stale backup. Prior liabilities must also be reconciled or conservatively charged against available budget before any new admission. This challenges step 9's recovery procedure, not the entire conditional claim or federation generally.

Final-liability evidence must also cover a still-possible delayed send, not merely report charges observed so far. The conditional accounting argument assumes this stronger finality; an operational release predicate remains to be established.

The two peer handoffs justify narrowly scoped admission and partition tests, not economic or statistical conclusions. The current packet supplies pointers and ledger summaries, not the earlier abstract-machine definitions; exact refinement correspondence therefore remains unreviewable without those definitions.
