reasoning_steps.argument: Let L denote campus-local only, A approved API only, G the campus gateway plus separately approved external access, and F the proposed federation extension. The supplied scenario has 2,000 monthly root tasks, including 200 sensitive campus-only roots and 1,800 API-eligible roots. Local deadline-feasible admission is 1,000 roots. The supplied MindRouter characterization includes protocol translation, WDRR, quotas, audit logging and GPU telemetry; these descriptions are not independently verified here. Federation and frontier routing remain hypothetical extensions. The project-reported 2026-10-31 reference review is not an access date established in this session. Original artifacts 5c8fdc17-0ce8-4ea3-b8dc-79e05f97d0db and 1e89585c-2b17-49bd-bb1e-dc1df98ba8ca are pointers only; I do not claim to have checked their ledger or full derivations.

review.rationale: The baseline definitions and cohort are explicitly scenario premises, covered by the conditional claim. Published capabilities and the reported review date are appropriately treated as supplied descriptions, not independently established facts.

reasoning_steps.title: Scope, baselines and evidence boundary

reasoning_steps.argument: Index strata s by data classification and task requirements, and destinations d by local, approved API or approved partner. Let N_s be offered roots and n_bds be distinct roots assigned to destination d under baseline b, with sum_d n_bds≤N_s. Unauthorized assignments must have n_bds=0. Let X_bdsj be 1 only if admitted root j completes through an authorized workflow and meets its prespecified quality, deadline and provenance requirements. Define q_bds as the average marginal probability of that joint event among those admissions. Then expected useful completions are μ_b=sum_s,d n_bds q_bds. No independence assumption is needed for this expectation identity. Calls, tool invocations and retries are descendants, not additional completed roots. Probabilities depend on the selected mix, load and configuration; they are not universal model constants.

review.rationale: For distinct assigned roots and a joint useful-completion indicator, summing marginal expectations gives the stated identity. Independence is unnecessary, and counting descendants separately would incorrectly inflate successes.

reasoning_steps.title: Define stratum-specific admissions and usefulness

reasoning_steps.argument: For 200 sensitive and 800 other local admissions, aggregate q_L=0.80 says only 200q_L,S+800q_L,N=800 under an expected-count interpretation. Choosing q_L,S=0 and q_L,N=1 satisfies this equation but yields zero expected sensitive completions. The same construction works as imposed exact counts: 0/200 sensitive and 800/800 other successes give 800/1,000 overall. Thus the aggregate provides no positive lower bound on sensitive successes. Sensitive-first admission does not repair this: admission priority is not task usefulness. This directly accepts the counterexample recorded in o168 and withdraws the unqualified sensitive-feasibility inference identified in o172.

review.rationale: Substitution of q_S=0 and q_N=1 gives 800 aggregate useful roots and zero sensitive usefulness. The exact-count construction has the same property, so neither interpretation supports the old sensitive-coverage inference.

reasoning_steps.title: Accept and reproduce the sensitive-stratum counterexample

reasoning_steps.argument: With n_G,local,S=200, the expected sensitive gate μ_G,S≥160 requires q_G,local,S≥0.80. If sensitive admissions instead equal a_S≤200, the condition is a_S q_G,local,S≥160; it is impossible when a_S<160. To retain the worksheet's 800 expected local completions, a simple explicit repair is q_G,local,S=q_G,local,N=0.80 with 200 and 800 admissions respectively. More generally, retaining the aggregate 800 and assuming q_G,local,S≥0.80 requires q_G,local,N=(800−200q_G,local,S)/800. The sensitive premise is additional and hypothetical, not implied by aggregate q_L.

review.rationale: The expected sensitive gate is exactly a_S q_S≥160. With 200 admissions it requires q_S≥0.80; with fewer than 160 it is impossible since probabilities cannot exceed one. The aggregate-preserving expression for the other stratum is algebraically correct.

reasoning_steps.title: Additional sensitive premise needed for G

reasoning_steps.argument: This repair interprets q values as hypothetical marginal probabilities and μ as expected counts. An imposed exact scenario could instead assign 160 sensitive, 640 other local and 900 API useful completions at 1,000 API admissions, totaling 1,700; those assigned integers describe that scenario only. Exact 0.90 fractions cannot be imposed for every integer admission count without an additional rounding convention. For actual service, let Y_b,S and Y_b be observed useful root counts: the proposed realized gate is Y_b,S≥160 and Y_b≥1,400. Expected counts alone do not imply this gate. For example, a common shock making all 200 sensitive roots succeed with probability 0.80 and all fail with probability 0.20 has the assumed marginals and expectation 160, yet fails coverage with probability 0.20. No distribution, confidence or predictive guarantee is established.

review.rationale: Assigned integer totals, expected totals and observed service gates are correctly separated. The common-shock example has marginal success probability 0.80 for each sensitive root but a 0.20 probability of zero sensitive completions, directly disproving a realized guarantee from the expectation.

reasoning_steps.title: Separate exact scenarios, expectations and realized service

reasoning_steps.argument: For L and G, retain the hypothetical local plan of 200 sensitive plus 800 other roots. G may admit up to 1,000 remaining, distinct API-eligible roots. A admits no sensitive roots and up to 1,800 eligible roots. For the cap formulas only, additionally assume average API usefulness remains 0.90 for each selected admission cohort, including cap-truncated cohorts; an aggregate API fraction at full admission would not justify this extrapolation. The illustrative F dominance case uses the same local/API plan as G and zero usable extra partner admissions. F's possible approval for some partner work is not usable capacity and does not expand sensitive permissions.

review.rationale: These are explicit conditional admission and selected-cohort usefulness premises, not deductions from aggregate quality. Requiring 0.90 for each cap-selected API cohort avoids the same aggregation error repaired locally.

reasoning_steps.title: Make the repaired admission plans explicit

reasoning_steps.argument: Assume a common positive enforceable maximum API liability r per admitted root, no opening liability or commitment, nonbinding subsidiary quotas, sufficient API capacity and no recycling of reservation savings. Define m_G(B)=min(1,000,floor(B/r)) and m_A(B)=min(1,800,floor(B/r)). Then L has (μ_S,μ_total)=(160,800); A has (0,0.90m_A); G has (160,800+0.90m_G); and F has the same expected counts as G in the scoped no-extra-service case. L fails the overall 1,400 gate. A fails sensitive coverage at every cap, even though its maximum overall expectation is 1,620. G and scoped F pass both expected-count gates iff m_G≥ceil((1,400−800)/0.90)=667. These are feasibility results for the declared plans and assumptions, not an optimization over every possible routing plan.

review.rationale: Under the uniform enforceable envelope and stated quota/capacity assumptions, the admission formulas follow. Since 600/0.90 is 666⅔ and the residual limit is 1,000, the expected total gate is equivalent to at least 667 API admissions. The exclusion of other routing plans is explicit.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive the cap-dependent expected comparison

reasoning_steps.argument: At B=0, no paid roots are admitted and none of these plans passes both expected gates. At B=$2,000, $4,000 or $8,000, G and scoped F pass iff r≤B/667: respectively about $2.9985, $5.9970 or $11.9940 of maximum reserved liability per root. These are derived reservation thresholds, not API prices or measured average task costs. If r exceeds the applicable threshold, no baseline in this scoped comparison passes; if the sensitive premise is absent, G and F cannot be certified even when the cap is sufficient. If r is unknown or unenforceable, paid admission is not justified by this rule. Zero API budget also does not make local operation free: local service still requires approved operating resources.

review.rationale: For positive r, floor(B/r)≥667 is equivalent to r≤B/667. The rounded thresholds are correct, and neither an unknown liability bound nor zero API budget is represented as establishing free or authorized operation.

reasoning_steps.title: Budget scenarios and the corrected feasible-baseline rule

reasoning_steps.argument: For a fixed admission plan with expected local usefulness μ_L=a_S q_L,S+a_N q_L,N and positive API usefulness q_A, the expected gate requires a_S q_L,S≥160 and k=max(0,ceil((1,400−μ_L)/q_A)) additional API roots. It is feasible under the conservative envelope only if k does not exceed the distinct eligible residual demand or available API capacity and rk≤B. If q_A=0, API calls cannot close a positive shortfall. If admissions or usefulness change with demand, overload, model fit or selection, recompute by stratum rather than extending the 667 threshold. Among plans passing policy, capacity, budget and declared performance gates, compare fully loaded cost; do not choose a cheap plan that fails a mandatory stratum.

review.rationale: For a fixed plan and positive selected-cohort q_A, the ceiling expression is the smallest integer admission count closing the expected shortfall. Sensitive coverage, residual demand, technical capacity and reservation feasibility remain separate necessary checks.

reasoning_steps.title: General rule when local strata or API quality differ

reasoning_steps.argument: Let C_G be cost on one explicitly chosen accounting basis and let F add overhead H>0. If F offers exactly the same usable service opportunities, approvals and non-federation entitlements as G, no additional peer service, and no offsetting reliability, scheduling or administrative benefit, G can reproduce F's useful outcomes without the federation overhead. Hence C_F=C_G+H>C_G while usefulness and feasibility are equal. For positive useful counts, G also has lower cost per useful completion. The result holds for fully loaded cost when H is fully loaded overhead; an incremental-cost claim additionally requires avoidable incremental H>0. Zero extra GPU capacity alone is insufficient if federation changes another useful service dimension. This dominance does not depend on whether the sensitive gate passes, but G's least-cost feasible status does.

review.rationale: Identical service opportunities and no offsetting benefit permit the same usefulness while positive H raises cost. The argument correctly distinguishes fully loaded overhead from avoidable incremental overhead and does not infer dominance from zero extra GPU capacity alone.

reasoning_steps.title: Retain only scoped G-over-F dominance

reasoning_steps.argument: Keep input, cached-input, output, embedding, tool and egress prices symbolic and undated until evidence is obtained. For each permitted workflow attempt j, reserve at least [I_j^max max(p_uncached,j^upper,p_cached,j^upper)+O_j^max p_output,j^upper]/10^6, plus enforceable upper ancillary charges. I_j^max includes all inputs, including candidates for caching; cache eligibility or a predicted cache hit never reduces the envelope below uncached exposure. Sum over bounded Investigator/Skeptic, agent, tool and permitted retry attempts, including repeated context, and include applicable tax, currency, commitment and other contractual liabilities without double counting. The per-root r must dominate this total. Missing finite bounds, unlimited descendants or unbounded price changes block the hard-cap argument. Actual cached discounts may lower settled cost after reconciliation, but are not assumed savings available for admission in this conservative worksheet.

review.rationale: Pricing every possible input token at the larger applicable upper rate covers uncached exposure. Summing over bounded attempts and ancillary liabilities gives a conditional envelope, not a current price estimate. Missing enforceable bounds appropriately invalidate the hard-cap argument.

reasoning_steps.title: Unknown prices and a cache-miss-safe reservation envelope

reasoning_steps.argument: A candidate ordering is: bind an immutable request manifest to authoritative identity and inherited classifications; check allowed destinations and retention/audit requirements; atomically prepare reservations at every applicable user/project/department/campus scope; then serialize current policy, cancellation/revocation state, reservation ownership and a one-use dispatch grant at a home-authority commit point. Merely checking policy before dispatch leaves a concurrent-revocation race. The system still needs crash-safe grant consumption, sender fencing, durable recovery and explicit semantics for a grant committed before revocation but transmitted later. Decision-time semantics permit that later transmission only if campus authorities explicitly accept it; they are not a no-post-revocation-delivery guarantee. Ambiguity or loss of authoritative access denies/defer new external grants. Timeout and cancellation requests do not release unresolved liability; retransmission or retry requires a bounded, authorized attempt and cannot silently escalate to paid or disallowed destinations. These transitions, including separately approved accounts, are proposed, not implemented or campus-approved.

review.rationale: As a proposed specification and explicit limitation, this is appropriately scoped: a pre-dispatch check alone does not order concurrent revocation, and a committed grant is not a delivery-time guarantee. The step leaves fencing, recovery and campus acceptance open rather than claiming safety.

reasoning_steps.title: Authorization-to-dispatch ordering remains an implementation obligation

reasoning_steps.argument: For handoff dd628675-9b61-4bce-9acf-0999f3290da6, I examined the supplied extract of f5e8dea1-e0d1-4076-bf15-3ea3c2f345bc against the scenario assumptions and ledger descriptions associated with target 5c8fdc17-0ce8-4ea3-b8dc-79e05f97d0db. The target original is unavailable, so full source-to-target verification remains open. Root-task accounting, complete financial mediation, bounded liabilities and nested reservations are compatible. However, the source additionally assumes a linearizable home authority, trusted request binding, one-use issuance and campus acceptance of decision-time authorization. Those are stronger than the economic worksheet and cannot be silently transferred as established premises. I adopt the machine as a method to test, not a safety result or evidence of economic benefit. This changes the next specification test: include revocation/grant/dispatch and crash orderings, and obtain campus acceptance of in-flight semantics before counting remotely served roots as authorized useful completions.

review.rationale: The supplied sovereignty assumptions explicitly add a linearizable home authority, trusted binding, mediated issuance and accepted decision-time semantics. Restricting transfer to a method for local testing is justified; the unavailable target original prevents stronger historical validation.

reasoning_steps.title: Sovereignty handoff: compatible semantics, narrower transfer

reasoning_steps.argument: For handoff b5946156-a3c9-4f8c-aba9-c809e329964f, the supplied extract of 2fef1213-38ff-4acf-9af2-a0c28b89b0da proposes paired root-task evaluation with identical non-federation entitlements and separate operational gates. This is compatible with the fixed-workload economic domain described for target 5c8fdc17-0ce8-4ea3-b8dc-79e05f97d0db, but its IID-pair or independent-block assumptions do not follow for live campus workloads. Independently, for the same horizon, workload, acceptance rules and cost basis, C_G>0, S_G>0, ΔC>0 and S_G+ΔS>0 imply (C_G+ΔC)/(S_G+ΔS)<C_G/S_G iff ΔS>S_GΔC/C_G, by cross multiplication. Thus positive completion gain alone is insufficient. I adopt separate measurement of incremental and fully loaded costs and paired authorized useful outcomes; I do not adopt the peer's proposed 0.10 gain gate or truncated planning numbers as an economic threshold. The next pilot specification must predeclare the estimand, sampling dependence, cost allocation and uncertainty rule. No peer result is independently verified.

review.rationale: The peer's paired or independent-block assumptions do not follow for arbitrary live workloads. Independently cross-multiplying positive denominators gives C_GΔS>S_GΔC, establishing the economic threshold without relying on truncated peer calculations or its proposed 0.10 gate.

reasoning_steps.title: Fairness/pilot handoff: completion gains are not cost-effectiveness

reasoning_steps.argument: The contribution is a logical repair and a reproducible symbolic decision rule: separate admission, useful completion, sensitive coverage and financial feasibility before comparing cost. Standard expectation accounting and algebra supply the derivations; material novelty and empirical generality are not assessed. The ledger's o138/o168/o169/o172/o173 inference issues are addressed analytically for the newly explicit scenario, not empirically resolved. Source, cost, implementation, legal and pilot obligations remain open. The saved itemized ledger need not be repeated to perform this repair, but its original must be inspected before reusing its numerical totals or recommending procurement.

review.rationale: The current derivations repair the identified inference and interpretation problems for a changed, explicit scenario. The step correctly limits that contribution and leaves empirical, source and implementation obligations open. It does not certify the absent historical ledger.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Evidence boundary and changes from the previous proposal

reasoning_steps.argument: G provides campus-local inference through the gateway and a separately approved external workflow; F adds approved remote-campus execution. Federation and frontier routing remain hypothetical extensions, not asserted MindRouter features. Both arms use identical home-campus classification, identity, retention, audit and destination rules, local resource allocations, paid-access entitlements and parent-task spending limits. F receives the declared additional remote capacity, whose operating and agreement costs are counted rather than treated as free. Separate external access must still have complete financial mediation if the earlier hard-cap argument is invoked. Approval alone is insufficient. No outage, model mismatch, better score, cancellation or budget exhaustion authorizes a new destination. Ambiguous classification fails closed. Revalidate policy and reserve funds before every billable subcall; retain unresolved liabilities. Public or synthetic tasks are used until all relevant campuses approve real-data processing.

review.rationale: As a proposed comparison, matching non-federation entitlements isolates the addition of remote capacity. Explicit financial mediation and policy-first eligibility avoid treating approval or failure as sufficient authorization.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Arms, policy boundaries and comparable resources

reasoning_steps.argument: A parent task is one registered research objective with an input snapshot, requested output, rubric, deadline, policy classification, provenance requirements and total resource envelope. Agent calls, tools, retries and reproducibility repeats are children, not additional tasks. Before routing, register every submitted parent task and distinguish: N_requested, all requests; N_authorized, requests with adequate classification and home-campus permission for at least one studied path; N_pair, authorized tasks permitted to undergo both G and F evaluation under the signed study manifest; and N_admitted,b, actual admissions in arm b. Primary success rates use the same fixed N_pair in both arms, not only admitted or completed tasks. Model fit, queue rejection, paid-cap exhaustion and outages are outcomes, not post hoc exclusions. Permission to enter both arms does not require that a compatible remote GPU exists. Tasks prohibited from paired evaluation are reported with reason and arm-specific coverage, never exported merely for comparability. This estimand is limited to the declared paired population; report N_pair/N_requested so selective eligibility is visible.

review.rationale: A common preregistered paired denominator prevents admission and completion filtering from inflating arm success. Reporting requested, authorized, paired and admitted counts exposes eligibility selection and limits the estimand's scope.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Parent-task registry and denominators

reasoning_steps.argument: For parent i in arm b define Y_ib=1 only if the final artifact satisfies its frozen quality rubric, required provenance record, authorized processing and end-to-end deadline; otherwise Y_ib=0. Proposed deadlines for approval are coding 120 seconds, routine analysis 5 minutes, demanding scientific reasoning 30 minutes, multimodal/long-context work 15 minutes, agentic workflows 60 minutes and reproducible batches 24 hours. They are illustrative service targets, not measurements or university policy. Sensitive-data tasks inherit their functional deadline and stricter domain restrictions. Coding requires registered tests and critical-correctness checks; analysis requires domain-specific numerical checks; scientific reasoning requires expert assessment of the substantive conclusion and evidence; multimodal work requires task-specific references; agents must meet the objective without unauthorized actions; reproducible batches require a registered rerun/tolerance criterion. Faculty and students must approve explicit pass rules and critical-failure criteria before enrollment. Two blinded assessors score artifacts independently, with a third adjudicator resolving disagreement; report agreement and ambiguous judgments. Latency starts at submission to the assigned workflow and includes approval handling, queueing, cold starts, tools, retries and recovery, ending at delivery of the completed artifact, not the first streamed token. Later human grading does not extend delivery latency. Required provenance includes available model/version, configuration, prompts, tools and retrieval snapshots; a version label alone does not establish reproducibility.

review.rationale: Success is conjunctive in quality, provenance, authorization and delivery deadline. End-to-end latency includes workflow delays rather than only generation time. The numerical deadlines and incomplete pass rules are correctly presented as proposals awaiting approval.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Define success before viewing results

reasoning_steps.argument: Each primary parent receives one G execution and one F execution with the same input and rubric. Randomize execution order within campus, task class, policy class and load block using a preregistered seed. Prevent answer sharing and shared cross-arm caches. Use isolated capacity slices with identical registered background arrivals, or separate matched replay windows; do not let duplicate study calls compete in one queue and then claim ordinary-service latency. Include declared peak, cold-start and maintenance conditions rather than reporting only warmed idle service. Lock model and workflow versions where possible and record changes. Repeats assess reproducibility separately and do not enlarge N_pair. Budget rejection, timeout, provider rejection, post-dispatch cancellation and non-delivery by the deadline remain failures in the primary requested-service analysis. Pre-dispatch withdrawal after enrollment remains in that denominator, with a separate withdrawal analysis; do not replace difficult tasks selectively. Missing required grading/provenance records count as not demonstrated successful in the primary analysis, accompanied by best/worst-case sensitivity. End enrollment sufficiently early for the longest deadline and grading before day 90. An early safety stop ends the efficacy claim as inconclusive; it does not justify analyzing only favorable completed pairs.

review.rationale: The pairing, cache isolation and matched-load requirements address leakage and interference. Keeping rejection, non-delivery and missing required evidence in the primary denominator prevents favorable complete-case selection. These remain proposed controls, not demonstrated execution fidelity.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Pairing, load, stopping and missing outcomes

reasoning_steps.argument: Within the frozen primary population let p10=P(Y_F=1,Y_G=0), p01=P(Y_F=0,Y_G=1), q=p10+p01 and Δ=E(Y_F−Y_G)=p10−p01. Thus Δ=0.10 means ten additional useful, on-time completions per 100 eligible parent tasks, net of tasks harmed by federation; it is neither a 10% relative increase nor a token-throughput gain. With n pairs and counts n10,n01, estimate Δ by (n10−n01)/n. Let D=Y_F−Y_G, taking values −1,0,1. Since D²=1 exactly on discordant pairs, E(D²)=q and Var(D)=q−Δ². For independent pairs, Var(mean D)=(q−Δ²)/n. This derivation explains why uncertainty depends on discordance rather than on two independent-arm binomial variances. Both-concordant outcomes still belong in n.

review.rationale: D takes values −1, 0 and 1, so E(D²)=p10+p01=q and Var(D)=q−Δ². Dividing by n is justified for independent identically sampled pairs, not arbitrary live-service observations.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. The paired estimand and its variance

reasoning_steps.argument: For the single primary stratum use α=0.05. Obtain a two-sided Clopper–Pearson binomial interval [L10,U10] for n10 out of n with confidence 1−α/2, and independently calculate [L01,U01] at the same confidence level. Each marginal count is binomial under independent identically sampled pairs; the two counts need not be independent. The union bound gives joint coverage at least 1−α. Therefore [max(−1,L10−U01), min(1,U10−L01)] covers Δ with probability at least 0.95. Compute each binomial interval by inverting the binomial tails, with lower endpoint zero for zero successes and upper endpoint one for n successes. These endpoint conventions handle all-concordant and boundary samples; n=0 yields no inference. This procedure uses the paired discordance categories and is conservative. A sign/McNemar test alone is not the decision procedure because testing Δ=0 does not supply evidence that Δ exceeds 0.10. Do not substitute a zero-width Wald interval when no discordances occur.

review.rationale: Each discordance count has a binomial marginal under the stated model. Two intervals with failure probability α/2 each have joint coverage at least 1−α by the union bound, regardless of their dependence; subtracting endpoints therefore gives valid conservative coverage for Δ.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Prespecified paired uncertainty procedure

reasoning_steps.argument: For planning only, set true Δ=0.10 and hypothetical q values 0.20, 0.40 and 0.60. These imply valid (p10,p01) values (0.15,0.05), (0.25,0.15) and (0.35,0.25). The efficient large-sample paired-normal half-width is approximately 1.96 sqrt((q−0.01)/n). At n=30 these are about 0.156, 0.223 and 0.275; at n=400 they are about 0.043, 0.061 and 0.075. To target half-width 0.05, this approximation gives n≥ceil(1.96²(q−0.01)/0.05²), namely 292, 600 and 907 pairs. These are optimistic reference calculations, not the sample requirements of the conservative primary interval. For that interval, away from boundaries its approximate half-width is 2.2414[ sqrt(p10(1−p10))+sqrt(p01(1−p01)) ]/sqrt(n), because each marginal interval has 97.5% confidence. This gives roughly 665, 1,255 and 1,665 pairs for half-width 0.05 in the three scenarios. Values are hand-evaluated approximations; binomial discreteness and finite-sample corrections require exact evaluation before enrollment. None is a measured discordance rate, power result or guarantee.

review.rationale: The proposed probabilities are valid and have Δ=0.10. Substitution into the variance and normal-width formulas reproduces the reported rounded values and approximate sample sizes. The text properly separates these hand approximations from exact interval requirements and measured discordance.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Explicitly hypothetical precision scenarios

reasoning_steps.argument: If the true Δ equals 0.10, a valid 95% interval can put its lower endpoint above 0.10 only on a coverage failure, with probability at most 0.05 under the stated model. No sample-size increase gives 80% power to establish a strict improvement beyond a margin when truth lies exactly on that margin. Power planning must posit a larger benefit. For illustration, under true Δ=0.20 and hypothetical q=0.40, p10=0.30, p01=0.10 and Var(D)=0.36. A normal approximation to the actual conservative gate gives n approximately [(2.2414(sqrt(0.21)+sqrt(0.09))+0.84 sqrt(0.36))/(0.20−0.10)]², about 486 pairs for 80% power. This is not exact. The exact planning calculation sums the multinomial probabilities for (n10,n01,n−n10−n01), with probabilities p10,p01,1−q, over count combinations whose interval lower bound exceeds 0.10. That finite calculation, plus affordability and dependence checks, must be completed before a fixed N is signed. A provisional planning envelope is up to 1,700 primary pairs to explore five-point precision in these scenarios; it is not a promise that the 90-day budget or capacity can support them. If the affordable N is smaller, register the attainable precision and allow an explicitly inconclusive pilot rather than weaken the gate after observation.

review.objection: The inference is valid as an approximation and planning method, but the actual gate's power and an affordable fixed N remain unresolved; this step does not make the protocol enrollment-ready.
review.rationale: At truth Δ=0.10, a lower confidence bound above 0.10 entails noncoverage, so high power at the boundary is impossible for a valid interval. The alternative probabilities and approximate 486-pair calculation are internally consistent, and multinomial summation describes the exact gate-power calculation.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Precision is not power to exceed the margin

reasoning_steps.argument: Many prompts from one researcher, templates, repeat executions and tasks exposed to the same outage are not independent new evidence. Before collection, define workload blocks and researcher/template clusters; seek distinct parent objectives rather than many variants of one prompt. The exact binomial procedure is confirmatory only if the independent-pair sampling model is defensible for the stated population. Otherwise use a prespecified independent-block analysis: for each block form its average paired difference X_j in [−1,1], retain equal block weights as the target estimand, and use the finite-sample interval mean(X) ± sqrt(2 log(2/α)/m), clipped to [−1,1], for m independent blocks. Hoeffding's inequality gives coverage at least 1−α because each block average has range two. This changes the estimand to the average block effect and must be declared, not silently substituted for task weighting. For m=30 and α=0.05 the half-width is about 0.496; about 2,952 independent blocks are sufficient for half-width at most 0.05 under this conservative bound. If even block independence is unsupported, report finite-window paired differences descriptively without a population confidence claim. Controlled replay and live-service results remain separate: neither proves the other's generality.

review.rationale: For independent block averages in [−1,1], Hoeffding gives radius sqrt(2 log(2/α)/m). The stated approximately 0.496 radius and 2,952-block sufficient count follow. The change to equal-block weighting and the absence of inference without defensible independence are explicit.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Dependence and limits of population inference

reasoning_steps.argument: Before outcome collection choose one primary underserved campus/task/policy population from inventory and expressed research needs, not observed federation wins. For mutually exclusive task classes, assign the principal deliverable before routing; sensitive status, campus and interactive/batch status are additional registered tags. Report all requested task categories, including those with no lawful paired sample. The primary comparison uses its single 95% interval. Secondary strata are descriptive unless a confirmatory family of K strata is signed in advance; for simultaneous family coverage use the same interval construction with α/K per stratum. An exploratory successful subgroup cannot replace a failed primary population. Provisional bounded-scope go requires the primary lower bound >0.10, at least 80% observed useful/on-time success in the supported primary stratum, the service and safety gates, and campus-approved incremental and fully loaded administrative-cost ceilings. Report uncertainty around absolute success and availability as well; these observed operational gates are not population guarantees. If the upper bound is ≤0.10, the registered >10-point benefit criterion is not met; if the interval crosses 0.10, data are missing, or independent sample size is inadequate, classify efficacy as inconclusive. An upper bound below zero supports harm in that population. Any authorization or accounting violation triggers immediate remote-routing suspension regardless of efficacy. For both no-go and inconclusive outcomes retain G as the default, without claiming federation is universally inferior. No efficacy peeking or optional stopping; continuous safety monitoring is mandatory.

review.rationale: Preregistering one primary population prevents subgroup replacement. Using α/K yields simultaneous coverage by a further union bound. The three-way decision separates demonstrated margin benefit, failure to meet that criterion and inconclusive evidence; observed operational gates are not promoted to population guarantees.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Strata, multiplicity and the three-way decision

reasoning_steps.argument: Evaluate fairness separately within compatible GPU/model/memory pools and registered interactive/batch capacity partitions; raw tokens across heterogeneous models are not comparable service units. Computing records charged GPU-seconds, estimation errors, backlog, fit, weights and home-campus quotas. Integrate a frozen hierarchical weighted, demand-limited reference allocation over time: department entitlement first, project within department, user within project. Only policy-eligible, funded, compatible backlog earns entitlement, using the declared capacity offered to that service; do not erase outages or maintenance from the accompanying availability denominator. Measure actual service S and reference entitlement E, including boundary-crossing jobs and scheduler deficits. Evaluate rolling seven-calendar-day windows daily only when they contain at least 40 declared service hours, compatible available-service time at least ten times the maximum permitted non-preemptive blocking time, and E at least 100 maximum scheduling quanta for the tenant under review. Otherwise extend to 14 and then 28 days; if still insufficient, label fairness unassessed rather than passed. These are proposed diagnostic windows, not WDRR guarantees. Flag S/E<0.80 for investigation, report every deadline violation and maximum no-service backlog age, and inspect daily so a weekly average cannot hide interactive starvation. If blocking or work size cannot be bounded, do not claim a positive waiting-time guarantee. Also report policy-ineligible, unfunded and unfit demand separately; excluding it from share fairness must not conceal lack of useful access.

review.rationale: Compatible-pool accounting avoids treating heterogeneous tokens as interchangeable service. Explicit minimum exposure, window extension and an unassessed outcome prevent unsupported fairness passes. Daily backlog diagnostics address failures that weekly averages could hide; the reference allocation still needs executable specification.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Fairness denominator and observation window

reasoning_steps.argument: Days 1–15: computing inventories compatible GPU memory, model fit, queues and maintenance; security/legal define approved domains and classification; procurement/finance establish dated prices, liability bounds and reconciliation; faculty/students approve rubrics, deadlines and accessibility. Days 16–30: instrument both workflows, test public/synthetic tasks and the fault matrix, choose the primary population without outcome-based subgroup selection, evaluate exact sample-size scenarios and sign fixed N, analysis, budgets and administrative ceilings. Days 31–60: measure local-only, approved-API-only and G descriptively under their lawful scopes, and prepare approved federation capacity. Earlier G observations are not substitutes for contemporaneous primary pairs. Days 61–90: conduct the registered F/G paired comparison only if approvals and fault gates pass, ending enrollment before all deadlines and grading must close. Computing owns latency, throughput, availability and fairness; faculty own blinded quality; security owns egress/retention checks; finance owns settled charges and held liabilities; service management logs staff hours, agreements and incidents. Proposed operational gates retain at least 99% observed availability during declared service hours, with maintenance additionally counted against the full requested window, and zero observed unauthorized transmissions or cap violations. Test stale policy, malicious identities, WAN/home/remote/provider outages, charged timeouts, cancellation, concurrent reservations and prohibited fallback. Zero observed failures remains bounded evidence, not a safety proof. Funding must cover both executions and all child calls; study duplication is separately attributed and not hidden in ordinary cost-per-task. Zero paid budget permits no positive-charge admission, even to reach a sample-size target.

review.rationale: The staged schedule assigns measurement owners and gates primary pairing on approvals and fault tests. It correctly excludes historical G observations as substitutes for contemporaneous pairs, accounts for duplicate study work and does not allow sample targets to override zero paid budget.

reasoning_steps.title: 13. Ninety-day execution, owners and resource feasibility

reasoning_steps.argument: Report paired gains alongside monthly and annual sunk, incremental and fully loaded costs, active-researcher counts and cost per successful parent task; a statistically positive gain is not automatically economical. The supplied peer extract 5c8fdc17-0ce8-4ea3-b8dc-79e05f97d0db emphasizes this distinction, but its original and numerical example were not inspected and are not adopted as measured evidence. The supplied peer extract bfcf812f-b3a9-46ff-862c-4d0b4cd76978 concerns disconnected remote authorization with immediate home-campus revocation and no fresh information. Its warning is compatible with fail-closed remote admission; it does not prove all locally authorized egress or weaker approved lease models unavailable. Adopt both extracts only as prompts for cost and partition tests; leave their broader claims unverified. The project's descriptions of MindRouter protocol translation, WDRR, quotas, audit and telemetry are unverified background here. The required documentation and PEARC'26 paper still need actual access dates and version checks at https://mindrouter.ai/documentation.html and https://ai4ra.uidaho.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Sheneman_MindRouter_PEARC26_Short_Paper.pdf. The date 2026-10-31 is project-reported prior review, not this session's access date. This design adds statistical and operational specificity; novelty against established evaluation methods and empirical generality are not assessed.

review.rationale: The supplied peer scopes support treating economics and disconnected authorization as separate constraints, not empirical validation. The proposal does not transfer the partition limitation to models with fresh local authorization or approved weaker leases, and correctly leaves source access and novelty unassessed.

reasoning_steps.title: 14. Cost, peer evidence and source verification remain separate gates

strategy_findings.skeptic_response:
The analytical core is sound. The paired-difference variance, conservative discordance-based confidence interval, multiplicity correction and independent-block bound follow under their stated sampling models. The hand-calculated planning values are consistent with the formulas. The revised gate correctly distinguishes evidence of any improvement from evidence that the improvement exceeds 10 percentage points. It also correctly treats inadequate precision as inconclusive rather than evidence of equivalence.

This substantially addresses the cycle's design question, but does not yet produce an enrollment-ready protocol. The task-specific pass rules, primary population, independent sampling unit, fixed sample size, budget feasibility and fairness reference allocation remain unsigned or unspecified. In particular, the approximate power calculation is not the power of the exact conservative decision procedure. A final design needs either that exact calculation when a runtime becomes available or a conservative analytic guarantee—not another restatement of the proposal.

The cycle preserves the useful cycle-1 constraints: unresolved liabilities cannot be released merely after timeout or cancellation, and WDRR weights alone do not establish latency or starvation guarantees. No source access, execution, current-price verification, campus approval or empirical federation result occurred. The project objective therefore remains partial. The next cycle should close the analytic planning gap without inventing campus inputs: derive a conservative fixed-sample sufficient bound for the actual confidence-bound gate and give an explicit rule for declaring the pilot underpowered or unaffordable.

research-sessions/36e06a52-e138-48ee-9cc.problem:
Can universities with uneven GPU capacity provide useful, reliable AI research access while retaining control of sensitive data and staying within hard budgets? Compare four baselines: (1) campus-local inference only, (2) approved frontier API only, (3) a campus gateway with separately approved external access, and (4) a proposed cooperative federation among campuses. Treat federation and frontier routing as hypothetical extensions, not existing MindRouter features.

Ground the investigation in MindRouter's published campus gateway: protocol translation across OpenAI/Ollama/Anthropic clients and Ollama/vLLM backends; WDRR fair-share scheduling; per-user quotas; audit logging; and GPU telemetry. Its documentation describes an on-campus service, not a multi-institution federation. Start with its documentation (https://mindrouter.ai/documentation.html) and PEARC'26 short paper (https://ai4ra.uidaho.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Sheneman_MindRouter_PEARC26_Short_Paper.pdf); record access dates (the starting references were reviewed on 2026-10-31), distinguish published claims from independently measured facts, and verify any changed claims against current sources.

Design a policy-first admission and routing study for varied tasks: classroom coding, routine analysis, demanding scientific reasoning, multimodal/long-context work, agentic multi-call workflows, sensitive data, and reproducible batches. Each campus must retain authority over identity, data classification, approved destinations, retention, audit policy, contracts and quotas. Restricted, student, patient, controlled, sponsor-restricted and unpublished data—including derived prompts, outputs, logs, embeddings and cache—must remain inside approved domains by default. Ambiguous classification fails closed. Outage, overload, timeout, retry, cost exhaustion or a better score must never silently bypass policy.

Compare task completion quality, provenance/version reproducibility, latency, throughput, availability and administrative burden. Include heterogeneous GPU memory/model fit, queues, cold starts, maintenance, peak demand, batch vs interactive service, per-campus autonomy, cross-campus agreements, fairness and starvation. Propose a minimal deployable architecture and routing rule, but test when campus-only service plus separately approved frontier access is simpler and safer than federation. Identify trust boundaries and adversarial cases: stale policy, malicious tenant, WAN partition, campus/provider outage, provider rejection, ambiguous charged timeout, cancellation, quota contention and unsafe fallback.

Build transparent total-cost models. For local capacity include GPU purchase and depreciation, replacement, utilization and idle capacity, power, cooling, storage, network, hardware support, procurement and staff operations. For APIs include current dated input/output/cached-token prices, repeated Investigator/Skeptic or agent calls, retries, tools/embeddings, egress and minimum commitments. Separate sunk, incremental and fully loaded cost. State every assumption, distinguish measured values from hypothetical scenarios, and report annual/monthly totals, cost per active researcher and cost per successfully completed useful research task at a stated quality and latency target. Explore break-even, utilization, quality, price, demand and capacity sensitivity. An illustrative $4,000/month shared frontier cap (sensitivities $2,000/$8,000) is a scenario only, not measured campus spending. Include zero/no-budget operation, reservations before calls, per-user/project/department limits, attribution, alerts, budget exhaustion and no paid retry escalation.

Deliver a bounded comparison, uncertainty register, counterexamples, measurable 90-day pilot, stop/go thresholds and questions for campus computing, security, procurement, faculty and students. Do not invent prices, workload traces, evaluation results or university policy. An architecture proposal or agent consensus is not deployment evidence; report what would require real campus measurements and legal/security review.

reasoning_steps.argument: Let H be the home-campus authority and E an admission point considering a new operation that would disclose campus-controlled content to destination D. E possesses an earlier approval snapshot. During a partition, E cannot receive information about subsequent H policy changes through any channel. The request has no previously committed, request-specific authorization exempting it from subsequent revocation. Immediate revocation means that requests whose authorization decisions occur after H's revocation takes effect must be denied. Partition availability means E can authorize a new, otherwise eligible request during the partition when H has not revoked approval. These are alternative requirements to test, not established university policy.
reasoning_steps.title: 1. Define the authorization and partition model

reasoning_steps.argument: In execution A, H approves D, the partition begins, and H leaves approval unchanged. In execution B, the same approval and partition occur, but H then revokes D before E receives the new request. Give E the same request, identity credentials, cached policy, clock readings, and local state in both executions. Because no revocation information reaches E, its observations are identical. A signed cached policy authenticates its historical issuer and contents; it does not distinguish these two executions.
reasoning_steps.title: 2. Construct the indistinguishable executions

reasoning_steps.argument: A deterministic E makes the same decision in both executions. If it admits in A to provide partition availability, it admits in B and violates immediate revocation. If it denies in B to guarantee safety, it must also deny in A. For randomized E, couple the random choices: the admission probability is identical in both executions. Zero probability of unauthorized admission in B therefore requires zero admission probability in A. Deferral until authoritative contact returns preserves safety but does not provide the defined partition availability. This proves the claim within the stated model.
reasoning_steps.title: 3. Derive the safety–availability limitation

reasoning_steps.argument: An unexpired lease changes the authorization semantics only if the campus has explicitly agreed that revocation may wait until lease expiry; a time-to-live alone does not deliver immediate revocation. A connected home-controlled admission service avoids the disconnected-authorizer premise. Previously disclosed data cannot be recalled by denying a later request. Authorization and revocation can be ordered at a home authority's decision point, but this does not establish that bytes cannot arrive remotely after a later revocation. A policy requiring no delivery, retention, or execution after revocation needs stronger destination cooperation and separate treatment of in-flight work. None of these cases refutes the scoped limitation.
reasoning_steps.title: 4. State edge cases and limits explicitly

reasoning_steps.argument: For the proposed study, enumerate client to gateway, gateway to local backend, gateway to partner or API, backend to tool, and every path to logs, caches, embeddings, storage, telemetry, and returned outputs. Each edge needs a responsible campus authority, authenticated principal, data classification, approved destination and purpose, retention rule, audit rule, and failure disposition. Derived content conservatively inherits the applicable restrictions of its inputs unless an authorized transformation or review changes that classification; unknown or incompatible classifications stop processing at an approved quarantine boundary. Verification must precede sensitive payload transfer: checking authorization at a partner only after sending the prompt is already too late. Campus-local placement alone does not establish acceptable access, retention, or logging.
reasoning_steps.title: 5. Extend the boundary map beyond the model endpoint

reasoning_steps.argument: Retain a home-campus identity and policy authority, local gateway/backends, restricted audit store, and budget ledger. Put all optional external egress through a controlled adapter; deny direct tenant/backend network paths that would bypass it. Normalize protocol requests without dropping policy-relevant attachments, tool instructions, or metadata; reject unsupported semantics. Before each external disclosure, including each agent tool call, require authorization bound to principal, project, operation identifier, destination, content/classification, policy version, retention conditions, and bounded resource use. Serialize authorization decisions against revocation at the authoritative decision point; expire unused decisions and reject replay. A disconnected enforcement point cannot mint fresh authority from a cached allow-list. WDRR and quotas can allocate service among eligible operations, but cannot make an ineligible destination eligible. These controls are proposed requirements; their implementation and complete mediation remain unverified.
reasoning_steps.title: 6. Propose a minimal enforcement design, without attributing it to MindRouter

reasoning_steps.argument: The proposed state machine is classify, authorize, reserve, dispatch, then reconcile; any fallback is a new candidate operation that repeats the checks. Provider rejection, outage, overload, or a better model score cannot enlarge the approved destination set. An ambiguous charged timeout must retain its outstanding reservation until reconciled, not be treated as a free failed call. Cancellation stops future issuance but does not imply cancellation of remote work or charges. Atomic reservations must cover all applicable user, project, department, and campus limits using an enforceable upper bound on the operation's possible charge. If that bound or authoritative remaining budget is unavailable, paid dispatch is denied. A zero paid budget therefore permits no paid calls; local execution still consumes resources and requires its own limits. Retry is not automatic permission to spend again. These are design constraints, not verified properties of any provider or gateway.
reasoning_steps.title: 7. Preserve policy and budget state across failures

reasoning_steps.argument: Campus-local inference avoids partner/provider model egress but still requires control of local tools, logs, users, and backups; it may not fit or complete every workload. Approved API-only service requires external permission for every submitted data class and has no permitted service for classes lacking such permission. A campus gateway plus separately approved external access can retain local service for eligible sensitive work while isolating optional external workflows, at the cost of workflow separation and separate governance. Federation adds partner identity, destination-specific data agreements, remote retention/audit obligations, WAN failures, and revocation semantics; it does not automatically make otherwise prohibited external processing permissible. Thus federation has no sovereignty advantage merely because its destination is another university. Whether its capacity or task-quality gains justify these extra boundaries remains an empirical and governance question, not a conclusion of the lemma.
reasoning_steps.title: 8. Compare the four baselines within this strategy's scope

reasoning_steps.argument: Build a synthetic, non-sensitive two-authority harness before any live cross-campus transfer. Replay paired executions A and B with identical requests and random seeds while suppressing all home-to-partner policy communication. Include an unexpired cached approval, revocation before a new request, and a later reconnection. A cached-approval design that admits both traces demonstrates the predicted safety failure; denying both preserves safety with a measured availability cost. Separately inject ambiguous classification, an agent's unapproved tool URL, a tenant's attempted direct egress, provider rejection, charged timeout, cancellation, simultaneous quota reservations, and stale-policy replay. Inspect packet destinations and protected decision records independently; decision logs alone cannot establish absence of bypass. Require zero observed unauthorized disclosures, replay admissions, and reservation overshoots before considering a reviewed live pilot. A finite pass is only bounded support, not proof of security or a deployment authorization.

Model replacement through shorter lives or a separately labeled future cash-flow schedule, not double-counted depreciation and purchase outlay. Procurement labor and operations must not overlap. For a stable annual scenario, monthly equivalent is C_L/12; actual monthly cash flow can differ. reasoning_steps.title: 5. Local/API break-even requires success adjustment and a feasible operating range

reasoning_steps.argument: Let C_F=C_G+ΔC and S_F=S_G+ΔS, with C_G>0, S_G>0, ΔC>0 and S_F>0. Cross-multiplying positive denominators gives C_F/S_F<C_G/S_G iff (C_G+ΔC)S_G<C_G(S_G+ΔS), iff ΔC·S_G<C_G·ΔS, iff ΔS/S_G>ΔC/C_G. This is both necessary and sufficient for this economic metric. A nonpositive ΔS cannot pass when added cost is positive. Since S_F≤D, a strict improvement is impossible if D−S_G≤S_G·ΔC/C_G. That bound can reject an expensive federation before benchmarking it: even perfect completion would not repay its overhead on this metric. If S_G=0, use absolute completion and feasibility instead of this ratio test. If ΔC≤0, use the original cross-product inequality rather than the positive-overhead interpretation. Economic superiority is not sufficient for deployment: policy, latency, coverage, per-campus autonomy and administrative constraints remain independent gates.
reasoning_steps.title: 6. Federation threshold and edge cases

reasoning_steps.argument: Consider an explicitly hypothetical monthly cohort of D=2,000 tasks and A=100 active researchers. Assign gateway cost C_G=$6,000 and S_G=1,200 useful completions. Assign federation net overhead ΔC=$1,500. These are illustrative aggregate accounting inputs, not campus spending, hardware quotes or current API prices. The gateway costs $5 per useful task and $60 per active researcher-month. Federation must add more than 1,200×1,500/6,000=300 useful completions to lower unit cost. If it adds 200, its cost is $7,500/1,400=$75/14≈$5.36 per useful task: useful throughput rises but unit cost worsens. If it adds 400, the ratio is $7,500/1,600=$4.6875. At 300 it ties at $5. Federation costs $75 per active researcher-month in either case. If these monthly costs repeat for twelve months, annual costs are $72,000 versus $90,000; for the same 100 distinct researchers throughout the year, annual per-researcher costs are $720 versus $900. These arithmetic examples do not establish achievable completion gains.
reasoning_steps.title: 7. Hand-worked synthetic counterexample to throughput-only reasoning

reasoning_steps.argument: Treat monthly frontier caps B=$0/$2,000/$4,000/$8,000 as scenarios. Their twelve-month ceilings are $0/$24,000/$48,000/$96,000, not predicted expenditure. With 100 active researchers their monthly ceilings are $0/$20/$40/$80 per researcher, not entitlements. Let X be settled charges and R outstanding reserved liability. Dispatch only after an atomic reservation r keeps X+R+r≤B and also fits user, project and department limits. If every call's eventual charge c satisfies 0≤c≤r, settlement changes X+R by c−r≤0; dispatch and settlement therefore preserve the cap by induction. This guarantee requires an enforceable bound covering output, tools, descendant calls, price changes and charge ambiguity, plus all paid traffic passing through the ledger. An uncertain timeout retains its reservation until reconciled; cancellation alone is not evidence of zero charge. Retries require new reservations or unused explicit workflow reservations, never paid escalation after exhaustion. Carry unresolved liabilities across billing-period accounting rather than releasing them at a calendar reset. With no enforceable maximum charge, the proof does not apply and strict-cap paid dispatch must remain disabled. With B=0, no positive-cost API call is allowed; existing local hardware still has energy, staffing and capacity costs.
reasoning_steps.title: 8. Budget scenarios and the reservation invariant

reasoning_steps.argument: Propose a campus-controlled identity and classification gate, versioned destination policy, admission/quota ledger, local queue and worker adapters, with a separately approved external connector rather than automatic fallback. Filter destinations by data and derived-artifact policy, current campus authority, contracts, retention, model fit and available reservations before optimizing expected cost per useful result subject to latency targets. Unknown classification or stale authorization closes external admission. Keep request attribution, policy version, model/version and resource/cost events in approved audit domains, minimizing sensitive payload logging. The supplied WDRR claim is not evidence of cross-campus fairness, deadline guarantees or dollar reservations. A proposed federation adds mutually authenticated campus gateways, explicit bilateral permissions and ownership of every reservation and audit event; it must not imply transitive trust. WAN partition, provider rejection, outage or overload can produce a queued request or explicit failure, but cannot widen authorized destinations. Per-campus fairness and starvation must be measured independently of aggregate task counts. Cross-campus sharing is useful only for work whose data, outputs, logs, embeddings and cache are all authorized for the receiving domain.
reasoning_steps.title: 9. Minimal policy-first comparison architecture

reasoning_steps.argument: Days 1–30: retrieve and date the two starting sources; obtain dated provider quotes/contracts; inventory campus assets, power, staff effort and billing rules; freeze task strata, quality rubrics, latency deadlines and acceptable coverage. Days 31–60: run paired authorized tasks on L, A and G, initially using public or synthetic data, with a proposed starter sample of 20 roots per task stratum per feasible baseline. Randomize ordering, record workload and model versions, and expand only within explicit cost reservations. Calls within one root are not independent observations. Days 61–90: test F only after campus security/legal agreement; compare with G using the same roots and include coordination labor. Inject stale policy, malicious-tenant quota contention, WAN partition, campus/provider outage, rejection, charged timeout, cancellation and exhausted-budget cases. Proposed immediate stop conditions are any unauthorized disclosure or committed spending beyond the applicable cap. Proposed economic go condition is that conservative paired-task uncertainty bounds support ΔS/S_G>ΔC/C_G on the chosen cost basis, with no failed mandatory task stratum. Proposed service gates are at least 95% deadline compliance and at least 90% rubric acceptance in each mandatory eligible stratum; campuses must approve these illustrative targets before testing. Record provenance completeness, queue tails, starvation, availability and administrative hours separately. Use project/day clustering when estimating uncertainty and report inconclusive intervals as inconclusive. Without approval, sufficient budget or adequate precision, continue G rather than calling federation validated. This is a test plan, not a completed experiment.

assumptions: Every billable action, including client/provider retries and agent/tool subcalls, is mediated by the reservation mechanism; there are no alternate credentials or untracked spending paths.

Each admitted billable action has a finite enforceable upper charge bound in the ledger currency, including applicable token limits, ancillary charges, exchange-rate exposure and taxes; final liability does not exceed that bound.
Reservations and settlement are durable, atomic across every applicable budget scope, and serialized under concurrent admissions; recovery does not duplicate releases or erase unresolved obligations.
Initial settled charges plus reservations do not exceed the caps; budget changes and accounting-window transitions preserve all outstanding liabilities.
A reservation is released only on authoritative final reconciliation or evidence that no liability remains, not on a timeout or cancellation request alone.
output.claim: Under the accounting and enforcement assumptions listed below, a campus-controlled, atomic reservation ledger preserves user, project, department and campus spending caps even when calls time out or are cancelled. Unresolved calls must retain their reservations; releasing a reservation merely because a timeout or cancellation occurred is unsafe. This safety property does not establish task quality, availability or starvation freedom, and does not require federation.

reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied project description attributes protocol translation across OpenAI/Ollama/Anthropic clients and Ollama/vLLM backends, WDRR scheduling, per-user quotas, audit logging and GPU telemetry to MindRouter's published campus gateway. These are starting descriptions, not independently measured capabilities in this session. Cross-campus federation, frontier routing, hierarchical financial reservations and the enforcement protocol below are proposed extensions, not asserted MindRouter features. The logical result concerns an abstract ledger, not a verified implementation.
reasoning_steps.title: 1. Scope and published-claim boundary

reasoning_steps.argument: For each proposed call, construct an eligible destination set from the home campus's authoritative identity, data classification, approved processing domains, retention terms, contract, audit requirements, model/context requirements and available quota. The classification covers prompts, attachments, outputs, embeddings, caches and logs, not just the original file. Ambiguity yields an empty set. Restricted categories remain inside their approved domains unless the campus explicitly authorizes otherwise. Rank only eligible destinations by quality estimate, deadline feasibility and incremental cost; if none qualify, queue locally where permitted, reject, or request explicit approval. Failure is not an authorization event. Re-evaluate every agent/tool call and every destination change. Actual enforcement requires mediation of network egress, tools, logging and storage; a router recommendation alone cannot enforce this rule.
reasoning_steps.title: 2. Policy eligibility precedes ranking

reasoning_steps.argument: Let s range over all applicable user, project, department and campus budget scopes. Within an accounting window, B_s is its cap, L_s its settled cumulative charges, and H_s the sum of reservations for unresolved billable actions. Initially require L_s + H_s <= B_s. Before a call is dispatched, choose an enforceable upper bound r on its total possible charge and atomically add r to every applicable H_s only if all caps remain satisfied. The same charge is attributed to each scope; this is hierarchical control, not multiple billing. Bind the reservation to one call identity, destination, authorized scope and request limits. GPU service quotas and concurrency reservations are separate resources and need their own admission controls.
reasoning_steps.title: 3. Define the reservation invariant

reasoning_steps.argument: Induct on ledger events. Admission preserves the inequality by its atomic guard. On final reconciliation of a reserved call, replace reservation r with actual liability z, where 0 <= z <= r: the scope total changes from L_s + H_s to L_s + H_s - r + z and cannot increase. A proven unbilled rejection has z=0. A timeout, cancellation request, lost acknowledgement or WAN failure without final billing evidence leaves the reservation unchanged. Thus each event preserves all caps. Base cases include zero budget and no calls: no positive-charge reservation can pass, though already funded local resources may remain usable. Budget reduction is allowed only above current obligations, or after explicit additional funding. Open obligations cannot disappear at month-end; they must be carried into an explicitly funded liability account or retained against their original allocation. This proves allocation safety, not invoice-month cash-flow safety unless billing timing is also bounded.
reasoning_steps.title: 4. Preservation proof and ambiguous outcomes

reasoning_steps.argument: Hypothetical ledger example, not an API price: with a $100 cap, reserve $70, dispatch, then receive an ambiguous timeout. Releasing that reservation permits a second $70 call. If both are charged $70, liability is $140, exceeding the cap by $40. A cancellation acknowledgement that does not settle billing has the same problem. Conversely, keeping the first reservation blocks the second $70 reservation. If no finite enforceable charge bound exists for a paid action, no nonzero admission rule can guarantee a finite cap against every allowed billing outcome: an outcome larger than the remaining budget remains possible. A hard-cap deployment must therefore obtain contractual/enforced bounds or refuse that action. Disable hidden client retries and automatic paid retry escalation. An explicit retry requires authorization and a separate reservation unless an audited provider contract guarantees the two attempts share one bounded billable identity.
reasoning_steps.title: 5. Concrete counterexample and necessity of a charge bound

reasoning_steps.argument: A valid reservation is not permission to export data. At actual egress, validate a campus-issued authorization against the current local policy epoch and an unexpired, destination-specific capability. Unknown freshness during a partition fails closed for new remote work. Reservation and dispatch need a crash-safe state machine: record dispatch intent before sending, deduplicate it, and retain the reservation after uncertain sends. The local egress gate defines the authorization instant; revocation after data has already left cannot recall it. Remote retention and deletion require contractual and technical evidence. A federation must preserve these home-campus decisions and enforce remote logging/cache/output restrictions; a remote scheduler must not reinterpret home-campus permission. This is a proposed boundary design, not a proof that a distributed implementation meets it.
reasoning_steps.title: 6. Policy freshness is a different safety obligation

reasoning_steps.argument: Consider one GPU pool and a batch job that occupies the entire pool non-preemptively for two hours. An interactive request arriving just afterward cannot meet a one-minute deadline regardless of its WDRR weight. A model that cannot fit any eligible GPU has no service opportunity at all. Strict interactive priority can instead starve batches under continuous interactive arrivals. These counterexamples block inference from fair-share scheduling to latency or starvation guarantees. Proposed controls are model/memory-fit eligibility including context/KV-cache and concurrency headroom, separate interactive reservations and batch windows, bounded work quanta where technically possible, aging, and explicit admission deadlines. Compare service in GPU-seconds within compatible resource pools, with recorded estimation error; raw token counts across different models and GPUs are not interchangeable. Any waiting-time guarantee additionally requires bounded blocking, positive allocated capacity and a feasible admitted workload; none is established here.
reasoning_steps.title: 7. Fair-share scheduling alone cannot guarantee access

reasoning_steps.argument: Campus-local only minimizes external trust boundaries but cannot promise frontier quality, model fit or uptime during local maintenance. Approved API only avoids campus GPU operations but remains subject to data eligibility, provider outages/rejections, hard paid caps and model-version availability. A campus gateway plus separately approved external access retains local identity, audit and quota control while allowing explicitly authorized external tasks; a separate portal/account workflow may suffice, with no automatic cross-route fallback. Proposed federation adds remote-campus identity mapping, resource heterogeneity, WAN dependencies, incident coordination, retention enforcement and agreements; it is useful only where additional approved capacity actually matches the task. Start with a campus policy/identity authority, egress enforcement, durable reservation ledger, scheduler/backend adapters, redacted audit store and telemetry. Maintain separate paid-access approval until integration demonstrates a benefit. Federation should not be required merely to obtain a frontier model that no participating campus hosts.
reasoning_steps.title: 8. Four baselines and minimal deployment

reasoning_steps.argument: For baseline b report annual fully loaded cost C_b = annualized capital + operations + paid services + integration/agreement overhead. Local operations include staff, support, power, cooling, storage and network; disclose depreciation horizon, replacement treatment and idle capacity without double-counting the same replacement in both depreciation and an added reserve. Report sunk, incremental and fully loaded costs separately. API cost sums actual dated input/output/cached-token charges, repeated Investigator/Skeptic or agent calls, tools, embeddings, billable failures/retries, egress and commitments under the applicable contract. Prices are unavailable here and must not be filled with invented rates. Monthly caps of $2,000/$4,000/$8,000 correspond to annual allocation ceilings of $24,000/$48,000/$96,000, not predicted spending. Divide realized total cost by explicitly defined active researchers and by parent tasks meeting both the preregistered quality and latency target; do not count agent subcalls as successful research tasks. Report zero successful tasks as an undefined cost-per-success, alongside the incurred cost. Spending caps do not cap staff burden or guarantee useful completions.
reasoning_steps.title: 9. Budget and useful-task accounting for the comparison

reasoning_steps.argument: Days 1–15: computing verifies source claims and records actual access dates, inventories GPU/model fit and maintenance, and instruments queue, service, cold-start, cost and administrative time; security and procurement approve data/destination scopes and billing bounds. Faculty and students preregister task rubrics, provenance requirements and latency targets for classroom coding, routine analysis, demanding reasoning, multimodal/long-context, agentic workflows, sensitive-data tasks and reproducible batches. Days 16–30: use synthetic/public data for fault injection and replay. Days 31–60: compare local, API and gateway-plus-separate-access using blocked assignments of the same eligible parent tasks. Days 61–90: add a federation arm only after independent campus approvals; otherwise retain it as an unevaluated proposal. Target at least 30 distinct parent tasks per stratum where funding and eligibility allow, with paired executions and two repeats for reproducibility; do not force restricted tasks through ineligible arms. Record exclusions, unfinished work and budget exhaustion. Repeats and agent calls are clustered under the parent task, not treated as independent samples. Freeze or record weights/version, quantization, prompts, tools, seeds where supported and retrieval snapshots; provider version labels alone do not establish reproducibility.
reasoning_steps.title: 10. Bounded 90-day discriminating pilot

reasoning_steps.argument: Computing owns end-to-end completion, p50/p95 queue and total latency, throughput, cold starts, utilization, maintenance availability and admitted-task starvation. Security owns destination/retention conformance; finance owns settled charges, held liabilities and invoice reconciliation; faculty own blinded task-quality adjudication; service management records administrative hours and incident handling. Report useful-and-on-time completions both per authorized request and per admitted request, so rejection cannot inflate reliability. Proposed gates, to approve before observation: zero observed unauthorized transmissions or cap violations; every ambiguous charge remains held until reconciliation; at least 80% useful-and-on-time completion in each claimed-supported stratum; service availability at least 99% during declared service hours, with maintenance also reported against the full requested window. Set class-specific deadlines in advance rather than hiding them in pooled latency. Investigate any continuously eligible, funded, backlogged tenant receiving under 80% of its declared resource-pool share over a sufficiently long window despite available compatible capacity; this is a diagnostic threshold, not a WDRR theorem. Stop remote routing immediately on a policy or accounting violation. Federation receives a provisional go only if it adds at least 10 percentage points of useful-and-on-time completion on a preregistered underserved stratum, with a paired uncertainty interval excluding zero, while meeting the safety gates and a campus-approved administrative cost ceiling. Otherwise prefer the simpler gateway-plus-separate-access baseline. These numerical thresholds are proposed decisions, not observed results or universal standards.
reasoning_steps.title: 11. Measurements, failure tests and proposed stop/go gates

reasoning_steps.argument: The fault matrix must include stale/revoked policy, malicious tenant identity or classification changes, concurrent quota races, WAN partition, home/remote/provider outage, provider rejection with and without billing, charged timeout, cancellation before and after dispatch, duplicate send, month rollover, and attempts to fall back to a prohibited destination. For each case check egress, durable reservation state, attribution, audit redaction and recovery—not just response status. Also test peak demand, unavailable models, long non-preemptive jobs and maintenance drain. A test suite with zero observed violations establishes only bounded empirical support; it does not prove the implementation safe or the true failure probability zero. Federation benefit may disappear when sensitive tasks, incompatible GPUs, WAN delay and administrative work are included. That possibility is the experiment's intended negative outcome, not a failure of the study.

reasoning_steps.argument: Use 100 distinct active researchers and 2,000 root tasks each month: coding 600, routine analysis 400, demanding scientific reasoning 300, multimodal/long-context 200, agentic workflows 200, campus-only sensitive analysis 200, reproducible batches 100. These are disjoint accounting bins, not a claim that sensitivity is a distinct technical task type. Proposed deadlines respectively are 30 s, 120 s, 600 s, 180 s, 900 s end-to-end, 120 s and 24 h. A useful completion must be authorized, meet its deadline, pass the frozen task rubric and contain no critical factual/security error. Rubrics use held-out coding tests, known-result/unit checks, blinded scientific review, labeled multimodal fixtures and agent root-goal/tool-boundary checks. Batch acceptance requires complete provenance and a specified numerical tolerance; it does not assume bitwise API replay. Calls, Investigator/Skeptic exchanges and retries remain descendants of one root. Correct refusal is recorded separately, not counted as delivered research. These deadlines and rubrics require campus approval.

reasoning_steps.argument: For this scenario only, the campus approves all 2,000 roots locally, approves 1,800 non-sensitive roots at one named API destination, and approves only coding, routine analysis and batches at a named partner campus: 1,100 partner-eligible roots. The 200 sensitive roots remain campus-only. Thus policy-eligible counts are L=2,000, A=1,800, G=2,000 and F=2,000; federation does not increase eligibility by default. Separately, assume local model/context/memory requirements admit only coding, routine, sensitive analysis and batch work: 1,300 technically suitable roots. The other 700 require capabilities unavailable in this hypothetical local installation. Assume the approved API can technically serve all 1,800 eligible roots. These are proposed domain and capability assumptions, not university policy or model benchmark findings. Restricted, student, patient, controlled, sponsor-restricted and unpublished content, including derived prompts, outputs, logs, embeddings and cache, stays inside its approved domains; ambiguous classification gets no execution destination until resolved.
reasoning_steps.title: 3. Keep policy eligibility separate from capability

Let F keep G's local/API dispatches and incur the itemized $1,500 monthly coordination overhead. Then S_F=S_G and V_F=V_G, whereas C_F=C_G+1500.
